## MFCC k-NN baseline
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/03-audio-classification/code/main.py

```python
sr = 8000                                   # demo rate in the code
mag = stft_mag(signal, frame_len, hop)      # Hann, then DFT per frame
fb = mel_filterbank(n_mels, frame_len, sr)  # n_mels x (n_fft // 2 + 1)
mels = apply_filterbank(mag, fb)            # weighted sum per mel bin
lm = log_transform(mels)                    # log(max(v, eps))
feats = [dct_ii(f, n_mfcc) for f in lm]     # 13 coefficients per frame
emb = summarize(feats)                      # mean + var, 26 dims
pred = knn(emb, X_train, y_train, k=3)      # cosine top k, majority vote
```

## Score a model
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md
span: 2

```python
from jiwer import wer, Compose, ToLowerCase, RemovePunctuation, Strip
transform = Compose([ToLowerCase(), RemovePunctuation(), Strip()])
score = wer(truth="Please turn on the lights.", hypothesis="please turn on the light",
            truth_transform=transform, hypothesis_transform=transform)
sv = EncoderClassifier.from_hparams("speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb")
secs = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(emb_ref, emb_clone, dim=-1).item()  # SECS
fad = FrechetAudioDistance()
score = fad.get_fad_score("generated_folder/", "reference_folder/")  # lower is better
```

## Libraries
type: command-table
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/03-audio-classification/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `soundfile` | Reads WAV, FLAC, OGG as float32 |
| `torchaudio.transforms.Resample` | Resamples with anti-aliasing built in |
| `numpy.fft.rfft` | Real FFT for real audio |
| `torch.stft` | Vectorized STFT |
| `librosa.power_to_db` | Reference-normalized dB |
| `ffprobe` | Reports sr, channels and codec of a file |
| `jiwer` | WER and CER with normalization |
| `ASTForAudioClassification.from_pretrained` | Loads AST to fine-tune |

## Pick a classifier
type: concepts
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/03-audio-classification/docs/en.md

- **Under 1000 clips**: k-NN on MFCC means plus audio augmentation.
- **1K to 100K clips**: BEATs or AST fine-tune.
- **Over 100K clips**: train from scratch or fine-tune Whisper-encoder.
- **Real-time, edge**: 40-MFCC CNN, quantized to int8.
- **Multi-label**: BEATs-iter3 with BCE loss, mixup and SpecAugment.
- **Exclusive classes**: report top-1 and top-5 accuracy.
- **Imbalanced classes**: report per-class recall and macro F1.

## Metrics
type: glossary
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

- **WER**: Word Error Rate. (S + D + I) / N after normalization.
- **CER**: Character Error Rate. For tone languages.
- **RTFx**: audio seconds per wall-clock second. Higher is better.
- **MOS**: Mean Opinion Score. 1 to 5, 20+ listeners, 100+ samples.
- **UTMOS**: learned MOS predictor. Correlates ~0.9 with human MOS.
- **SECS**: ECAPA cosine of reference and clone. Above 0.75 is recognizable.
- **EER**: threshold where FAR equals FRR. ECAPA on VoxCeleb1-O: 0.87%.
- **DER**: (FA + Miss + Confusion) / total speaker time.
- **FAD**: Fréchet distance on VGGish embeddings. Lower is better.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Garbage that looks like a model bug | 44.1 kHz stereo into Whisper | Resample to 16 kHz mono float32 |
| FFT peak at a false frequency | Energy above Nyquist aliased | Low-pass filter before downsampling |
| Silent failure after deploy | 80 mels in training, 128 at inference | Log the feature shape at both ends |
| Mels look different | Featurized at 22.05 kHz | Fix SR before featurization |
| Whisper input looks wrong | dB-mel, not log-mel | Feed log-mel. Custom code does not autodetect |
| WER doubles in production | Per-utterance norm in training, global at inference | Use the same normalization |
| Flat trailing frames | Zero-padding at the clip end | Pad symmetrically or replicate |
| 5% WER hides 30% on accents | Aggregate WER | Report by demographic slice |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

- **Why mel, not Hz?** Humans hear pitch on a log scale.
- **Why a window?** It removes spectral leakage at the frame edges.
- **Why log-magnitude?** Raw magnitudes span 5-6 orders of magnitude.
- **Bigger FFT?** Better frequency resolution. Worse time resolution.
- **Why FFT, not DFT?** The DFT is O(N²). The FFT is O(N log N).
- **Why minDCF?** It weights cost at a chosen operating point.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/03-audio-classification/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

- Match sample rate before you match anything else.
- If you are not working on music, start with 80 log-mels.
- Start with a frozen backbone, not a fresh model.
- Use balanced sampling in training, not in evaluation.
- Normalize text before you score WER. Report the rule.
- Report P50/P95/P99 for latency.
- Keep an in-house held-out set. Public benchmarks saturate.

title: Music Generation and Audio-Language Models
subtitle: Codec tokens, MusicGen, audio encoders and projectors, Thinker and Talker, TTFAB budgets and audio pitfalls.
markdown:
## Audio becomes codec tokens
type: architecture
from: phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md

```arch
node | wave | 1,1 | Waveform | 16-48 kHz | client
node | enc | 2,1 | Encoder conv | per-timestep vector | process
node | rvq | 3,1 | RVQ | 8 codebooks at 75 Hz | store
node | gen | 3,2 | Generator | token-AR or diffusion | model
node | dec | 2,2 | Codec decoder | tokens to audio | process
node | out | 1,2 | Audio out | |
edge | wave | enc |
edge | enc | rvq | vectors
edge | rvq | gen | indices
edge | gen | dec | new tokens
edge | dec | out |
```

## Numbers that matter
type: concepts
from: phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/09-music-generation/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/docs/en.md

- **Codec rate**: 8 RVQ codebooks at 75 Hz give 600 tokens/sec.
- **Stream floor**: at 75 tokens/second, generate ≥75 tokens/sec per user.
- **Talker floor**: 50 Hz speech tokens need ≥50 tok/s from the Talker.
- **Codebook**: 1024 or 2048 entries is typical.
- **MusicGen codec**: EnCodec at 32 kHz with 4 codebooks.
- **Log-Mel shape**: 30 s at 100 Hz frame rate gives (3000, 80).
- **Round trip**: below 500ms, the user stops noticing the lag.

## Two generator families
type: concepts
from: phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/09-music-generation/docs/en.md

- **Token-autoregressive**: a decoder-only transformer over flattened RVQ tokens.
- **Delayed parallel**: MusicGen emits K codebook streams with per-stream offsets.
- **VALL-E**: speech tokens from a text prompt and a 3-second voice sample.
- **Latent diffusion**: Stable Audio Open works on compressed audio. Good for loops.
- **Flow matching**: Stable Audio 2.5 uses it on continuous audio latents.
- **Trend**: flow matching wins for music. Token-AR dominates speech.

## MusicGen, melody and FAD
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/09-music-generation/docs/en.md

```python
from audiocraft.models import MusicGen
model = MusicGen.get_pretrained("facebook/musicgen-small")  # 300M, fast
model.set_generation_params(duration=10)  # seconds of audio
wav = model.generate(["upbeat synthwave with driving drums, 128 BPM"])
torchaudio.save("out.wav", wav[0].cpu(), 32000)  # 32 kHz output
melody, sr = torchaudio.load("humming.wav")
wav = model.generate_with_chroma(  # keeps the tune, swaps timbre
    ["jazz piano cover"], melody.squeeze(), sr)
from frechet_audio_distance import FrechetAudioDistance
fad = FrechetAudioDistance()  # VGGish embedding distance
fad.get_fad_score("generated_folder/", "reference_folder/")  # lower is better
```

## Audio-language model template
type: flow
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/docs/en.md

1. **Audio encoder**: Whisper encoder, BEATs, CLAP or WavLM makes features.
2. **Projector**: a linear layer or MLP maps features into the LLM embedding space.
3. **LLM**: a decoder reads interleaved text and audio tokens and writes text.
4. **Stage 1**: freeze encoder and LLM. Train the projector on ASR or captioning data.
5. **Stage 2**: full or LoRA fine-tune on instruction audio tasks.
6. **Stage 3**: optional. Add a speech decoder for voice-in and voice-out.

## Projector and audio Q-former
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/code/main.py

```python
class AudioProjector(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, audio_dim=1280, llm_dim=4096):
        super().__init__()
        self.down = nn.Linear(audio_dim, llm_dim)  # audio to LLM width
        self.act = nn.GELU()
        self.up = nn.Linear(llm_dim, llm_dim)
    def forward(self, audio_features):
        return self.up(self.act(self.down(audio_features)))
qf = QFormer(n_queries=8, hidden=20)  # N=8 queries
tokens = qf.forward(frames)  # 99 frames in, 8 tokens out
```

## Log-Mel and encoder settings
type: defaults
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sample rate | 16 kHz | Resample first |
| Window | 25ms | `win_ms: int = 25` |
| Hop | 10ms | `hop_ms: int = 10` |
| Mel filters | 80 | 0-8000 Hz |
| Log compress | `math.log(1 + x)` | Dynamic range |
| Q-former queries | 32 or 64 | AF3 uses 64 |
| Whisper encoder | 12-layer | Frozen in the ALM pattern |

## Thinker and Talker
type: architecture
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/docs/en.md

```arch
node | mic | 1,1 | Mic and VAD | speech tokens | client
node | think | 2,1 | Thinker | 7B-80B, TMRoPE | model
node | talk | 3,1 | Talker | 200M-1B | model
node | dec | 3,2 | Speech decoder | SNAC, MoVQGAN | process
node | spk | 2,2 | Speakers | audio samples | client
edge | mic | think | audio tokens
edge | think | talk | text tokens
edge | talk | dec | RVQ indices
edge | dec | spk | stream
```

## TTFAB budget at 7B
type: defaults
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Mic to audio tokens | 40-80ms | Streams |
| Prefill | 100-200ms | Much more at 70B |
| First Thinker text token | 40ms | Grows with Thinker size |
| Talker on first text token | 20ms | At least 15ms in the lesson model |
| First speech tokens commit | 40ms | Before residual-VQ decode |
| Residual-VQ decode | 30ms | `rvq_decode = 30` |
| Speech waveform decode | 50-80ms | `wave_decode = 70` |
| Total TTFAB | 320-490ms | 600-900ms at 70B |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/09-music-generation/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Music loops past 30 s | AR models loop | Crossfade, or use ACE-Step |
| Tempo leaves the BPM | Models wander | BPM tags, librosa `beat_track` |
| Mushy sung words | Open models are weak on lyrics | Commercial API or fine-tune |
| Hallucinations on silence | Whisper encoder issue | VAD-gate |
| Speakers mixed past 10 minutes | Long-audio degradation | Diarize first, then summarize |
| Multi-audio near 25% | Random-chance level | Do not trust "which clip" tasks |
| Errors from RVQ layer 1 spread | RVQ error accumulation | Temperature 0 on higher layers |
| Artifacts at clip joins | Crossfade boundaries | Careful overlap-add |

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/code/main.py, phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/code/main.py, phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Load the ALM processor | `AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Omni-7B")` |
| Generate an answer | `model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=200)` |
| Load MMAU-Pro | `load_dataset("gamma-lab-umd/MMAU-Pro", split="test")` |
| Score MMAU-Pro officially | `evaluate_mmau_pro_comprehensive.py` |
| Cut audio into frames | `window_frames(wave, 16000, 25, 10)` |
| List TTFAB parts | `ttfab(cfg)` |
| Sample codec tokens | `generate(counts, style, start, length, rng, temperature=1.0)` |

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/19-audio-language-whisper-to-af3/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/20-omni-models-thinker-talker/docs/en.md

- **When is a cascade enough?** Transcription is the goal, with no music and no emotion.
- **When do I need end-to-end?** Music, emotion, multi-speaker or complex audio reasoning.
- **What does a cascade lose?** Mood, speaker identity, timing and deepfake cues.
- **Why a small Talker?** A 7B Talker falls behind the 50 tok/s floor.
- **Why TMRoPE?** It gives each token an absolute timestamp. Vision, audio and text align.
- **Half or full duplex?** Qwen2.5-Omni is half-duplex by default. Moshi supports full-duplex.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/09-music-generation/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/10-audio-language-models/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/11-audio-generation/docs/en.md

- To ship safely, generate instrumental only.
- Tag each generation with watermarks and metadata.
- Report each MMAU-Pro `category` separately.
- Check the codec first. It caps output quality. DAC is the current open best.
- For voice cloning, add abuse detection and opt-out lists.

title: Autonomous Agents and Permissions
subtitle: Run an agent unattended with limits. Permission modes, budgets, kill switches, durable execution, approvals, rollback.
markdown:
## Operator tasks
type: task-table
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/10-claude-code-permission-modes/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Review a plan first | permission mode `plan` |
| Auto-approve file edits only | permission mode `acceptEdits` |
| Cap spend and loop turns | `max_budget_usd`, `max_turns` |
| Limit the tool set | `allowed_tools` / `disallowed_tools` |
| Kill the agent container | `kubectl delete pod` |
| Trip on repeated calls | `CircuitBreaker(threshold=5)` |
| Replay after a crash | `workflow(EventLog(<path>), <query>)` |
| Make an approval retry-safe | `k = p.key()` |

## Control layers
type: architecture
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/10-claude-code-permission-modes/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/docs/en.md

```arch
node | loop | 1,1 | Agent loop | turns, tool calls
node | perm | 2,1 | Permission mode | plan to bypassPermissions
node | gov | 3,1 | Cost governor | stack of caps
node | kill | 4,1 | Kill switch | agent cannot write it
node | breaker | 1,2 | Circuit breaker | closed, open, half-open
node | canary | 2,2 | Canary token | access is the alarm
node | prop | 3,2 | Proposal store | propose, commit, verify
node | log | 4,2 | Event log | keyed by thread_id
edge | loop | perm | action
edge | perm | gov | spend
edge | gov | kill | breach
edge | loop | breaker | calls
edge | loop | canary | reads
edge | perm | prop | approve
edge | prop | log | persist
```

## Propose, commit, verify
type: flow
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/code/main.py

1. **Propose**: Store intent, lineage, blast radius, rollback. Status `waiting`.
2. **Surface**: A person reviews the metadata, not the agent.
3. **Approve**: `checklist_approve` needs all three checks. Status `approved`.
4. **Precondition**: State still matches the approval. Else `aborted-precondition`.
5. **Commit**: Persist the intent first, then run the side effect.
6. **Verify**: Re-read the target. A failure runs the rollback.
7. **Retry**: A terminal status returns the stored result. No second run.

## Durable activity
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/code/main.py

```python
def activity(name: str):
    def deco(fn):
        @functools.wraps(fn)
        def wrapper(log: EventLog, *args):
            hit = log.lookup(name, args)  # done event in log?
            if hit:
                return hit["result"]  # replay, no re-run
            log.append({"name": name, "args": list(args), "status": "started"})
            result = fn(*args)  # the real side effect
            log.append({"name": name, "args": list(args),
                        "status": "done", "result": result})  # log output
            return result
        return wrapper
    return deco
```

## Governor and breaker
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/code/main.py

```python
gov = Governor(max_turns=200, max_budget_usd=50.0)  # session caps
if gov.enable_iter_cap and turn >= gov.max_turns:
    run.stopped_by = "max_turns"  # iteration cap
if gov.enable_session_cap and run.dollars >= gov.max_budget_usd:
    run.stopped_by = "max_budget_usd"  # dollar cap
if gov.enable_velocity and velocity_exceeded(run, gov, now_min):
    run.stopped_by = "velocity_limit"  # rolling spend rate
if kill_switch["enabled"]:
    break  # external off-button
allowed = breaker.record(f"{a.kind}:{a.payload}")
if not allowed:
    break  # 5 identical calls opened it
```

## Permission modes
type: concepts
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/10-claude-code-permission-modes/docs/en.md

- **`plan`**: User approves the plan. Each action is reviewed first.
- **`default`**: "Manual". Prompts for shell, destructive and network actions.
- **`acceptEdits`**: File writes auto-approve. Shell and network still prompt.
- **`auto`**: A classifier model reviews each action. Blocks escalation.
- **`dontAsk`**: Never prompts. Unapproved actions are denied.
- **`bypassPermissions`**: Approves everything. Throwaway containers only.

## Defaults in the simulators
type: defaults
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `max_tokens_per_request` | 10_000 | Per-call completion cap |
| `max_turns` | 200 | Loop iterations per session |
| `max_budget_usd` | 50.0 | Session dollars, aborts on breach |
| `velocity_usd_per_min` | 0.03 | Rolling spend rate cut-off |
| `velocity_window_min` | 10.0 | Window for the rate |
| `monthly_cap_usd` | 500.0 | Catches slow leaks late |
| `threshold` | 5 | Identical calls that open the breaker |
| Half-open probes | default 1 | 1 to 3 after the cool-down |

## Which cap catches what
type: concepts
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md

- **Runaway loop**: Caught by the velocity limit.
- **Slow leak**: About 2x expected work. Caught by the daily cap.
- **Bad release**: New version uses 5x tokens. Caught by weekly or monthly cap.
- **Legitimate surge**: Caught by the hour or day cap with a clear log.
- **Slow adversarial drift**: Beats statistical detectors. Hard limits catch it.
- **Composed safe actions**: No detector catches them.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Crash re-runs all tool calls | Naive `while True` loop | Activities plus an event log |
| Replay diverges | Wall clock or random in workflow | Register it as a side effect |
| Approved action runs twice | No idempotency key | One key per proposal |
| Overdraft after resume | Idempotency check only | Add a precondition check |
| "Committed" but no side effect | Status saved, action lost | Verify by re-read, then roll back |
| Approvals with no real review | Plain Approve button | Challenge-and-response checklist |
| Bill tripled after a new tool | No per-tool cap | Per-tool cap, daily-growth alert |
| Agent turns off its canary | Detector in the agent's reach | Keep it where agent cannot write |

## Glossary
type: glossary
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/01-long-horizon-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/docs/en.md

- **HITL**: Human-in-the-loop. A person approves before the action.
- **METR horizon**: Task length a model completes at 50% reliability.
- **Denial of Wallet**: Agent loop that spends with no cap to stop it.
- **thread_id**: Key that scopes durable state for one session.
- **Lease**: Short claim that a worker runs a run. It expires on crash.
- **Blast radius**: Scope of effect if the action goes wrong.
- **SAGA**: Compensating transaction that neutralizes the original action.

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/01-long-horizon-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/10-claude-code-permission-modes/docs/en.md

- **99% per step, 70 steps?** The agent still fails half the time.
- **Why a stack of caps?** One monthly cap fires after the wallet is gone.
- **Why persist every transition?** Replay lands anywhere and lease recovery is precise.
- **When skip durable execution?** Short runs with no human input, or read-only work.
- **What does `auto` miss?** Subtle injection and harmful sequences of safe actions.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/13-cost-governors/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/14-kill-switches-canaries/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/15-propose-then-commit/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/16-checkpoints-rollback/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/12-durable-execution/docs/en.md

- Never run `auto` without `max_budget_usd`.
- Check the kill switch on every consequential action.
- Re-enable a kill switch only by an explicit human action.
- Give every new tool its own cap and alert.
- Always HITL for irreversible writes. Never for reads.
- Rehearse each rollback end to end at least once.

title: Self-Improving and Research Agents
subtitle: Generator plus evaluator loops, self-editing agents, research loops, RSI gaps and the controls for each.
markdown:
## The generator plus evaluator loop
type: flow
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md

1. **Seed**: start from a seed program `P_0`. It is correct but suboptimal.
2. **Database**: keep variant programs. The evaluator scores each one.
3. **Sampler**: pick parents from a MAP-elites grid or from islands.
4. **LLM**: propose a targeted edit. The prompt holds top variants and the evaluator signature.
5. **Evaluator**: compile, run and score the variant on held-out inputs.
6. **Database**: insert the variant by its score and feature vector.
7. **Loop**: repeat for hours to weeks.

- **MAP-elites**: grid keyed by feature vectors. Each cell holds its best variant.
- **Island model**: independent populations that migrate periodically.
- **DGM**: Darwin Godel Machine. Archive plus empirical scores, no proof.
- **AAR**: Automated Alignment Researcher. A model run autonomously on alignment problems.
- **RSI**: recursive self-improvement. The system proposes edits to itself each cycle.
- **VLM critique**: a vision-language model reads figures and rewrites them.
- **Evaluator firewall**: the evaluator lives in a namespace the agent cannot edit.
- **Reward hacking**: the loop raises the score without the intended task.

- **Why does DGM drop the proof?** Nobody completed one for a non-trivial agent. DGM uses score deltas.

title: BERT, GPT and T5 Compared
subtitle: Encoder-only, decoder-only and encoder-decoder side by side. Objectives, masks, blocks, decoding and when to pick each.
markdown:
## Three families side by side
type: comparison
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/06-bert-masked-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

| Factor | BERT | GPT | T5 / BART |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stack | Encoder only | Decoder only | Encoder and decoder |
| Attention | Bidirectional, no mask | Causal triangle mask | Bidirectional encoder, causal decoder |
| Cross-attention | None | None | Q from decoder, K/V from encoder |
| Objective | MLM on 15% of tokens | Next token, shift by one | Span corruption or denoising |
| Predicts | $P(x_{\text{masked}} \mid x_{\text{unmasked}})$ | $P(x_t \mid x_{<t})$ | Target spans or the clean sequence |
| Generates text | No | Yes, token by token | Yes, from the encoder output |
| Best for | Classification, retrieval, NER | Chat, code, reasoning | Translation, speech to text |
| Examples | BERT, DeBERTa, ModernBERT | GPT, Llama, Qwen | T5, BART, Whisper |

## Block wiring
type: architecture
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

```arch
node | src | 1,1 | Source tokens | embed + position | client
node | enc | 2,1 | Encoder block | LN, self MHA, LN, FFN | process
node | encout | 3,1 | Encoder output | (N_src, d_model), runs once | store
node | tgt | 1,2 | Target tokens | shift by one | client
node | self | 2,2 | Masked self-attention | sublayer 1 | process
node | cross | 3,2 | Cross-attention | sublayer 2 | process
node | ffn | 4,2 | FFN | sublayer 3 | process
node | logits | 4,1 | Next-token logits | final LN + projection | model
edge | src | enc |
edge | enc | encout |
edge | tgt | self |
edge | self | cross |
edge | encout | cross | K, V
edge | cross | ffn |
edge | ffn | logits |
```

## One encoder-decoder forward pass
type: flow
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/code/main.py, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

1. **Embed**: tokens become vectors. Add RoPE or a sinusoidal position signal.
2. **Encoder**: each block runs pre-norm self-attention, then pre-norm FFN, each with a residual.
3. **Encoder output**: the encoder runs once per input. Cache it for long inputs.
4. **Decoder self-attention**: masked, so position `i` sees positions up to `i` only.
5. **Decoder cross-attention**: the only place encoder information enters the decoder.
6. **Decoder FFN**: then a final LN before the output projection.
7. **Check**: a 6-token source and a 5-token target give output shape `(5, vocab)`.

## Pretraining objectives
type: concepts
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/06-bert-masked-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

- **MLM**: select 15% of tokens. 80% become `[MASK]`, 10% random, 10% unchanged.
- **Labels**: the original token at selected positions. -100 at all other positions.
- **NSP**: predict if sentence B follows A. RoBERTa showed it hurt. Modern encoders skip it.
- **Causal LM**: input `[t1, t2, t3]`, targets `[t2, t3, t4]`. Sum $-\log P$ over positions.
- **Causal mask**: $M_{ij} = 0$ if $j \le i$, else $-\infty$. Add it before softmax.
- **Span corruption**: spans of mean length 3, 15% total, each replaced by `<extra_id_0>`, `<extra_id_1>`.
- **T5 target**: only the corrupted spans, each after its sentinel.
- **BART**: five noise functions. The decoder rebuilds the full original sequence.

## Decoding strategies
type: command-table
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/code/main.py, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `sample_greedy(probs)` | Argmax each step. Code completion, deterministic tasks |
| `sample_temperature(logits, t, rng)` | Divide logits by T. Higher T gives more diversity |
| `sample_top_k(logits, k, rng)` | Sample from the top k tokens only |
| `sample_top_p(logits, p, rng)` | Smallest set with cumulative prob at least p |
| `sample_min_p(logits, min_p, rng)` | Keep tokens with `p >= min_p * max_p` |
| Beam search | Width 4 to 5 for translation and summarization |
| Speculative decoding | Draft model proposes N tokens. Big model verifies |

## Use each family when
type: tips
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/06-bert-masked-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

- Use BERT for classification, embeddings, NER, NLI and RAG rerankers. It runs 5 to 10× faster per token than decoders.
- Do not use BERT for generation. The encoder cannot produce tokens autoregressively.
- Use GPT for generation, chat, code and reasoning. Decoder-only scales cleanest.
- Use min-p + temperature 0.7 as a default for open-weights models.
- Use T5 or BART when the input is a clear source sequence: translation, speech, structured tasks.
- Use beam search with an encoder-decoder. The output distribution is narrower than chat.
- Summarization and extraction work with either encoder-decoder or decoder-only.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/06-bert-masked-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Model fails without `[MASK]` at fine-tune | Trained on 100% `[MASK]` | Use the 80/10/10 rule |
| Model cheats by looking at the answer | No causal mask | Add the `-inf` triangle before softmax |
| Future weights not exactly zero | Softmax never outputs an exact zero | Put `-inf` into future scores |
| Gradients vanish in a deep stack | No residual connections | Use `x + sublayer(x)` |
| Activations explode after 12 layers | Post-norm | Switch to pre-norm |
| Corrupted span does not rebuild | Off-by-one in span bookkeeping | Run the round-trip check |
| Slow decode on long inputs | Encoder runs again each step | Cache the encoder output |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/06-bert-masked-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/08-t5-bart-encoder-decoder/docs/en.md

- **Why can BERT use the right context?** The encoder has no causal mask.
- **Why is GPT training parallel?** One pass gives N next-token losses. Inference stays serial.
- **How many params in one block?** MHA is `4 · d²`. SwiGLU FFN is about `3rd²`.
- **Why is T5 pretraining cheaper than BART?** T5 decodes only the spans. BART decodes the full sequence.
- **Are embedding models BERT?** Yes. Same encoder, contrastive loss.

title: Calculus, Gradients and Convex Optimization
subtitle: Derivatives, autodiff, GD, momentum, Adam, Newton and convexity tests. From-scratch Python and PyTorch.
markdown:
## Forward and backward through one neuron
type: architecture
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md

```arch
node | x | 1,1 | x | input
node | z1 | 2,1 | z1 = w*x | multiply
node | z2 | 3,1 | z2 = w*x + b | add bias
node | a | 4,1 | a = sigmoid(z2) | activation
node | dw | 1,2 | dL/dw | dL/dz2 * x
node | db | 2,2 | dL/db | dL/dz2 * 1
node | dz2 | 3,2 | dL/dz2 | dL/da * a(1-a)
node | loss | 4,2 | L | cross-entropy loss
edge | x | z1 | *w
edge | z1 | z2 | +b
edge | z2 | a |
edge | a | loss |
edge | loss | dz2 | backward
edge | dz2 | dw | x
edge | dz2 | db | 1
```

## Reverse-mode autodiff in Value.backward
type: flow
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/code/autodiff.py

1. **Record**: each operation makes a new `Value` with its children and a `_backward` closure.
2. **Sort**: `build_topo` puts every node after the nodes it depends on.
3. **Seed**: set `self.grad = 1.0` on the output. This is dy/dy = 1.
4. **Walk back**: call `v._backward()` for each node in reversed topological order.
5. **Accumulate**: each closure adds to `.grad` with `+=`. A value used twice gets the sum.
6. **Reset**: set `p.grad = 0.0` for every parameter before the next `loss.backward()`.
7. **Update**: `p.data -= lr * p.grad` for each parameter.

## Optimizers from scratch
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/code/optimizers.py

```python
GradientDescent(lr=0.001)  # w = w - lr * gradient
SGDMomentum(lr=0.001, momentum=0.9)  # v = beta * v + gradient
Adam(lr=0.001, beta1=0.9, beta2=0.999, epsilon=1e-8)  # two moments per weight
m_hat = [m / (1 - self.beta1 ** self.t) for m in self.m]  # bias correction
p - self.lr * mh / (vh ** 0.5 + self.epsilon)  # per-weight step size
adam_history = optimize(Adam(lr=0.01), rosenbrock, rosenbrock_gradient, start)
```

## Autograd and optimizers in PyTorch
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md

```python
x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)
y = x ** 2 + 3 * x + 1
y.backward()  # reverse mode through the recorded graph
print(x.grad)  # 7.0 = 2*x + 3
sgd = torch.optim.SGD(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, momentum=0.9)
adam = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
adamw = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=0.01)
scheduler = torch.optim.lr_scheduler.CosineAnnealingLR(adam, T_max=100)
```

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/18-convex-optimization/docs/en.md

- **Central difference**: $f'(x) \approx \frac{f(x + h) - f(x - h)}{2h}$.
- **Chain rule**: $\frac{dy}{dx} = f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)$. Sum the paths where the graph branches.
- **Gradient descent**: $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot \text{gradient}$.
- **Momentum**: $v = \beta \cdot v + \text{gradient}$, then $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot v$.
- **Adam**: $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot \hat{m} / (\sqrt{\hat{v}} + \epsilon)$ with bias-corrected moments.
- **Newton**: $x_{\text{new}} = x - H^{-1} \cdot \text{gradient}$.
- **Convex**: $f(tx + (1-t)y) \le t f(x) + (1-t) f(y)$ for $t \in [0, 1]$.
- **Lagrangian**: $L(x, \lambda) = f(x) + \lambda g(x)$. Set its gradient to zero.

## Derivatives to know
type: command-table
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| x^2 | 2x. MSE loss |
| wx + b | x for w, 1 for b, w for x. Linear layer |
| e^x | e^x. Softmax, attention |
| ln(x) | 1/x. Cross-entropy loss |
| sigmoid | f(x)(1-f(x)). Sigmoid activation |
| tanh | 1 - tanh^2. Classic activation |
| x^n | n x^(n-1). Used by `__pow__` |
| sin(x^2) | cos(x^2) * 2x. Chain rule example |

## Pick a method
type: command-table
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/18-convex-optimization/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| Gradient descent | First derivatives. O(n) memory. Baseline |
| SGD with momentum | Best final accuracy with more tuning |
| Adam | Diagonal curvature from gradient moments. Deep learning default |
| AdamW | Adam with decoupled weight decay. Transformers |
| Newton's method | Full Hessian. O(n^3) per step. Small convex problems |
| L-BFGS | Last m gradient differences. Medium convex problems |
| K-FAC | Kronecker-factored Fisher. Large-batch training |

## Numbers and defaults
type: defaults
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/code/derivatives.py, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/code/optimizers.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Adam `lr` | 0.001 | Start here for most problems |
| Adam `beta2` | 0.999 | `beta1` is 0.9. Moment decay rates |
| Adam `epsilon` | 1e-8 | Stops division by zero |
| SGD momentum `lr` | 0.01 | With momentum 0.9 |
| AdamW `weight_decay` | 0.01 | Decoupled from the gradient step |
| Mini-batch size | 32-256 | Good gradient estimate, moderate noise |
| Finite difference `h` | 1e-7 | In `numerical_derivative` |
| Gradient check difference | < 1e-5 | Autodiff against numerical |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/18-convex-optimization/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Loss grows or becomes nan | Learning rate too large | Reduce the learning rate |
| Training is too slow | Learning rate too small | Increase it. Add a schedule |
| Zigzag in a narrow valley | High condition number of the Hessian | Add momentum, or use Newton |
| Gradient near 0, no progress | Saddle point | Momentum and mini-batch noise |
| Gradients grow each step | `.grad` adds with `+=` | Set `p.grad = 0.0` before `backward` |
| Autodiff disagrees with numeric | Bug in a `_backward` rule | Run `gradient_check` |
| Noisy second derivative | Step h too small | Use `h=1e-4` for both calls |
| Newton too costly for a big model | O(n^2) memory, O(n^3) inverse | Use L-BFGS or Adam |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/18-convex-optimization/docs/en.md

- **Why reverse mode for networks?** Many inputs and one loss. One backward pass gives all gradients.
- **How do I test convexity?** f'' >= 0 in 1D. Hessian positive semidefinite in many dimensions.
- **Why does SGD work on non-convex losses?** Most critical points are saddle points. Most minima are good.
- **Why does L1 give sparse weights?** The diamond has corners on the axes.
- **What is complementary slackness?** $\lambda_i \, g_i(x) = 0$. Support vectors have $\lambda > 0$.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/18-convex-optimization/docs/en.md

- Use a learning rate schedule for runs longer than a few epochs.
- Cosine annealing and warmup suit transformers and large models.
- Newton's method solves a quadratic in one step.
- Gradient checks cost 2 forward passes per parameter. Do not run them in production training.
- A Hessian with mixed eigenvalue signs at a critical point marks a saddle.
- Flat minima generalize better than sharp minima.

title: Classical Machine Learning
subtitle: Fit, validate, tune and fix regression, classification and clustering models with scikit-learn.
markdown:
## Fit a model
type: task-table
col: 1
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/02-linear-regression/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/04-decision-trees/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/05-support-vector-machines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/06-knn-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| L2 regularized regression | `Ridge(alpha=1.0)` |
| Classifier for rare positives | `LogisticRegression(class_weight="balanced")` |
| Random forest | `RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42)` |
| Kernel SVM | `SVC(kernel="rbf", C=1.0, gamma="scale")` |
| Linear SVM for large data | `LinearSVC(C=1.0, max_iter=10000)` |
| k nearest neighbours | `KNeighborsClassifier(n_neighbors=5, metric="euclidean")` |
| K-Means clusters | `KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42).fit(data)` |
| Density clusters and noise | `DBSCAN(eps=1.5, min_samples=5).fit(data)` |

## Metrics
type: command-table
col: 2
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/09-model-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md

| Metric | Formula and use |
|---|---|
| Accuracy | $(TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)$. Misleading on imbalanced classes |
| Precision | $TP / (TP + FP)$. Use when false positives are costly |
| Recall | $TP / (TP + FN)$. Use when false negatives are costly |
| F1 | $2 \cdot P \cdot R / (P + R)$. Harmonic mean of both |
| AUC-ROC | 0.5 is random, 1.0 is perfect. Threshold independent |
| R-squared | $1 - SS_{\text{res}} / SS_{\text{tot}}$. Below 0 is worse than the mean |

## Key formulas
type: concepts
col: 3
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/02-linear-regression/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/03-logistic-regression/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/04-decision-trees/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/05-support-vector-machines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/10-bias-variance/docs/en.md

- **MSE**: $\text{MSE} = \frac{1}{n} \sum (y_{\text{predicted}} - y_{\text{actual}})^2$
- **Normal equation**: $w = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y$. Cost is $O(n^3)$ in features.
- **Ridge**: $\text{Cost} = \text{MSE} + \lambda \sum w_i^2$
- **Log loss**: $-\frac{1}{n} \sum \left( y \log(p) + (1-y) \log(1-p) \right)$, $p = \sigma(wx + b)$
- **Gini**: $\text{Gini}(S) = 1 - \sum_k p_k^2$. 0 is a pure node.
- **Soft margin SVM**: $\min \frac{1}{2} \lVert w \rVert^2 + C \sum_i \max(0, 1 - y_i (w^T x_i + b))$
- **RBF kernel**: $K(x, z) = \exp(-\gamma \lVert x - z \rVert^2)$
- **Error split**: $\text{Bias}^2 + \text{Variance} + \text{Irreducible Noise}$

## Leak-free preprocessing
type: annotated-code
col: 2
lang: python
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/code/pipeline.py

```python
# Leaky: the scaler sees the test rows
X_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X)
# Correct: fit on train, reuse on test
X_train_scaled = scaler.fit_transform(X_train)   # learn mean and std
X_test_scaled = scaler.transform(X_test)         # train statistics only
# Best: one Pipeline object for train and serve
pipe = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("model", LogisticRegression()),
])
pipe.fit(X_train, y_train)                       # fit_transform, then fit
predictions = pipe.predict(X_test)               # transform, then predict
scores = cross_val_score(full_pipe, df, y, cv=5, scoring="accuracy")  # refit per fold
```

## Validate without leakage
type: flow
col: 4
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/09-model-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md

1. **Split**: hold out a test set. Touch it exactly once, at the end.
2. **Folds**: split the rest into $K$ folds. Stratify for class ratios.
3. **Fit**: the scaler calls `fit_transform` on the $K-1$ training folds.
4. **Train**: the model calls `fit` on the scaled training folds.
5. **Score**: the scaler calls `transform` on the validation fold, then the model predicts.
6. **Average**: repeat for each fold and average the $K$ scores.
7. **Report**: score the final model on the test set.

## Questions
type: qa
col: 4
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/03-logistic-regression/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/05-support-vector-machines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/10-bias-variance/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/09-model-evaluation/docs/en.md

- **Why not MSE for logistic regression?** With a sigmoid it is non-convex. Log loss is convex.
- **Why scale before an SVM?** The margin depends on $\lVert w \rVert$.
- **Why does L1 select features?** It pushes some weights exactly to zero.
- **Will more data fix high bias?** No. Change the model.
- **Why class weights over oversampling?** Same in expectation, no duplicate rows.

## Tips
type: tips
col: 1
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/12-hyperparameter-tuning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/09-model-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md

- Sweep the learning rate first. Fix the rest at defaults.
- Search learning rate and regularization on a log scale.
- Set n_estimators high and let early stopping decide.
- Use nested cross-validation for the final estimate.
- Add a was_this_missing column before you impute.
- Pick the threshold on the validation set, not the test set.

## ColumnTransformer pipeline
type: architecture
col: 1
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/code/pipeline.py

```arch
node | cimp | 2,3 | SimpleImputer | most_frequent, then OneHotEncoder
node | ct | 1,4 | ColumnTransformer | joins both outputs
node | model | 2,4 | Model | GradientBoostingClassifier, predict
edge | raw | num | select

edge | cat | cimp |

```

## Tune hyperparameters
type: annotated-code
col: 1
lang: python
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/12-hyperparameter-tuning/docs/en.md

```python
param_dist = {
    "learning_rate": loguniform(1e-4, 0.5),      # log scale for rates
    "max_depth": randint(2, 10),                 # integer range
    "n_estimators": randint(50, 500),
}
search = RandomizedSearchCV(
    GradientBoostingRegressor(), param_dist,
    n_iter=100, cv=5,                            # 100 samples, 5 folds each
    scoring="neg_mean_squared_error",            # negated, higher is better
    random_state=42, n_jobs=-1,                  # all CPU cores
)
search.fit(X_train, y_train)
print(search.best_params_, -search.best_score_)  # negate back to MSE
```

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
col: 3
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/10-bias-variance/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/05-support-vector-machines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/12-hyperparameter-tuning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/06-knn-and-distances/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| High train and test error | high bias | more features, complex model, less regularization |
| Low train error, high test error | high variance | more data, regularization, simpler model |
| Test error rises, train error falls | overfitting in progress | early stopping |
| CV score higher than production | scaler fit on full data | Pipeline with cross_val_score |
| Crash on a new category | encoder never saw the value | `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` |
| 99% accuracy, no positives found | class imbalance | class weights, threshold tuning |
| SVM or KNN scores low | unscaled features | `StandardScaler()` first |
| Best value at the search edge | range too narrow | widen the search space |

type: glossary

from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/09-model-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/17-imbalanced-data/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/docs/en.md

- **AUC-ROC**: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic curve.
- **SMOTE**: synthetic minority samples by k-NN interpolation.

title: CNN Architectures and Transfer Learning
subtitle: Size convolutions, build LeNet to ResNet, train a classifier and fine-tune a pretrained backbone. PyTorch and NumPy.
markdown:
## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/02-convolutions-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md

- **Output size**: $H_{out} = \lfloor (H - K + 2P) / S \rfloor + 1$
- **Same padding**: $P = (K - 1) / 2$ for odd $K$ and $S = 1$.
- **Conv parameters**: `C_out * C_in * K * K + C_out`. The last term is the biases.
- **Receptive field**: $1 + L (K - 1)$ for $L$ stacked convs at stride 1.
- **Two 3x3 or one 5x5**: same 5x5 view. $18C^2$ against $25C^2$ parameters.
- **Residual block**: $y = F(x) + x$. The block learns identity with $F(x) = 0$.
- **Cross-entropy**: $-z_y + \log \sum_j \exp(z_j)$ on raw logits.
- **Layer-wise LR decay**: $\mathrm{lr}_k = \mathrm{base} \cdot \mathrm{decay}^{L - k}$

## Four families
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md

- **LeNet-5 (1998)**: conv, avg pool, dense, tanh. 60,000 parameters.
- **AlexNet (2012)**: ReLU, dropout, 5 conv and 3 dense layers. 60M parameters.
- **VGG (2014)**: only 3x3 convs, 16 or 19 layers. 138M parameters.
- **Inception (2014)**: 1x1, 3x3, 5x5 and pool in parallel, then concatenate.
- **ResNet (2015)**: identity skip connections. 100+ layers train.
- **BasicBlock**: two 3x3 convs with a skip. ResNet-18 and ResNet-34.
- **Bottleneck**: 1x1 down, 3x3, 1x1 up. ResNet-50, -101, -152.
- **ResNet-18 or VGG-16**: 11.7M or 138M parameters. Top-1 69.8% or 71.6%.

## TinyResNet for 32x32 input
type: architecture
from: phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/code/main.py

```arch
node | in | 1,1 | Input | (1, 3, 32, 32)
node | stem | 2,1 | stem | 3x3 conv, 32 ch, BN, ReLU
node | l1 | 3,1 | layer1 | 2 BasicBlocks, 32 ch
node | l2 | 4,1 | layer2 | stride 2, 64 ch
node | l3 | 4,2 | layer3 | stride 2, 128 ch
node | l4 | 3,2 | layer4 | stride 2, 256 ch
node | head | 2,2 | head | AdaptiveAvgPool2d, Linear
node | out | 1,2 | Logits | 10 classes
edge | in | stem |
edge | stem | l1 |
edge | l1 | l2 |
edge | l2 | l3 |
edge | l3 | l4 |
edge | l4 | head |
edge | head | out |
```

## ResNet BasicBlock
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/code/main.py

```python
self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(in_c, out_c, kernel_size=3, stride=stride, padding=1, bias=False)  # BN beta holds the bias
self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(out_c, out_c, kernel_size=3, stride=1, padding=1, bias=False)
if stride != 1 or in_c != out_c:
    self.shortcut = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Conv2d(in_c, out_c, kernel_size=1, stride=stride, bias=False),
        nn.BatchNorm2d(out_c))               # 1x1 conv matches the shape
else:
    self.shortcut = nn.Identity()            # no-op skip
out = F.relu(self.bn1(self.conv1(x)))
out = self.bn2(self.conv2(out))              # no ReLU before the add
out = out + self.shortcut(x)                 # F(x) + x
return F.relu(out)
```

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/04-computer-vision/02-convolutions-from-scratch/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Output size of one conv | `output_size(h_in, k, p, s)` |
| Receptive field of a stack | `receptive_field(layers)` |
| Conv as one matmul | `conv2d_im2col(x, w, b, padding=1)` |
| Apply a hand kernel | `apply_kernel(x[0], KERNELS["sobel_x"])` |
| Mix a batch | `mixup_batch(x, y, num_classes, alpha=0.2)` |
| Loss on soft labels | `soft_cross_entropy(logits, soft_targets)` |
| Frozen backbone, new head | `make_feature_extractor(num_classes=10)` |
| Keep BN running stats | `freeze_bn_stats(model)` |

## One training epoch
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md

1. **Augment**: `random_hflip()` and `random_crop(pad=4)` with reflect pad. Train set only.
2. **Normalise**: `standardize(mean, std)` with the mean and std of your train set.
3. **DataLoader**: `shuffle=True` for train. `shuffle=False` for val.
4. **Model**: `model.train()` first. The model gives raw logits (N, C).
5. **Loss**: `soft_cross_entropy` with mixup, else `cross_entropy` with `label_smoothing=0.1`.
6. **Step**: `optimizer.zero_grad()`, `loss.backward()`, `optimizer.step()`.
7. **Metrics**: add `loss.item()`, so no graph stays alive.
8. **Epoch end**: `scheduler.step()`. Then `model.eval()` and evaluate under `torch.no_grad`.

## Fine-tune with discriminative LR
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/code/main.py

```python
model = resnet18(weights=ResNet18_Weights.IMAGENET1K_V1)
model.fc = nn.Linear(model.fc.in_features, 10)   # new head
groups = discriminative_param_groups(model, base_lr=1e-3, decay=0.3)
optimizer = SGD(groups, momentum=0.9, weight_decay=1e-4, nesterov=True)
scheduler = CosineAnnealingLR(optimizer, T_max=epochs)
for epoch in range(epochs):
    model.train()
    if freeze_bn:
        freeze_bn_stats(model)                    # after model.train()
start, unfreeze = progressive_unfreeze_schedule(model)
start()                                           # only fc trains
unfreeze(epoch)                                   # layer4 first, then layer3
```

## Pick a transfer recipe
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md

- **< 1k images, close to ImageNet**: freeze the backbone. Train the head only.
- **1k-10k, close**: freeze the first 2-3 stages. Fine-tune the rest.
- **10k-100k, any domain**: fine-tune end-to-end with discriminative LR.
- **100k+, far domain**: fine-tune everything. Consider training from scratch.
- **BN, >= 5k examples**: keep BN in train mode. It updates its running statistics.
- **BN, small dataset**: freeze BN in eval mode. Keep the ImageNet statistics.
- **Tiny batch per GPU**: replace BN with GroupNorm.
- **Head to replace**: `backbone.fc` (ResNet), `backbone.classifier[1]` (EfficientNet, MobileNet).

## Training defaults
type: defaults
span: 1
from: phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SGD `lr` | 0.1 | TinyResNet from scratch, cosine over 10 epochs |
| `momentum` | 0.9 | With `nesterov=True` |
| `weight_decay` | 5e-4 | Fine-tune uses 1e-4 |
| `label_smoothing` | 0.1 | Target 1-eps for the true class |
| Mixup `alpha` | 0.2 | lambda from Beta(a, a) |
| `base_lr` | 1e-3 | The fc group. Earlier stages get less |
| `decay` | 0.3 | conv1 gets about 0.00243 times `base_lr` |
| `batch_size` | 128 | Val loader uses 256 |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Wrong gradient, flat curve | Softmax before the loss | Pass raw logits to `CrossEntropyLoss` |
| Looks like an unstable LR | Gradients accumulate | Call `optimizer.zero_grad()` each step |
| About 1% accuracy lost | ImageNet mean and std on CIFAR-10 | Compute stats on your train set |
| A "6" becomes a "9" | Augment changes the label | Use smaller rotation ranges |
| Fine-tuned below pretrained-only | LR or BN bug | Use discriminative LR, check BN mode |
| 5-15% accuracy lost silently | BN stats from another distribution | Freeze BN stats or use GroupNorm |
| All images get one class | LR destroys pretrained features | Lower the backbone LR |
| Deep plain net trains worse | Degradation past ~20 layers | Add residual connections |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/02-convolutions-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md

- **Why 3x3 kernels?** It is the smallest odd kernel with a centre.
- **How to downsample without a pool?** Use a conv with `stride=2`. It halves H and W.
- **Why does mixup raise train loss?** The targets are soft. Test accuracy goes up.
- **Which two numbers for a transfer run?** Pretrained-only is the floor. Fine-tuned is the ceiling.
- **Why a smaller LR for early layers?** They hold generic edge and texture features.
- **When to rebuild the optimizer?** Each time the set of trainable parameters changes.

## Mask R-CNN pipeline
type: architecture

```arch
node | img | 1,1 | Input image | list of (3, H, W)
node | bb | 2,1 | ResNet backbone | strides 4, 8, 16, 32
node | fpn | 3,1 | FPN | top down + lateral
node | rpn | 4,1 | RPN | about 1000 proposals
node | roi | 3,2 | RoIAlign | bilinear, no rounding
node | box | 2,2 | Box head | class + refine
node | mask | 4,2 | Mask head | 28x28 per class
node | nms | 1,2 | NMS | boxes, labels, masks
edge | img | bb |
edge | bb | fpn |
edge | fpn | rpn |
edge | fpn | roi | features
edge | rpn | roi | top K
edge | roi | box |
edge | roi | mask |
edge | box | nms |
```

## Preprocess for a pretrained model
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/01-image-fundamentals/docs/en.md

1. **Decode**: the file becomes `uint8` HWC in `[0, 255]`.
2. **Colour**: convert to RGB. BGR input costs about ten points.
3. **Float and layout**: divide by 255, then HWC to NCHW.
4. **Resize**: shorter side to 256, bilinear.
5. **Crop**: center crop to 224x224.
6. **Standardize**: subtract the ImageNet mean, divide by the std.
7. **Model**: the input now matches the training input.

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/02-convolutions-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/06-object-detection-yolo/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/07-semantic-segmentation-unet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md

- **Output size**: $H_{\text{out}} = \left\lfloor \frac{H - K + 2P}{S} \right\rfloor + 1$
- **Same padding**: $P = (K - 1) / 2$ for odd $K$ and $S = 1$
- **Conv params**: $C_{\text{out}} \cdot C_{\text{in}} \cdot K \cdot K + C_{\text{out}}$
- **Receptive field**: $1 + L \cdot (K - 1)$ for $L$ stacked convs, stride 1
- **Residual**: $y = F(x) + x$
- **IoU**: $\mathrm{IoU}(A, B) = \frac{\mathop{\mathrm{area}}(A \cap B)}{\mathop{\mathrm{area}}(A \cup B)}$
- **Dice**: $\frac{2 \sum (p \cdot y)}{\sum p + \sum y + \epsilon}$, and $\text{Dice} = 2 \cdot \text{IoU} / (1 + \text{IoU})$
- **YOLO decode**: $x = (\sigma(t_x) + \text{cell}_x) \cdot \text{stride}$, $w = \text{anchor}_w \cdot \exp(t_w)$

## ViT forward
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

```python
self.proj = nn.Conv2d(in_channels, dim, kernel_size=patch_size, stride=patch_size)
self.cls_token = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, 1, dim))  # one learned token
self.pos_embed = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(1, num_patches + 1, dim))  # learned
x = self.proj(x)                                 # (N, dim, 14, 14) at 224 px
x = x.flatten(2).transpose(1, 2)                 # (N, 196, dim) tokens
cls = self.cls_token.expand(x.size(0), -1, -1)
x = torch.cat([cls, x], dim=1)                   # (N, 197, dim)
x = x + self.pos_embed                           # add position
normed = self.ln1(x)                             # pre-LN
a, _ = self.attn(normed, normed, normed, need_weights=False)
x = x + a                                        # residual
x = x + self.mlp(self.ln2(x))                    # D to 4D to D, GELU
return self.head(self.ln(x[:, 0]))               # classify from [CLS]
```

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/01-image-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/07-semantic-segmentation-unet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/08-instance-segmentation-mask-rcnn/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Garbage output, no error | raw uint8 into the model | divide by 255, then standardize |
| First conv sees height as channels | HWC input | `permute(2, 0, 1)` to CHW |
| Wrong gradient, no error | softmax before cross-entropy | pass raw logits |
| Unstable loss | no `zero_grad()` each step | call it before `backward()` |
| Fine-tuned worse than linear probe | LR or BN bug | discriminative LR, `freeze_bn_stats` |
| 99% pixel accuracy, useless masks | class imbalance | add Dice to the loss |
| Checkerboard artifacts | transposed conv | bilinear upsample + 3x3 conv |
| Head has one class too few | background not counted | `num_classes` = classes + 1 |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/04-computer-vision/06-object-detection-yolo/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/07-semantic-segmentation-unet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/08-instance-segmentation-mask-rcnn/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

- **IoU**: Intersection over Union. Overlap of two boxes or masks.
- **NMS**: Non-maximum suppression. Keeps the top box, drops overlaps.
- **mAP@0.5:0.95**: COCO AP. Mean over IoU 0.5 to 0.95, step 0.05.
- **mIoU**: mean IoU over classes. The segmentation metric.
- **FPN**: Feature Pyramid Network. Semantic features at every stride.
- **RPN**: Region Proposal Network. Object or no object per anchor.
- **ViT**: Vision Transformer. Patches as tokens.
- **MAE**: Masked Autoencoder. Mask 75% of patches, reconstruct.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/02-convolutions-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/03-cnns-lenet-to-resnet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/08-instance-segmentation-mask-rcnn/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/06-object-detection-yolo/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

- **Why 3x3 everywhere?** Two 3x3 convs see 5x5 with $18C^2$ params, not $25C^2$.
- **Why residuals?** A block can learn identity, so depth stops hurting.
- **Why RoIAlign over RoIPool?** No rounding. It adds 3 to 4 mask AP on COCO.
- **Why anchors?** The head predicts small deltas from a prior box.
- **Why pre-LN in ViT?** It trains deep stacks without warmup.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/04-computer-vision/04-image-classification/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/05-transfer-learning/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/07-semantic-segmentation-unet/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/06-object-detection-yolo/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/01-image-fundamentals/docs/en.md

- Compute mean and std on your own training set.
- Use nearest resize for masks and label maps.
- Print linear probe and fine-tuned accuracy for every transfer run.
- Rebuild the optimizer when the set of trainable parameters changes.
- Report IoU per class, not only mIoU.
- Report precision, recall, AP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.95 together.

title: Constitutional AI and Input/Output Classifiers
subtitle: Critique-and-revise training, tier resolution, input and output rails, their bypasses, and a YAML rules engine.
markdown:
## CAI training, two phases
type: flow
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/05-constitutional-ai-rlaif/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/17-constitutional-ai/docs/en.md

1. **SFT model**: answers a red-team prompt. It is helpful but not yet harmless.
2. **Critic**: reads one sampled principle and critiques the response.
3. **Reviser**: revises the response to address the critique. That is the SFT target.
4. **Policy**: generates pairs of completions.
5. **Feedback model**: ranks each pair against sampled principles.
6. **Reward model**: trains on the AI preferences. PPO runs against it.

type: concepts

title: Context Engineering and Agent Memory
subtitle: Budget the window, order the context, page memory in and out, fuse memory stores and persist agent state.
markdown:
## The context window budget
type: architecture
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md

```arch
node | sys | 1,1 | System prompt | ~500 tokens, goes first
node | tools | 2,1 | Tool definitions | ~2K-8K tokens
node | ret | 3,1 | Retrieved context | ~2K-10K tokens
node | hist | 4,1 | Conversation history | ~2K-20K tokens
node | shots | 1,2 | Few-shot examples | ~1K-3K tokens
node | query | 2,2 | User query | ~100-500 tokens, goes last
node | gen | 3,2 | Generation budget | ~2K-8K tokens
node | win | 4,2 | Context window | 128K tokens | model
edge | sys | tools |
edge | tools | ret |
edge | ret | hist |
edge | shots | query |
edge | query | gen |
edge | gen | win | fits or truncates
```

## Numbers that matter
type: concepts
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md

- **Lost in the middle**: 85-90% accuracy with the document first or last. 60-70% at position 10 of 20.
- **Low zone**: positions 40-70% of the context lose 10-20% accuracy.
- **Curated beats dumped**: a 10K token context often beats a dumped 100K token context.
- **Tool cost**: 50-200 tokens per tool. 50 tools at 150 tokens is 7,500 tokens.
- **Tool pruning**: cuts tool tokens by 60-80%.
- **History**: 50 turns at 200 tokens is 10,000 tokens.
- **Summary**: 100 tokens replace 10 turns that took 2,000 tokens.
- **Token estimate**: word count times 1.3 in `count_tokens`.

## Assemble context per query
type: flow
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/code/main.py

1. **Classifier**: `classify_intent(query)` counts keyword hits per intent. No hit gives `["code"]`.
2. **Tool selector**: `select_tools(query, token_budget=2000)` keeps tools whose category matches.
3. **Retriever**: `score_relevance(query, documents)` scores word overlap. Docs below `threshold` drop out.
4. **Reorder**: `reorder_lost_in_middle(items, scores)` puts the best items first and last.
5. **History**: `ConversationManager` summarizes the oldest 2 turns while history is over the cap.
6. **Budget**: `ContextBudget` truncates each component to its cap and to the space left.

## ContextEngine.assemble
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/code/main.py, phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md

```python
budget = ContextBudget(max_tokens=128000, generation_reserve=4000)
budget.allocate("system_prompt", self.system_prompt, max_tokens=1000)
tools, tool_tokens = select_tools(query, token_budget=2000)
budget.allocate("tools", tool_text, max_tokens=2000)
budget.allocate("retrieved_context", doc_text, max_tokens=3000)
budget.allocate("conversation_history", history_text, max_tokens=5000)
budget.allocate("user_query", query, max_tokens=500)  # query goes last
print(budget.report())  # tokens and percent per component
```

## Memory designs side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/14-agent-engineering/07-memory-virtual-context-memgpt/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/08-memory-blocks-sleep-time-compute/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/09-hybrid-memory-mem0/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/34-repo-memory-and-state/docs/en.md

| Factor | MemGPT two tiers | Letta blocks | Mem0 hybrid | Repo memory |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Stores | Main context plus archival | Core, recall, archival | Vector, KV, graph | JSON files under a schema |
| Write | Memory tool call | Block tools and sleep-time rewrites | `add(text, user_id, metadata)` to all three | Validate, then atomic write |
| Read | `archival_memory_search` | Core blocks stay in the prompt | `search(query, user_id)` fuses scores | Load and validate |

| Main risk | Memory rot, poisoning | Block bloat, silent drift | Embedding drift, graph explosion | Partial writes |
| Use it when | Data is larger than the window | Some facts must stay in the prompt | Queries mix similarity, lookup, relations | State must outlive the chat |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/07-memory-virtual-context-memgpt/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/08-memory-blocks-sleep-time-compute/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/09-hybrid-memory-mem0/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/34-repo-memory-and-state/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Model ignores a fact in the middle | Lost in the middle | Key facts first, query last. Repeat the key point at the end |
| Tools fill the window | Every tool sent on every call | Classify intent and prune tools |
| Retrieval drowns in stale facts | Memory rot | Consolidate and invalidate in a sleep pass |
| Agent obeys an old injected note | Memory poisoning | Treat retrieved memory as untrusted text |
| Agent recalls but cannot cite | Citation loss | Store session ID and turn ID with each write |
| Block hits its cap | Block bloat | Summarize before the write that crosses the cap |
| One user sees another user's facts | Scopes mixed | Pick one scope for each write |
| Session resumes on corrupt state | Non-atomic write | Temp file, `fsync`, `os.replace` |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/05-context-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/07-memory-virtual-context-memgpt/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/08-memory-blocks-sleep-time-compute/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/09-hybrid-memory-mem0/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/34-repo-memory-and-state/docs/en.md

- **Bigger window, no memory?** 128k-window baselines still miss long-horizon facts that a 4k-window agent with external memory catches.
- **Why sleep-time compute?** Primary turns do not wait. The sleep agent can use a stronger, slower model.
- **Why three stores?** A single store is wrong for two of three query classes.
- **How does fusion rank?** A weighted sum of relevance, importance and recency. Weights change per product.
- **What goes in repo memory?** Task id, touched files, assumptions, blockers, next action. Not raw chat transcripts.

## Migration rehearsal
type: flow
from: projects/database-migration-rehearsal/API.md, projects/database-migration-rehearsal/solution/main.py, projects/database-migration-rehearsal/README.md

1. **snapshot**: open the source read-only and back it up into memory.
2. **snapshot**: record schema, row counts, row-content SHA-256 and sequences.
3. **rehearse**: apply the migration to the in-memory copy only.
4. **rehearse**: deny ATTACH, DETACH, PRAGMA, virtual tables and file functions.
5. **test_rollback**: run migration and rollback on one disposable backup.
6. **reversible**: no errors and the restored snapshot equals before.
7. **receipt**: check each invariant. `release_ready` needs all of them and rollback.

## Errors and fixes
type: troubleshooting
from: projects/csv-repair-workbench/solution/main.py, projects/csv-sql-question-workbench/solution/main.py, projects/dataset-contract-gate/README.md, projects/dataset-split-auditor/README.md, projects/database-migration-rehearsal/API.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "ragged row" | A row has the wrong cell count | Fix the source row |
| Pending "ambiguous date" | Both parts are 12 or less and differ | Give an ISO date in decisions |
| "stale review" | Table or recipe changed after review | Review the new preview again |
| "Query rejected: " | SQL left the read boundary | Write one SELECT over `data` |
| "Aggregate column must contain finite numeric values" | Column is TEXT | Aggregate a REAL column |
| Contract `--check` exits 1 | Rows are in quarantine | Read review.html. Decide on rows apart |
| Split `usable` is false | Content or group leak | Split by group with `--split` |
| `release_ready` is false | Rollback is not exact | Write rollback SQL that restores rows |

## Rules in code
type: concepts
from: projects/csv-repair-workbench/API.md, projects/dataset-contract-gate/API.md, projects/dataset-split-auditor/solution/main.py, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/09-data-management/docs/en.md

- **Recipe order**: trim, then alias, then date for each column.
- **Changes**: each change names row, column, before and after.
- **No coercion**: Boolean true fails integer and number fields.
- **Duplicates**: every colliding row is reported, the first one too.
- **Gate**: a dataset passes with no quarantined rows and no dataset issues.
- **Fingerprint**: NFKC, casefold and collapsed spaces, then SHA-256.
- **Group split**: SHA-256 of seed and group over `2**256`, below the fraction is test.
- **Formats**: Parquet for storage, Arrow in memory, CSV and JSON to exchange.

## Questions
type: qa
from: projects/dataset-split-auditor/README.md, projects/database-migration-rehearsal/API.md, projects/dataset-contract-gate/API.md, projects/csv-sql-question-workbench/README.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/09-data-management/docs/en.md

- **Does normalization catch paraphrases?** No. It finds exact normalized copies only.
- **Does rehearsal change the source database?** No. The source is never opened writable.
- **Does the model run its SQL freely?** No. SQLite authorization still controls execution.
- **Can I drop quarantined rows at once?** No. Partitions are evidence, not permission to discard.
- **Why set a seed?** The same seed produces the same split every time.

- Wait for the gate command to finish before you load its outputs.
- Keep the input beside the output so others can reproduce it.

title: Debate, Roles and Review Panels
subtitle: Run N agents for R rounds, split work into planner, executor, critic and verifier, and gate reviews with a quorum.
markdown:
## Debate protocol
type: flow
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/07-society-of-mind-debate/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/25-multi-agent-debate/docs/en.md

1. **Each of N agents**: produces an initial answer to the question.
2. **Round r = 2..R**: each agent reads the other agents' round r-1 answers.
3. **Each agent**: critiques the peers and gives an updated answer.
4. **Every round**: re-inject the question to stop topic drift.
5. **After R rounds**: majority-vote the final answers.
6. **Cost**: N agents × R rounds = N·R LLM calls with growing context.

## Debate topologies
type: comparison
from: phases/14-agent-engineering/25-multi-agent-debate/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/25-multi-agent-debate/code/main.py

| Factor | Full mesh | Sparse star |
|---|---|---|
| Who reads whom | Every debater reads every peer | Spokes read only the hub |
| Runner | `full_mesh_round` | `sparse_star_round` |
| Ops per round | `ops += len(peers)` per debater | Spokes read only the hub |
| N=5, R=3 | 60 critique ops | 12 critique ops |
| Proposals at N=5, R=3 | 15 | 15 |
| Main risk | Convergence collapse | Hub failure |
| Fix for the risk | Required disagreement rounds | Rotate or use multiple hubs |

## Four canonical roles
type: concepts
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/08-role-specialization/docs/en.md

- **Planner**: reads the goal. Output is a structured plan or spec.
- **Executor**: reads one plan step at a time. Output is the artifact.
- **Critic**: reads the artifact against the plan. Output is accept/reject with reasons.
- **Verifier**: runs a deterministic check. Output is pass/fail with evidence.
- **Critic vs verifier**: a critic is subjective and LLM-based. A verifier is code. They are not the same role.
- **Communicative dehallucination**: the executor asks the relevant role by name when a detail is missing.
- **SOP pattern**: `Code = SOP(Team)`. Each role has a strict input/output schema.

## Role pipeline in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/08-role-specialization/code/main.py

```python
spec = planner(user_wish)            # Spec with signature and 3 tests
art = executor(spec)                 # Artifact holds a code string
crep = critic(spec, art)             # checks def, return, task name
vrep = verifier(spec, art)           # runs the tests
exec(art.code, ns, ns)               # verifier sandbox namespace
fn = ns.get(spec.task_name)          # no callable gives a failure
got = fn(*args)                      # compare with expected
if crep.approved and vrep.passed:    # ship only when both pass
```

type: architecture
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/10-multi-agent-software-team/docs/en.md

```arch
node | issue | 1,1 | GitHub issue URL | | client
node | arch | 2,1 | Architect | plan with subtasks + interfaces | model
node | board | 3,1 | Task board | file / Redis | queue
node | coders | 4,1 | Coders A to D | worktree + Daytona each | process
node | merge | 4,2 | Merge coordinator | three-way merge | process
node | rev | 3,2 | Reviewer | approve or request changes | model
node | test | 2,2 | Tester | clean sandbox | process
node | pr | 1,2 | Open PR | | client
edge | issue | arch |
edge | arch | board | plan_request
edge | board | coders | subtask
edge | coders | merge | diff_ready
edge | merge | rev | review_needed
edge | rev | test | approved
edge | test | pr | test_passed
```

from: phases/19-capstone-projects/10-multi-agent-software-team/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/10-multi-agent-software-team/docs/en.md

## Quorum and budget code
type: annotated-code
lang: typescript
from: projects/multi-agent-code-review-panel/solution/main.ts

```typescript
if (ids.has(review.reviewer)) throw new Error("duplicate reviewer");
if (seen.has(key)) continue;       // one vote per reviewer per group
status: g.supporters.length >= quorum ? "consensus" : "needs-review",

if (spent + r.cost > budget) {     // trace status "budget-skipped"
controller.abort();                // deadline hit, status "timeout"
```
