```bash
sbx policy init balanced  # once, before the first sandbox
sbx create shell --name m101-policy  # no workspace mount
sbx exec m101-policy sh -c \
  'curl -sS --max-time 10 https://example.com'  # Approval required
sbx policy log m101-policy  # forward, default deny
sbx policy allow network \
  --sandbox m101-policy example.com  # rule for one sandbox
sbx policy check network example.com \
  --sandbox m101-policy --verbose --json  # read allowed, rule
```

## What the agent sees inside
type: command-table
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/04-env.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/10-env-sentinel.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/09-policy-log.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-4-sbx-policy-log-and-the-proxy.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-3-sbx-policy-init-allow-deny-and-check-network.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `HTTPS_PROXY=http://gateway.docker.internal:3128` | Forward proxy for HTTP and HTTPS |
| `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=proxy-managed` | Sentinel. The real key stays on the host |
| `M101_RECV_KEY=sbx-cs-<rand>` | Custom secret placeholder |
| `SSH_AUTH_SOCK=/run/ssh-agent.sock` | Host SSH agent, forwarded by default |
| `forward-bypass` | Log proxy type. Tunnel, no inspection |
| `transparent` | Log proxy type. Other TCP, no injection |
| `"deny_kind": "explicit"` | A rule denied it. `implicit` means no allow |

## Defaults
type: defaults
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/r-1-sbx-commands.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/r-3-settings-keys-environment-variables-and-paths.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `--name` | `<agent>-<workdir>` | Set it, so two agents stay apart |
| `-m, --memory` | 50% of host memory | Clamped from 512 MiB to 32 GiB |
| `--pull` | `always` | Also `missing` or `never` |
| `--skills` | `readonly` | Also `off` or `readwrite` |
| `secret set --refresh` | `55m` | Refresh for a dynamic source |
| `ssh.agentForwardingEnabled` | `true` | Turn off for agents you do not trust |
| `sandbox.disk.dockerVolume` | `10g` | Size of `/var/lib/docker` |
| `kit.allowedSources` | `["docker.io/"]` | Allowed remote kit sources |

## Key concepts
type: concepts
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/r-8-glossary-and-index-of-figures.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-3-sbx-policy-init-allow-deny-and-check-network.md

- **Sandbox**: a microVM with its own kernel and a private Docker Engine.
- **Clone mode**: `--clone`. The agent works on a private clone. Commits return through a remote.
- **Preset**: `allow-all`, `balanced` or `deny-all`, set once with `sbx policy init`.
- **Policy scope**: `global` for all sandboxes, or one sandbox with `--sandbox`.
- **Deny wins**: a deny rule takes precedence over an allow for the same host.
- **Sentinel**: the placeholder the agent sees in place of a secret.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/09-blocked.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/05-ports-curl.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/06-cp.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/09-deny-conflict.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/09-rm-allow.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/capture/out/07-template-save.txt, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-2-sbx-exec-cp-and-ports.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-5-sbx-secret-set-import-and-set-custom.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-2-clone-and-run-sandbox-source.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-4-sandboxd-diagnose-and-reset.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Approval required for example.com:443.` | No allow rule matches | `sbx policy allow network --sandbox <name> <host>` |
| curl to `::1` fails with exit 7 | Port published as `tcp4` | Publish `8080/tcp` for both families |
| `copying between sandboxes is not supported` | `cp` needs a host side | Copy through the host |
| Deny `conflicts with existing allow rule` | Allow and deny in one scope | `sbx policy rm network --id <uuid>` first |
| No API key from `~/.zshrc` | Host environment not read since v0.35.0 | `sbx secret set` or `sbx secret import` |
| `ensure daemon: daemon exited unexpectedly` | sandboxd problem | `sbx daemon status --json`, read `daemon.log` |

## Q&A
type: qa
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/1-1-sbx-and-docker-agent.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-1-sbx-run-create-stop-and-rm.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-4-sbx-policy-log-and-the-proxy.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-5-sbx-secret-set-import-and-set-custom.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-2-clone-and-run-sandbox-source.md

- **Do I need Docker Desktop?** No. You need `sbx login`. Containers of the agent never show in host `docker ps`.
- **stop or rm?** `sbx stop` keeps state. `sbx rm` deletes the sandbox, its state and scoped secrets.
- **Does a host allow block a gist upload?** No. A host allow passes any method, path and body.
- **Does the agent see my key?** No. It sees `proxy-managed`. The proxy adds the key after the VM.

## Tips
type: tips
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-1-sbx-run-create-stop-and-rm.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-3-sbx-policy-init-allow-deny-and-check-network.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-5-sbx-secret-set-import-and-set-custom.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-4-sandboxd-diagnose-and-reset.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/2-2-sbx-exec-cp-and-ports.md

- Set memory, ports, skills and static MCP servers at creation. A re-attach ignores them.
- Run `sbx prune --dry-run` before a prune.
- Add narrow rules with `--sandbox`. Keep global rules for hosts every agent needs.
- Store keys with `sbx secret set`, never with `-e KEY`.
- Bind a custom secret to exact hosts. The proxy replaces the placeholder anywhere.

title: Edge Inference Targets
subtitle: Pick an edge target and a quantization format. Bandwidth ceilings, formats, export steps and on-device measurement.
markdown:
## Four edge targets side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/code/main.py

| Factor | Apple ANE | Qualcomm Hexagon | WebGPU / WebLLM | NVIDIA Jetson |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Peak | 38 TOPS, M4 / A18 | 45 TOPS, X Elite / 8 Gen 4 | Browser GPU, no install | Orin Nano Super, AGX Orin, Thor |
| Memory | Unified, no copy | Separate memory domain | Browser penalty ~25% | Memory-bound on Nano |
| Access | Core ML or MPS | QNN SDK, AI Hub | WebGPU compute shaders | vLLM, TensorRT Edge-LLM |
| Format | INT4 weights + FP16 activations | QNN INT8 / INT4 | Q4 MLC (`q4f16_1`) | Q4 GGUF, TRT-LLM INT4, NVFP4 |
| Observed | 8 tok/s estimate, A18, 8B Q4 | 7 tok/s, 8 Gen 3, 8B Q4 | ~41 tok/s, M3 Max, 8B Q4 | ~40 tok/s, AGX Orin, gpt-oss-20b |
| Limit | Native ANE needs Core ML | Convert from PyTorch or ONNX | ~70-75% mobile coverage | Nano fits 3B models |

## Use each target when
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

- **Apple ANE**: an iOS app. Convert with Core ML. INT4 weights plus FP16 activations.
- **Qualcomm Hexagon**: Snapdragon phones and Windows ARM laptops. Convert with QNN or AI Hub.
- **WebGPU / WebLLM**: a browser app with no install. Keep a server fallback on the same OpenAI-compatible API.
- **Jetson Orin Nano Super**: Llama 3.2 3B or Phi-3 on 8GB.
- **Jetson AGX / Thor**: larger models, NVFP4 plus FP8 KV, EAGLE-3.
- **GGUF Q4_K_M**: CPU and Apple Silicon laptops.
- **GPTQ or AWQ INT4**: GPU inference with CUDA or ROCm.

## Decode ceiling
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/code/main.py

```python
def ceiling(target: Target, model_gb: float) -> float:
    seconds_per_token = model_gb / target.bandwidth_gb_s  # all weights per token
    return 1 / seconds_per_token  # tok/s upper bound
model_gb = 4.7  # Llama 3.1 8B Q4
Target("Apple A18 (iPhone 16)",   60,   8,  "phone with ANE")  # GB/s, observed tok/s
Target("Snapdragon 8 Gen 3",      77,   7,  "mid/high Android")
Target("WebGPU on M3 Max",       400,  41,  "browser penalty ~25%")
Target("Jetson AGX Orin",        205,  45,  "edge-datacenter bridge")
```

## Bandwidth math
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md

- **Rule**: decode reads the full set of weights for every token.
- **7B Q4**: 3.5 GB. At 50 GB/s one token takes 70 ms, ~14 tok/s.
- **High-end mobile**: 90 GB/s gives ~25 tok/s.
- **HBM3 at 3 TB/s**: 1.2 ms per token, ceiling 830 tok/s.
- **Gap**: 30-50x between datacenter and mobile DRAM.
- **Long context**: 4 GB model plus 2 GB KV at 32K on an 8 GB phone is OOM.
- **Context on edge**: keep 4K-8K unless you accept Q4 KV.

## Quantization formats, Llama 3 70B
type: comparison
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

| Factor | FP16 | FP8 | AWQ INT4 | GGUF Q4_K_M |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Size | 140GB | 70GB | 35GB | 40GB |
| Perplexity | 3.12 | 3.14 | 4.18 | 4.25 |
| MMLU | 79.5% | 79.3% | 78.1% | 77.9% |
| Tokens/sec | 38, A100 | 55, A100 | 75, A100 | 28, CPU |
| Best for | Baseline | H100 deploys | GPU inference | CPU, Metal |

## Quantize and dequantize
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

```python
scale = max(abs(tensor)) / 127  # symmetric INT8
quantized = clamp(round(tensor / scale), -128, 127)
reconstructed = quantized * scale  # error at most scale / 2
quantized = round(tensor / scale) + zero_point  # asymmetric, for ReLU outputs
```

## Tasks
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/code/main.py, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Edge decode ceilings, lesson 12 | `code/main.py` |
| Measure p50, p95, p99 on the device | `measure_latency(model, input_shape, device="cpu", warmup=10, iters=50)` |
| Time GPU work correctly | `torch.cuda.synchronize()` before and after the timed block |
| Static INT8 PTQ config | `model.qconfig = tq.get_default_qconfig(backend)` |
| Export to ONNX | `torch.onnx.export(model, sample_input, path, opset_version=17)` |
| GPTQ INT4 | `GPTQConfig(bits=4, group_size=128)` |
| GGUF Q4_K_M | `llama.cpp/build/bin/llama-quantize llama-8b-f16.gguf llama-8b-q4km.gguf Q4_K_M` |
| WebLLM weights | `mlc_llm convert_weight` plus a compiled `.wasm` |

## Vision deployment path
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md

1. **Pick a backbone**: under 3M params, MobileNetV3-Small. 3-10M, EfficientNet-Lite-B0.
2. **Measure**: warm up 5-10 passes. Fix the input size to production resolution.
3. **Quantise**: post-training static INT8. Verify accuracy loss under 1%.
4. **Export**: PyTorch to ONNX. `dynamic_axes` allows any batch size.
5. **Runtime**: TensorRT on Jetson. Core ML on iOS. TFLite on Android.
6. **Decide**: from a table of model, latency, memory and accuracy measured on the device.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 8B Q4 at 3 tok/s on iPhone 16 Pro | Mobile bandwidth gap | Smaller model or fewer bits |
| OOM at long context on a phone | KV cache for 32K is 2 GB | Keep context at 4K-8K or use Q4 KV |
| WebLLM rejects a GGUF file | GGUF is not supported | Convert to Q4 MLC (`q4f16_1`) |
| llama.cpp on iOS skips the ANE | Metal backend uses MPS | Convert with Core ML |
| No WebGPU on an old Android browser | Needs Chrome v121+ | Fall back to the server API |
| First latency numbers too high | Cold caches and JIT | Warm up with 5-10 dummy passes |
| Naive INT4 output is garbage | Rounding errors accumulate | GPTQ or AWQ with calibration data |
| Perplexity delta above 2.0 | Something went wrong | Recheck. Under 0.5 is excellent |

## Format glossary
type: glossary
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

- **BF16**: 8 exponent bits, 7 mantissa bits. Same range as FP32.
- **FP8 E4M3**: weights and activations for inference.
- **FP8 E5M2**: gradients in training. More range.
- **INT8**: 256 values from -128 to 127. Needs a scale factor.
- **INT4**: 16 levels. Needs GPTQ or AWQ for quality.
- **GGUF**: llama.cpp file with mixed precision layers.
- **PTQ**: quantize after training. 128-1024 calibration examples.
- **QAT**: fake quantization in training. Better at INT4 and INT2.

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/11-quantization/docs/en.md

- **Why is compute secondary on edge?** Decode is memory-bound. Bandwidth sets the ceiling.
- **How fast is WebLLM against native?** About 70-80% of native on the same backend.
- **FLOPs or latency?** FLOPs for architecture search. On-device latency for deployment.
- **PTQ or QAT for vision?** PTQ static gives 95% of the benefit with 5% of the effort.
- **Is FP8 safe?** Yes on H100. 30-50% faster with under 0.1% quality loss.

title: Embeddings and Vector Search
subtitle: Encode text, pick a metric, size the vectors, choose an index and fix bad recall. Python, NumPy and FAISS.
markdown:
## Retrieve, then rerank
type: architecture
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/14-information-retrieval-search/docs/en.md

```arch
node | docs | 1,1 | Documents | split into chunks
node | enc | 2,1 | Bi-encoder | text to vector
node | norm | 3,1 | L2 normalize | unit length
node | idx | 4,1 | Vector index | HNSW or flat
node | q | 1,2 | Query | same model, query prefix
node | out | 2,2 | Top 10 | to the reader
node | rerank | 3,2 | Cross-encoder | scores pairs
node | topk | 4,2 | Top 100 | ANN search
edge | docs | enc | chunks
edge | q | enc | embed
edge | enc | norm |
edge | norm | idx | add
edge | idx | topk | search
edge | topk | rerank |
edge | rerank | out | top 10
```

## Encode, search, truncate
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/14-information-retrieval-search/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/06-knn-and-distances/docs/en.md

```python
encoder = SentenceTransformer("BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5")  # 384 dim
embeddings = encoder.encode(corpus, normalize_embeddings=True)  # unit vectors
q_emb = encoder.encode([query], normalize_embeddings=True)
sims = (embeddings @ q_emb.T).flatten()  # dot equals cosine
order = np.argsort(-sims)[:top_k]        # best first
def truncate(vectors, dim):              # Matryoshka cut
    out = vectors[:, :dim]
    return out / np.linalg.norm(out, axis=1, keepdims=True)  # renormalize
emb_256 = truncate(emb, 256)
index = faiss.IndexFlatL2(dimension)     # exact search
index.add(embeddings)
distances, indices = index.search(query_vectors, k=5)
```

## Tasks
type: task-table
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/code/main.py, phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/code/embeddings.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/03-word-embeddings-word2vec/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/04-glove-fasttext-subword/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Truncate one vector | `truncate_matryoshka(vec, 64)` |
| Binarize a vector | `binarize(vec)` |
| Search by Hamming distance | `engine.index.search(query_vec, top_k=5, metric="hamming")` |
| Fuse dense and sparse ranks | `rrf_fuse([dense_ranked[:5], sparse_scores[:5]])` |
| Load BGE-M3 | `BGEM3FlagModel("BAAI/bge-m3", use_fp16=True)` |
| Run an analogy | `analogy(vocab, W, "man", "king", "woman")` |
| Vector for an unseen word | `fasttext_vector(word, ngram_table)` |
| Evaluate on MTEB tasks | `evaluation.run(encoder, output_folder="./mteb-results")` |

## Similarity math
type: concepts
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/code/embeddings.py, phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/code/main.py

- **Cosine**: $\cos(a, b) = \frac{a \cdot b}{\lVert a \rVert \, \lVert b \rVert}$. Range -1 to 1. Ignores length.
- **Cosine distance**: $1 - \cos(a, b)$. Range 0 to 2.
- **Dot product**: $\sum_i a_i b_i$. Equals cosine on unit vectors.
- **L2**: $\sqrt{\sum_i (a_i - b_i)^2}$. Smaller is closer.
- **Unit vectors**: $\lVert a - b \rVert^2 = 2 - 2 \cos(a, b)$.
- **Hamming**: count of different bits after binarize.
- **MaxSim**: best doc token per query token, then sum.
- **RRF**: $\sum \frac{1}{k + \text{rank} + 1}$ over rankings, rank from 0.

## HNSW search
type: flow
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md

1. **Build**: put each vector in a multi-layer graph, linked to approximate neighbors.
2. **Top layers**: sparse, with long links between distant clusters.
3. **Bottom layer**: dense, holds all vectors with short links.
4. **Enter**: the query starts at the top layer.
5. **Descend**: greedy moves to closer nodes, then one layer down.
6. **Return**: approximate top-k in $O(\log n)$, not $O(n)$.
7. **Cost**: typically 95 to 99 percent recall. Milliseconds at 10 million vectors.

## Choose an index
type: command-table
from: phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/06-knn-and-distances/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `IndexFlatIP` | Exact inner product. Cosine on unit vectors. About 100k vectors |
| `IndexFlatL2` | Exact L2, no training. Up to about 1M vectors |
| `IndexIVFFlat` | K cells, searches the closest few. Needs training. About 10M |
| `IndexIVFPQ` | IVF plus product quantization. 100M and more |
| `IndexHNSW` | Graph index. Fastest for many queries. Large index |
| LSH | Random hash projections. Near-duplicate detection |
| KD-trees, ball trees | Exact. Low and medium dimension only |

## Size and compression
type: concepts
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md

- **float32, 1536 dim**: 6,144 bytes per vector. 61 GB for 10 million.
- **3,072 dim**: 12 KB per vector at full precision.
- **Binary**: 192 bytes per vector, 32x smaller. 5 to 10 percent recall loss.
- **Rescore**: binary first pass, then full precision on the top 1000.
- **Matryoshka 256 of 1536**: 6x less storage, about 3 to 5 percent loss.
- **Safe cut**: 1,536 to 256 is usually safe. 1,536 to 64 is not.

## Defaults in the code
type: defaults
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/code/embeddings.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/code/main.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/04-glove-fasttext-subword/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `chunk_size` | 200 | Words per chunk, `chunk_text` |
| `overlap` | 50 | Words shared by two chunks |
| `top_k` | 5 | Results per search |
| `metric` | `"cosine"` | Also dot, euclidean, hamming |
| RRF `k` | 60 | `rrf_fuse` |
| `hash_embed` dim | 256 | Hash trick demo embedder |
| `n_min` | 3 | FastText n-grams, `n_max` 6 |
| `x_max` | 100 | GloVe weighting, `alpha` 0.75 |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/03-word-embeddings-word2vec/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/04-glove-fasttext-subword/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| bge recall 3 to 5 points low | No query prefix | Prepend the prefix from the model card |
| Truncated vectors rank badly | No renormalize after the cut | Divide by the norm again |
| Recall falls after truncation | Cut too far, or no Matryoshka training | Validate on your eval set |
| Nearest neighbors change | Cosine and L2 conventions mixed | Match the training metric |
| Query and doc do not match | Asymmetric model | Check the model card |
| `cosine: dim mismatch` | Vectors of different size | One model and one dim for both |
| Long docs match nothing | One vector averages all topics | Chunk 256 to 512 tokens, 50 overlap |
| Unseen word has no vector | Word2Vec and GloVe have no fallback | Use FastText n-grams |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/03-word-embeddings-word2vec/docs/en.md

- **ANN**: Approximate Nearest Neighbor. Small accuracy loss, large speed gain.
- **HNSW**: Hierarchical Navigable Small World. Multi-layer graph index.
- **IVF**: Inverted file index. Searches a few clusters only.
- **PQ**: Product quantization. Search in compressed space.
- **LSH**: Locality-sensitive hashing. Random hash projections.
- **MTEB**: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark. 56 tasks at launch, 100+ in v2.
- **BEIR**: 18 zero-shot retrieval tasks.
- **OOV**: Out of vocabulary. A word not seen in training.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/65-hybrid-retrieval-bm25-dense/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/14-information-retrieval-search/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md

- **Cosine or dot product?** On L2-normalized vectors the choice does not matter.
- **Why ANN?** Brute force at 1M by 1536 is 1.5 billion multiply-adds per query.
- **Why rerank?** A cross-encoder reads query and doc together. It is slower but more accurate.
- **Why RRF, not a score sum?** BM25 is unbounded. Cosine is in -1 to 1. Ranks compare.
- **Which number for a RAG retriever?** Recall@k. No right passage, no answer.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/22-embedding-models-deep-dive/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/14-information-retrieval-search/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/04-embeddings/docs/en.md

- Always set `normalize_embeddings=True`.
- Benchmark on your own queries. Leaderboard rank is not enough.
- Swap a model only if it wins on your domain by more than 3 points.
- Report recall@1, @5 and @10 side by side.
- Measure p99 latency. MTEB scores hide it.
- For a failing query, diff the sparse and dense rankings.

title: Embodied VLAs and Computer-Use Agents
subtitle: Action formats for robots, GUI action schemas, safety gates and bounded agent loops for browsers and desktops.
markdown:
## Key terms
type: concepts
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/21-computer-use-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/docs/en.md

- **VLA**: one model takes image and instruction and outputs action commands.
- **Action tokenization**: quantize each joint target into 256 bins. Each bin is a vocab ID.
- **FAST**: DCT plus quantize. A 30-step trajectory becomes ~10 tokens.
- **Flow-matching head**: small transformer outputs a 50-step action sequence via rectified flow.
- **System 1 / System 2**: large VLM plans slowly. Small action head acts quickly.
- **GUI grounding**: model outputs (x, y) for the target of an instruction on a screenshot.
- **Hybrid agent**: uses screenshot and accessibility tree together.
- **Read/write boundary**: reading is never consequential. A write needs fresh approval.

## VLA action formats
type: comparison
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/code/main.py
span: 2

| Factor | RT-2 | OpenVLA | π0 | GR00T N1 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pattern | PaLM-X + discrete bin | Llama 7B + discrete bin | flow-matching head | dual-system humanoid |
| Action output | 10 tokens per step | 256 bins per dim | continuous 50-step sequence | subgoals, then joint commands |
| Rate | 3-5 Hz | 4-5 Hz on an A100 | effectively 50 Hz | ~1 Hz plan, 50-100 Hz act |
| Web to robot mix | ~1:1 | ~0.5:1 | similar | sim-to-real data |
| Weights | closed | open | open | open |

## Action tokenizers in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/code/main.py

```python
tokens = discretize(action, bins=256)          # [-1,1]^D to D integer bins
idx = int((a + 1) / 2 * (bins - 1))            # then clamp to 0..bins-1
recovered = undiscretize(tokens, bins=256)     # bin width = 2/255 ~ 0.0078
fast_tokens = fast_compress(trajectory, keep_coeff=4)  # per-dim DCT, bins=32
coeffs = dct(series)[:keep_coeff]              # keep low-frequency terms
continuous_flow_count = 1                      # single head output
```

## Multimodal agent loop
type: flow
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/code/main.py, phases/14-agent-engineering/21-computer-use-agents/docs/en.md

1. **Agent**: take a screenshot of the browser.
2. **VLM**: parse screenshot, URL and goal into a plan.
3. **VLM**: emit one structured JSON action per step.
4. **Safety**: assess each action before execution. Reject unsafe actions.
5. **Wrapper**: `apply_action(state, action)` returns the new state.
6. **Agent**: observe the next screenshot. Repeat until `done`.

type: task-table
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/docs/en.md

| Type text | `"type":  ["text", "x", "y"]` |
| Scroll | `"scroll": ["direction", "amount"]` |
| Drag | `"drag": ["x0", "y0", "x1", "y1"]` |
| Pick an option | `"select": ["option_index"]` |
| Go to a URL | `"navigate": ["url"]` |
| Crop and zoom | `"screenshot_region": ["x0", "y0", "x1", "y1"]` |
| End the task | `"done": ["success", "explanation"]` |

## Defaults and limits
type: defaults
from: projects/browser-agent/solution/main.ts, projects/browser-agent/solution/cli.ts, projects/desktop-control/solution/main.rs, projects/desktop-control/solution/cli.rs, projects/desktop-control/README.md

| Setting | Default | Note |

| `greenFraction` | 0.0005 | Above it the status is complete |
| `submitLabel` | Save request | Button must be unique, enabled, not dangerous |

## Errors and fixes
type: troubleshooting
from: projects/browser-agent/solution/main.ts, projects/browser-agent/API.md, projects/desktop-control/solution/main.rs, projects/desktop-control/README.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `origin changed` | Page URL left `allowedOrigin` | Keep the run on the allowed loopback origin |
| `missing or ambiguous field` | Label matches zero or two fields | Use exact unique labels |
| `completion values disagree` | done is true but a value differs | Do not trust the success banner |
| `unsafe or ambiguous submit` | Button is dangerous, disabled or not unique | Give one safe submit button |
| `stalled` | Observation repeats after an action | Check that the driver applies the action |
| `screenshot-error` | Capture or PNG check failed | CLI exits with status 2. Fix the image |
| `stale frame` | Click generation is not the last capture | Capture again and use its generation |
| `action budget exhausted` | Calls reached `max_calls` | Raise the budget or cut actions |

## Injection defenses
type: comparison
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/docs/en.md

| Page | naive | sanitizer | rw_boundary |
|---|---|---|---|
| Benign | posts ok | posts ok | posts ok |
| Visible-text injection | posts to /api/exfil | catches it | blocks the write |
| URL-fragment injection | posts to /api/exfil | misses it | blocks the write |
| Weak point | follows page text | does not inspect URLs | needs correct content origin |

## Numbers to know
type: concepts
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/21-computer-use-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/25-multimodal-agents-computer-use/docs/en.md

- **Control budget**: 30 Hz control loop means 33ms budget per action.
- **Open X-Embodiment**: 970k trajectories across 22 robots for OpenVLA.
- **Robot adaptation**: LoRA fine-tuning on 100-1000 task-specific demos.
- **OpenAI CUA at launch**: OSWorld 38.1%, WebArena 58.1%, WebVoyager 87%.
- **Gemini 2.5 Computer Use**: browser-only, 13 actions, ~70% Online-Mind2Web.
- **WebArena-Verified**: fixes ~11.3% false negatives. Hard subset has 258 tasks.
- **AgentVista**: frontier models 27-40%. Open models 10-20%.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/21-computer-use-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/docs/en.md

- **Why co-fine-tune?** Robot-only models fail on out-of-distribution instructions.
- **What counts as permission?** Only direct user instructions. Screenshots and DOM text are untrusted.
- **Can a filter fix prompt injection?** No. Defenses raise the cost. They do not close the class.

## Safety tips
type: tips
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/21-computer-use-agents/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/11-browser-agents/docs/en.md

- Put joint, velocity and workspace limits outside the VLA as control-layer checks.
- Run a per-step safety classifier before every action.
- Ask a human before login, purchase or file delete.
- Allow only the tools that the task needs.
- Run browser sessions with scoped credentials only.

title: Negotiation, Simulation and Agent Economies
subtitle: Contract Net, OG-Narrator bargaining, Smallville memory, Theory of Mind tests, Shapley credit and second-price auctions.
markdown:
## Contract Net task market
type: flow
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/code/main.py

1. **Manager**: decomposes the task into units.
2. **Manager**: broadcasts `cfp` with the task description to workers.
3. **Bidder**: returns a **propose** with `(price, eta, confidence)`, or a **refuse**.
4. **Manager**: keeps bids with price within budget and eta within the deadline.
5. **Manager**: picks the max of conf/price and sends **accept-proposal**.
6. **Manager**: sends **reject-proposal** to the losers. They bid on other tasks.

## Negotiation mechanisms
type: concepts
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md

- **OG-Narrator**: a deterministic offer generator computes the price. The LLM only narrates.
- **Offer generator**: Rubinstein bargaining, Zeuthen strategy or tit-for-tat over price.
- **Rule**: let the LLM narrate. Do not let the LLM compute the offer.
- **Structured proposal**: the LLM drafts it. Validate it against a schema before you send.
- **CoT concealment**: winners compute strategy privately. The public channel shows the offer only.
- **Persona manipulation**: a desperation persona gives about 20% more payoff.

## Bargaining in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/code/main.py

```python
state = BargainState(buyer_max=buyer_max, seller_min=seller_min)
og_narrator_bargain(state, rng, concession=0.35)  # buyer offer
seller_response(state, rng, concession=0.3)       # seller counter
move = max(1, int(concession * (state.seller_offer - prior)))
candidate = min(candidate, state.buyer_max)       # never past own max
naive_llm_bargain(state, rng)          # high variance, often outside ZOPA
bench_deal_rate(buyer_fn, label, trials=1000)     # deal rate in percent
winner = max(feasible, key=lambda b: b.confidence / max(b.price, 1))
```

## Generative agent loop
type: architecture
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/code/main.py

```arch
node | obs | 1,1 | Observation | invitation from a neighbor | client
node | stream | 2,1 | Memory stream | append-only log | store
node | retr | 3,1 | Retrieval | top-k by combined score | process
node | refl | 2,2 | Reflection | new belief back into the stream | model
node | plan | 3,2 | Plan | day, hour, action | model
node | act | 4,2 | Act | move to HobbsCafe | process
edge | obs | stream | observe
edge | stream | retr | score
edge | stream | refl | important memories
edge | refl | stream | reflection entry
edge | retr | plan | top-k
edge | plan | act | tick
```

## Memory retrieval
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/code/main.py

```python
top = retrieve_top_k(stream, query="party cafe", tick=4, k=3)
recency = math.exp(-0.3 * (tick - m.ts))     # exponential decay by age
importance = m.importance / 10.0              # self-rated 1 to 10
relevance = 0.6 if any(w in m.content.lower() for w in query.lower().split()) else 0.1
score = recency + importance + relevance  # sorted, keep [:k]
a.reflect(tick)          # importance >= 6 in the last 5 ticks
a.update_plan(tick)      # belief adds Plan(tick=5, where="HobbsCafe")
action = a.act(tick)     # move when the plan tick arrives
```

## Theory of Mind and coordination
type: concepts
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/18-theory-of-mind-coordination/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/18-theory-of-mind-coordination/code/main.py

- **Zeroth-order**: no model of others. The agent acts on its own observations only.
- **First-order**: a model of each other agent's beliefs. "Alice believes X."
- **Second-order**: recursive beliefs. "Alice believes that Bob believes X."
- **ToM state**: the `other_models` attribute. Keep it as `{agent_id: belief_list}`.
- **Riedl metrics**: identity-linked differentiation, goal-directed complementarity, higher-order synergy.
- **Real signals**: complementarity over time, anticipation and correction by turn T+2.
- **Demo**: `run_trial(n_agents, n_boxes, tom, seed, max_turns=10)` counts duplications.

## Economy mechanisms in code
type: task-table
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/code/main.py, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Exact Shapley, small N | `shapley_exact(value_fn, agents)` |
| Sampled Shapley | `shapley_sampled(value_fn, agents, samples, rng)` |
| Truthful auction | `second_price(bids)` |
| Winner pays | `payment = sorted_bids[1].value` |
| Reputation store | `Reputation(alpha=0.95, floor=0.1)` |
| Update after a task | `rep.update(agent, quality)` |
| Route by reputation | `weighted_choice(agents, rep.weights(agents), rng)` |

## Run the demos
type: command-table
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/18-theory-of-mind-coordination/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |

| `python3 code/main.py` in 16-17 | 3 of 5 agents converge at the party |
| `python3 code/main.py` in 16-18 | ToM duplicates ~5%, zeroth-order ~35% |
| `python3 code/main.py` in 16-21 | Rep routing gives 10-20% quality gain |

## Defaults in the lesson code
type: defaults
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/code/main.py, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/code/main.py, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/18-theory-of-mind-coordination/code/main.py, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |

| Buyer `concession` | 0.35 | Seller uses 0.3 |
| Bargain `trials` | 1000 | ToM bench uses 200 |
| Retrieval `k` | 3 | Top-k memories in the prompt |
| Reflection trigger | 150 | Sum of importance of unprocessed memories |
| `max_turns` | 10 | ToM token-collection budget |
| `alpha` | 0.95 | Reputation decay |
| `floor` | 0.1 | Lowest reputation score |

## Numbers to remember
type: concepts
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

- **OG-Narrator**: deal rate from 26.67% to 88.88%.
- **Competition**: ~180k negotiations. Concealing agents won.
- **Symmetric pairs**: inequitable outcomes on about 40% of scenarios.
- **Smallville**: 25 agents. 24 had no knowledge of the party.
- **Shapley cost**: N=3 has 6 permutations. N=10 has 3.6M.
- **Shapley sampling**: 100-1000 orderings.

## Failure modes
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/18-theory-of-mind-coordination/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Offers outside the ZOPA | LLM computes the price | Deterministic offer generator |
| Counterpart knows your limit | Reservation price in a visible trace | Separate private scratchpad |
| Agents enter closed stores | Spatial norm errors | Detect norm violations explicitly |
| Retrieval cost grows | Memory overflow | Summarize-and-prune, decay low importance |
| Invented relationships | Reflection hallucination | Put source memory ids in the prompt |
| Coordination only in demos | Prompt dressing, no control | Control condition and `p < 0.05` |
| Belief bound to wrong agent | Long horizon, context limits | Explicit or external ToM store |
| One operator inflates credit | Sybil attack | DIDs and reputation cost-to-forge |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

- **Does a larger model bargain better?** No. It writes better language with similar strategic error.
- **Why does Contract Net scale past 100 workers?** It is broadcast-and-respond, not synchronous chat.
- **Which Smallville part can you drop?** None. Each ablation hurts believability.
- **Why second-price?** Under monotone aggregation, agents bid their true value.
- **When do agent economies make sense?** Open networks, verifiable outputs, long-horizon work.

## Ship checklist
type: tips
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/16-negotiation-bargaining/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/17-generative-agents-simulation/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/21-agent-economies/docs/en.md

- Bound bargaining to 3-5 rounds. Escalate to a mediator on deadlock.
- Reject out-of-ZOPA offers at the protocol boundary.
- Memory is append-only. Corrections are new entries.
- Log the top-k memories that drove each action.
- Start with reputation, not tokens.
- Verify before you reward.

| Factor | Static benchmarks | Custom offline | Online |

| Examples | SWE-bench Verified, GAIA, BFCL V4 | LLM-as-judge, execution, trajectory | Session replays, guardrail alerts |

## Evaluator-optimizer loop
type: flow
from: phases/14-agent-engineering/30-eval-driven-agent-development/code/main.py, phases/14-agent-engineering/30-eval-driven-agent-development/docs/en.md

1. **Proposer**: `case.proposer(feedback)` gives a candidate.
2. **Judge**: `case.judge(candidate)` returns ok and a reason.
3. **Refine**: the reason becomes the next feedback.
4. **Stop**: after `max_rounds` the case fails.
5. **CI gate**: `ci_gate` blocks a regression above the threshold.

## Reviewer rubric
type: concepts
from: phases/14-agent-engineering/39-reviewer-agent/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/39-reviewer-agent/code/main.py

- **Scope discipline**: edits inside the contract?

- **Who overrides a block?** Only a human, with `override_reason` and `overridden_by`.

title: Bias, Fairness and Differential Privacy
subtitle: Measure bias, pick a fairness criterion, train with DP-SGD and audit the privacy claim. Stdlib Python toys.
markdown:
## Three fairness families side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/docs/en.md

| Factor | Group fairness | Individual fairness | Counterfactual fairness |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rule | Equal rates across protected groups | Similar individuals get similar decisions | Decision unchanged when sensitive attributes change |
| Source | Demographic parity, equalized odds, CUAE | Dwork et al. 2012 | Kusner et al. 2017 |
| Needs | Group labels and outcomes | A similarity metric d | A causal DAG |
| Formal test | Equal rates per group | Lipschitz constant L | Counterfactual alteration |
| Weak point | Criteria conflict under unequal base rates | Defining d is a policy question | Only as justified as the DAG |

## Use each criterion when
type: tips
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/docs/en.md

- Use demographic parity when the claim is equal acceptance rates.
- Use equalized odds when the claim is equal TPR and FPR across groups.
- Use conditional use accuracy equality when the claim is equal predictive value.
- Use individual fairness when you can define a task-specific metric d.
- Use counterfactual fairness when you have a causal DAG of the population.
- Use backtracking counterfactuals when the law forbids interventions on protected attributes.

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/code/main.py

- **Demographic parity**: P(Y=1 | A=a) = P(Y=1 | A=a') for all groups.
- **Equalized odds**: P(Y=1 | Y*=y, A=a) = P(Y=1 | Y*=y, A=a').
- **Conditional use accuracy**: P(Y*=y | Y=y, A=a) = P(Y*=y | Y=y, A=a').
- **Individual fairness**: |f(x) - f(x')| <= L * d(x, x')
- **(ε, δ)-DP**: $P(M(D) \in S) \le e^{\varepsilon} \cdot P(M(D') \in S) + \delta$
- **WEAT term**: s(w, X, Y) = mean cosine(w, X) - mean cosine(w, Y)
- **WEAT effect**: mean_a(s) - mean_b(s) over identity groups.

## DP-SGD recipe
type: flow
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/docs/en.md

1. **Sampler**: sample a mini-batch.
2. **Trainer**: compute per-example gradients.
3. **Clipper**: clip each per-example gradient to a threshold C.
4. **Noise**: sum the clipped gradients and add Gaussian noise with std $\sigma \cdot C$.
5. **Optimizer**: use the noisy sum to update parameters.
6. **Accountant**: track the privacy cost with Moments Accountant or Rényi DP accountant.

## Where bias is measured
type: architecture
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/docs/en.md

```arch
node | emb | 1,1 | Embedding-based | WEAT on pre-RLHF embeddings | model
node | prob | 2,1 | Probability-based | stereotype log-likelihood | model
node | gen | 3,1 | Generated-text-based | resume scoring, dialogue | process
node | rep | 2,2 | Representational harm | stereotypes, erasure |
node | alloc | 3,2 | Allocational harm | unequal material outcomes |
edge | emb | prob | representation
edge | prob | gen | behaviour
edge | gen | rep |
edge | gen | alloc |
```

## Toy WEAT probe
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/code/main.py

```python
A = ["he", "his", "man"]                      # identity group A
B = ["she", "her", "woman"]                   # identity group B
X = ["engineer", "programmer", "scientist"]   # tech / career
Y = ["nurse", "teacher", "caregiver"]         # care / family
pre = weat_score(A, B, X, Y)                  # positive: A closer to X
EMB = debias(EMB)                             # project out the gender direction
gender_dir = [1.0, -1.0, 0.0, 0.0]            # axis 1 minus axis 0
post = weat_score(A, B, X, Y)                 # drops, not to zero
```

## Group metrics and DP reweighting
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/code/main.py

```python
train_data = gen(1000)                        # A=0 base 0.3, A=1 base 0.6
test_data = gen(500)
baseline = train(train_data)                  # steps 200, lr 0.1
preds = predict(baseline, test_data)          # (pred, label, group)
demographic_parity(preds)                     # rate0, rate1
equalized_odds(preds)                         # (TPR, FPR) per group
conditional_use(preds)                        # (PPV, NPV) per group
dp_reweighted = train(train_data, sample_weights=weights)  # a=0 y=1: 2.0, a=1 y=1: 0.5
```

## DP-SGD toy
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/code/main.py

```python
grad_w = clip(grad_w, C)                      # scale to norm C
grad_b = max(-C, min(C, grad_b))              # clip the bias gradient
noise_b = random.gauss(0.0, sigma * C)        # noise std sigma * C
b -= lr * (grad_b + noise_b)                  # noisy update per example
for sigma in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 4.0):       # sweep the noise multiplier
    model = dp_sgd(train_data, epochs=epochs, lr=0.05, sigma=sigma, C=C)
    acc = accuracy(model, test_data)
eps = analytical_epsilon(max(sigma, 0.01), steps=epochs * len(train_data), delta=delta)
```

## Toy defaults
type: defaults
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Clip norm `C` | 1.0 | Lesson 22 toy |
| `delta` | 1e-5 | Default of `analytical_epsilon` |
| `epochs` | 10 | DP-SGD toy, 500 train rows |
| DP-SGD `lr` | 0.05 | Fixed in the sweep |
| `sigma` | 0.0 | Standard SGD, infinite epsilon |
| Published ε | [1, 10] | Illustrative, not a recommended default |
| Fairness `train` | `steps: int = 200` | `lr: float = 0.1` |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| WEAT effect does not drop to zero | Debiasing reduces but does not eliminate it | Add probability and generated-text metrics |
| Diverse portrayals, unequal decisions | Only representational harm measured | Measure allocational harm too |
| Gender eval passes, bias remains | Bias fires on (gender, race) pairs | Run intersectional tests |
| DP gap shrinks, EO and CUAE worsen | Unequal base rates | State the chosen criterion as policy |
| Canary MIA shows little leakage | Canaries are not "most extractable" data | Add training-data extraction tests |
| Outputs safe, individuals re-identified | Confidence scores leak | Do not expose, or truncate/quantize them |

## Call the toy code
type: task-table
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/code/main.py, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Score a WEAT probe | `weat_score(<identity_a>, <identity_b>, ...)` |
| Project out a bias direction | `debias(<emb>)` |
| Train with reweighting | `train(data, sample_weights=<w>)` |
| Demographic parity per group | `demographic_parity(preds)` |
| Equalized odds per group | `equalized_odds(preds)` |
| Clip one gradient | `clip(<g>, <C>)` |
| Train with DP-SGD | `dp_sgd(data, epochs, lr, sigma, C)` |
| Epsilon for a run | `analytical_epsilon(sigma, steps)` |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/21-fairness-criteria-group-individual-counterfactual/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/22-differential-privacy-for-llms/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/20-bias-representational-harm/docs/en.md

- **Can one model meet all three group criteria?** No. Unequal base rates prevent it (Chouldechova, KMR 2017).
- **Why backtracking counterfactuals?** They reason from actual features. They do not intervene on the attribute.
- **Why do MIA and extraction disagree?** They measure different things: inserted canaries vs "most extractable" data.
- **What does LoRA + DP-SGD protect?** The adapter. The base model is held fixed.
- **Why uncertainty in WinoIdentity?** Equal error with unequal uncertainty still changes allocation.

title: Feature Engineering and Pipelines
subtitle: Impute, scale, encode, select and ensemble inside one leak-free pipeline. Python from the lessons.
markdown:
## One pipeline for mixed columns
type: architecture
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md

```arch
node | raw | 1,1 | Training data | X_train only
node | num | 2,1 | numeric_pipe | median impute, scale
node | cat | 2,2 | categorical_pipe | most_frequent, one-hot
node | pre | 3,1 | ColumnTransformer | preprocess step
node | model | 4,1 | Model | GradientBoostingClassifier
node | pred | 4,2 | Prediction | transform, then predict
edge | raw | num | numeric cols
edge | raw | cat | categorical cols
edge | num | pre |
edge | cat | pre |
edge | pre | model | fit
edge | model | pred |
```

## Build it in sklearn
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md

```python
numeric_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="median")),
    ("scale", StandardScaler()),
])
categorical_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("impute", SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent")),
    ("encode", OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),  # unseen city gives zeros
])
preprocessor = ColumnTransformer([
    ("num", numeric_pipe, ["age", "income", "score"]),
    ("cat", categorical_pipe, ["city", "gender", "plan"]),
])
full_pipeline = Pipeline([("preprocess", preprocessor),
                          ("model", GradientBoostingClassifier())])
```

## What fit and predict do
type: flow
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/code/pipeline.py

1. **Split first**: `X_train, X_test = X[:800], X[800:]` before any fit.
2. **pipe.fit**: each transformer calls `fit_transform` on X_train.
3. **pipe.fit**: the last step calls `fit` on the transformed X_train.
4. **pipe.predict**: each transformer calls `transform`, not `fit_transform`.
5. **pipe.predict**: the model calls `predict` on the transformed X_test.
6. **Cross-validation**: each fold fits the preprocessor on its own training split.

## Transform and encode tasks
type: task-table
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/code/features.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Scale to [0, 1] | `min_max_scale(values)` |
| Mean 0, std 1 | `standardize(values)` |
| Compress right skew | `log_transform(values)` uses log(v + 1) |
| Equal-width bins | `bin_values(values, n_bins=5)` |
| Squares and pairs | `polynomial_features(row, degree=2)` |
| Smoothed target mean | `target_encode(feature_values, target_values, smoothing=10)` |
| Flag holes first | `add_missing_indicator(values)` |
| Text weights | `tfidf(documents)` returns vectors, vocab |

## Feature selection tasks
type: task-table
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/code/feature_selection.py, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Drop near-constant columns | `variance_threshold(X, threshold=0.01)` |
| Rank by MI | `mutual_information(X, y, n_bins=10)` |
| Prune by weight | `rfe(X, y, n_features_to_select=5)` |
| Zero weights with L1 | `l1_feature_selection(X, y, alpha=0.1)` |
| Split-gain importance | `tree_importance(X, y, n_trees=50)` |
| sklearn RFE | `RFE(LogisticRegression(), n_features_to_select=10)` |
| sklearn L1 | `SelectFromModel(Lasso(alpha=0.01))` |
| sklearn trees | `rf.feature_importances_` |

## Ensembles: use X when
type: command-table
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| Bagging / Random Forest | Cuts variance. Noisy data, many features |
| AdaBoost | Cuts bias. Clean data. Hurt by outliers |
| Gradient Boosting | Cuts bias. Tabular data. Easy to overfit |
| XGBoost / LightGBM | Both. Start here for production tabular ML |
| Stacking | Both. Last 1-2% accuracy. Use CV meta-features |
| Soft voting | Average probabilities of diverse models |

## Boosting loops
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/code/ensembles.py

```python
weights = np.full(n, 1 / n)                  # AdaBoost starts uniform
err = np.clip(err, 1e-10, 1 - 1e-10)         # weighted stump error
alpha = 0.5 * np.log((1 - err) / err)        # low error, high vote
weights *= np.exp(-alpha * y * pred)         # misses gain weight
weights /= weights.sum()
self.initial_pred = np.mean(y)               # gradient boosting start
residuals = y - current_pred                 # squared error gradient
current_pred += self.lr * update             # shrink each tree
```

## Defaults and numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/code/features.py, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/code/ensembles.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Target encoding `smoothing` | 10 | Pulls rare categories to the global mean |
| `remove_correlated` threshold | 0.9 | Drops the second column of a pair |
| `AdaBoostScratch` `n_estimators` | 50 | Decision stumps |
| `GradientBoostingScratch` | 100 | learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=3 |
| `BaggingClassifier` | 20 | n_estimators=20, max_depth=5 |
| Learning rate range | 0.01 to 0.3 | Smaller needs more trees |
| Bootstrap unique rows | 63.2% | 36.8% out-of-bag for validation |
| Forest split features | `sqrt(n_features)` | `n_features / 3` for regression |

## Pipeline failures
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Test score too high | Scaler fit before the split | Use Pipeline with `cross_val_score` |
| Train and serve outputs differ | Transforms outside the pipeline | One Pipeline object for both |
| Crash on a new city | Encoder never saw the value | `OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")` |
| Breaks on schema change | Hardcoded column names | Column name lists from config |
| Random ID ranks high | Tree importance cardinality bias | Check with permutation importance |
| Target encoding overfits | Encoded on test rows | Fit on train data only, smooth |
| Stacking leaks | Meta-features from fitted data | Generate them with cross-validation |

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md

- **TF-IDF**: $\frac{\text{count in doc}}{\text{words in doc}} \cdot \log \frac{\text{docs}}{\text{docs with word}}$
- **Mutual information**: $I(X; Y) = \sum_x \sum_y p(x, y) \log \frac{p(x, y)}{p(x) p(y)}$, zero when independent.
- **L1 loss**: prediction error plus $\alpha \sum \lvert w_i \rvert$. Higher alpha zeros more weights.
- **Majority vote**: 21 classifiers at 60% give about 74%. 101 give 84%.
- **RFE cost**: $N - \text{target}$ trainings. 500 features to 10 is 490 runs.
- **MI bins**: $\sqrt{n}$ bins or Sturges' rule $1 + \log_2 n$.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/08-feature-engineering/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/13-ml-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/18-feature-selection/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/11-ensemble-methods/docs/en.md

- **Why scale features?** K-Means, KNN and SVM use distance. Scaling makes all features count equally.
- **Why add a missing indicator?** The fact that data is missing can itself be informative.
- **Why MI and not correlation?** MI catches quadratic or periodic links. Correlation can read zero.
- **Why soft voting?** It uses confidence information. It is usually better than hard voting.
- **What makes a run reproducible?** Fixed seeds, pinned dependencies, versioned data and config files.
- **Which model first on tabular data?** LightGBM or XGBoost with default parameters.

## METR time horizon, step by step
type: flow
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/21-metr-external-evaluation/docs/en.md

1. **Suite**: collect tasks from minute-scale to hour-scale expert time.
2. **Run**: run the model on each task. Record success or failure.
3. **Fit**: fit a logistic curve of P(success) against log(expert time).
4. **Read**: the horizon is the expert time where P(success) = 0.5.
5. **Audit**: check eval-context gaming. It moves the observed horizon.
6. **Use**: treat it as an upper bound. Adjust down for your tasks and tooling.

type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/21-metr-external-evaluation/code/main.py

```python
p = sigmoid(w * math.log(t) + b)  # P(success) vs log expert time
w -= lr * dw / n  # gradient step, default lr 0.05
logit = math.log(p / (1 - p))
return math.exp((logit - b) / w)  # expert time at probability p
h50 = horizon_at(w, b, 0.50)  # METR headline, also 0.10 and 0.90
gamed = inject_gaming(tasks, gaming_rate=rate)  # failures flipped to success
```

title: GANs from DCGAN to StyleGAN
subtitle: Losses, DCGAN code, Pix2Pix, CycleGAN and StyleGAN. Defaults, failure signatures and fixes.
markdown:
## StyleGAN generator
type: architecture
from: phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md

```arch
node | z | 1,1 | z | N(0, I), 512 dims | store
node | map | 2,1 | Mapping network | 8-layer MLP | model
node | w | 3,1 | w in W | roughly disentangled | store
node | const | 1,2 | Learned constant | 4×4×512 | store
node | synth | 2,2 | Synthesis block | upsample, conv, AdaIN, noise | gpu
node | img | 3,2 | Image | 4 up to 1024 | client
node | noise | 1,3 | Per-layer noise | learned per-channel scale | process
edge | z | map |
edge | map | w |
edge | w | synth | AdaIN at every block
edge | const | synth |
edge | noise | synth |
edge | synth | img | resolution doubles
```

## One training step
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/code/main.py

1. **Sample**: draw a real batch and noise `z` from N(0, I).
2. **D step**: score real images against 1 and `G(z).detach()` against 0.
3. **G step**: make fresh fakes. Score `D(G(z))` against 1.
4. **Repeat**: one step of D, then one step of G, every batch.
5. **Probe**: every 100 steps, count samples per mode. Warn below 50.
6. **Inspect**: look at 64 samples at the end of every epoch.
7. **Equilibrium**: `p_G = p_data` and D outputs 0.5 everywhere.

## Losses and formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md

- **Minimax**: $\min_G \max_D \; \mathbb{E}_x[\log D(x)] + \mathbb{E}_z[\log(1 - D(G(z)))]$
- **D loss**: binary cross-entropy with real = 1 and fake = 0.
- **G loss**: $-\log D(G(z))$. This is the non-saturating form.
- **WGAN**: $\text{loss}_D = \mathbb{E}[D(\text{fake})] - \mathbb{E}[D(\text{real})]$, $\text{loss}_G = -\mathbb{E}[D(\text{fake})]$
- **Pix2Pix G**: $-\log D(x, G(x)) + \lambda \cdot \lVert y - G(x) \rVert_1$
- **Cycle**: $F(G(x)) \approx x$ and $G(F(y)) \approx y$.
- **AdaIN**: $y_{\text{scale}} \cdot \frac{x - \mathrm{mean}(x)}{\mathrm{std}(x)} + y_{\text{bias}}$
- **Truncation**: $w' = \hat{w} + \psi \cdot (w - \hat{w})$. $\psi < 1$ trades diversity for quality.

## DCGAN train_step
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md

```python
opt_d.zero_grad()
d_real = D(real)                    # logits, sigmoid only in the loss
d_fake = D(G(z).detach())           # no gradient flows into G
loss_d = (F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(d_real, torch.ones_like(d_real))
          + F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(d_fake, torch.zeros_like(d_fake)))
loss_d.backward()
opt_d.step()
opt_g.zero_grad()
d_fake = D(G(z))                    # second pass keeps the graph
loss_g = F.binary_cross_entropy_with_logits(d_fake, torch.ones_like(d_fake))
loss_g.backward()                   # non-saturating G loss
opt_g.step()
```

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/code/main.py, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Build the generator | `Generator(z_dim=64, img_channels=3, feat=32)` |
| Wrap a D conv in SN | `spectral_norm(c)` |
| Make the optimizers | `Adam(lr=2e-4, betas=(0.5, 0.999))` |
| Sample in eval mode | `sample(G, n=8, z_dim=z_dim, device=device)` |
| Count parameters | `sum(p.numel() for p in G.parameters())` |
| Condition G or D | `inp = z + one_hot(c, num_classes)` |
| Map z to w | `w = mapping(z, mapping_net)` |
| Truncate w | `w_bar[i] + psi * (w_test[i] - w_bar[i])` |

type: comparison

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| D loss low, G loss oscillates, variety drops | Mode collapse | Minibatch discrimination, spectral norm, labels |
| D accuracy ~100%, G loss huge and static | D wins | Smaller D, lower D learning rate, label smoothing |
| Both losses swing with no trend | Oscillation | TTUR or Wasserstein loss |
| D above 95% accuracy | D too strong | Cut D learning rate by 2-5x |
| One real mode never appears | G memorizes a mode | Noise on D inputs, or WGAN-GP |
| Output ignores the condition | Weak condition signal in D | Condition D early, projection D |
| Blurry Pix2Pix output | L1 weight too high | Anneal λ down once stable |
| Droplet artifacts | AdaIN zeroes the mean | Weight demodulation of StyleGAN2 |

## Terms
type: glossary
from: phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md

- **DCGAN**: strided convs, batch norm, ReLU in G, LeakyReLU in D.
- **WGAN-GP**: Wasserstein distance plus gradient penalty.
- **SN**: spectral norm. Bounds the Lipschitz constant of each D layer.
- **TTUR**: two-timescale update rule. Two learning rates.
- **cGAN**: conditional GAN. G(z, c) and D(x, c) both see the condition.
- **PatchGAN**: D outputs an N × N grid of per-patch scores.
- **AdaIN**: adaptive instance norm. Normalize, then scale and shift by w.
- **FID**: Fréchet Inception Distance. Lower is better.

## Use X when
type: tips
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/03-gans-generator-discriminator/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/01-generative-models-taxonomy-history/docs/en.md

- **GAN**: real-time generation under 10 ms, style transfer, image-to-image translation.
- **StyleGAN3**: photoreal human faces with a fixed pose.
- **Pix2Pix**: thousands of paired examples, a narrow task and fast inference.
- **CycleGAN**: image translation with no paired data.
- **Frozen mapping network**: domain adaptation from a few images.
- **Diffusion or flow matching**: anything multi-modal or open-ended.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/09-image-generation-gans/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/04-conditional-gans-pix2pix/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/05-stylegan/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/01-generative-models-taxonomy-history/docs/en.md

- **Why `G(z).detach()` in the D step?** It stops gradients into G during the D update.
- **Why the non-saturating loss?** Early on `D(G(z))` is near zero. The original G loss then has vanishing gradients.
- **Why switch to eval mode before sampling?** Batch norm then uses running stats.
- **Why does D see the pair (x, y)?** Without x, D cannot check consistency.
- **Why does StyleGAN still ship?** One forward pass. Under 10 ms for a 1024² face on a 4090.
- **Can a GAN give p(x)?** No. It is an implicit density model. It only samples.

type: flow

1. **`parseTrace`**: one JSON object per line. A bad line stops with its line number.

- **Which `invoke_agent` kind?** CLIENT for remote agent services. INTERNAL for in-process frameworks.

title: Evaluating Generative Models
subtitle: FID, CLIP score, CMMD, Elo, WER, MOS, SECS, EER and FAD. Code, sample sizes and the ways each number fails.
markdown:
## FID and CLIP score
type: architecture
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md

```arch
node | real | 1,1 | Real images | held-out set | store
node | gen | 1,2 | Generated images | 10k or more | store
node | inc | 2,1 | Inception-v3 | 2048-D features | model
node | gauss | 3,1 | Gaussian fit | mean and covariance | process
node | fid | 4,1 | FID | lower is better | client
node | prompt | 1,3 | Prompt | | client
node | clip | 2,3 | CLIP encoders | image and text | model
node | cos | 3,3 | Cosine | per image | process
node | score | 4,3 | CLIP score | higher is better | client
edge | real | inc |
edge | gen | inc |
edge | inc | gauss | two pools
edge | gauss | fid | Fréchet distance
edge | gen | clip |
edge | prompt | clip |
edge | clip | cos |
edge | cos | score | mean over 30k
```

## Production eval report
type: flow
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md

1. **Sample quality**: FID on 10-30k samples against a held-out real set.
2. **Adherence**: CLIP score or CMMD on the same samples against their prompts.
3. **Preference**: win rate in a blinded arena against the previous model.
4. **Failure audit**: flag 50 random outputs for hands, text and object count.
5. **Seeds**: run 3 seeds minimum. Report the std.
6. **Per PR**: FID and CLIP score on a 500-sample subset, about 30 min.
7. **Nightly**: full 10k FID, HPSv2 and Elo.

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md

- **FID**: $\lVert \mu_r - \mu_g \rVert^2 + \mathrm{Tr}(\Sigma_r + \Sigma_g - 2 (\Sigma_r \Sigma_g)^{0.5})$
- **CLIP score**: cosine of `CLIP_image(x_gen)` and `CLIP_text(prompt)`.
- **Elo expected**: $E_a = 1 / (1 + 10^{(r_b - r_a)/400})$
- **Elo update**: $r_a \leftarrow r_a + k (s_a - E_a)$. B moves by the same amount the other way.
- **WER**: $(S + D + I) / N$ after normalization. CER uses characters.
- **DER**: (FA + Miss + Confusion) / total speaker time.
- **EER**: the threshold where FAR equals FRR.
- **Show-o mask ratio**: $\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{2T}\right)$, from 1.0 at step 0 to 0 at step T.

## Image metrics in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/code/main.py

```python
mu_r = mean_vec(real_features)
mu_g = mean_vec(gen_features)
cov_r = covariance(real_features, mu_r)
mean_sq = sum((a - b) ** 2 for a, b in zip(mu_r, mu_g))
sqrt_prod = jacobi_sqrt(prod)                    # matrix square root
return mean_sq + trace(cov_r) + trace(cov_g) - 2 * trace(sqrt_prod)
score = clip_like(image, prompt)                 # cosine, higher is better
expected_a = 1 / (1 + 10 ** ((r_b - r_a) / 400))
actual_a = 1.0 if winner == "a" else 0.0
delta = k * (actual_a - expected_a)              # k=32
return r_a + delta, r_b - delta
```

## Audio metrics in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

```python
transform = Compose([ToLowerCase(), RemovePunctuation(), Strip()])
score = wer(truth="<ref>", hypothesis="<hyp>",
            truth_transform=transform, hypothesis_transform=transform)
sv = EncoderClassifier.from_hparams("speechbrain/spkrec-ecapa-voxceleb")
emb_ref = sv.encode_batch(load_wav("reference.wav"))
emb_clone = sv.encode_batch(load_wav("cloned.wav"))
secs = torch.nn.functional.cosine_similarity(emb_ref, emb_clone, dim=-1).item()
fad = FrechetAudioDistance()
score = fad.get_fad_score("generated_folder/", "reference_folder/")
```

## Metric functions
type: task-table
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/code/main.py, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/code/main.py, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Image FID | `fid(real_features, gen_features)` |
| Elo from a pair | `elo_update(r_a, r_b, winner, k=32)` |
| Word error rate | `wer(ref, hyp)` |
| Character error rate | `cer(ref, hyp)` |
| Equal error rate | `eer_from_scores(same, diff)` |
| FAD-shaped distance | `embedding_fad_like(real_embeds, fake_embeds)` |
| Multiple-choice accuracy | `mmau_accuracy(predictions, golds)` |
| TTS round-trip WER | `ttr_wer(tts_model, asr_model, texts)` |

## Image metrics side by side
type: comparison
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md
span: 2

| Factor | FID | CLIP score | CMMD | Human preference |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Measures | sample quality | prompt adherence | quality, subtle differences | overall preference |
| Features | Inception-v3, 2048-D | CLIP image and text | CLIP | humans or an LLM judge |
| Minimum | 10k vs held-out real | 30k | 5k | 200 blinded pairs |
| Weak spot | small N, domains far from ImageNet | weak composition, short prompts | not covered | judge variance, prompt choice |

## Sampling cost of unified models
type: comparison
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md

| Factor | Chameleon, Emu3 | Transfusion | Show-o |
|---|---|---|---|
| Decoding | autoregressive tokens | continuous diffusion | masked discrete diffusion |
| Steps | 1024-4096 passes | ~20 | ~16 |
| Each step | one token | full transformer pass | top-K tokens commit |

## Audio numbers to beat
type: concepts
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

- **WER**: below 5% is human parity on read speech.
- **UTMOS**: correlates ~0.9 with human MOS. F5-TTS 3.95, ground truth 4.08.
- **SECS**: above 0.75 is a recognizable clone.
- **CLAP**: above 0.3 is reasonable text-audio alignment.
- **EER**: ECAPA on VoxCeleb1-O gives 0.87%.
- **FAD**: MusicGen-small on MusicCaps 4.5. Lower is better.
- **MMAU-Pro**: random chance is 25% on 4-way.
- **Barge-in**: target below 150 ms.

## Defaults
type: defaults
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/code/main.py, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Elo `k` | 32 | `elo_update` |
| Elo start rating | 1000 | Both models |
| FID samples | 10k | Low-N FID is unreliable |
| CLIP score samples | 30k | Average to one scalar |
| Inception input | 299×299 | Match resolutions |
| MOS listeners | 20+ | 100+ samples per model |
| Show-o steps `T` | 8 | Cosine schedule |
| Keep ratio floor | 0.15 | `keep_ratio` per step |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Low FID from few samples | Small N underestimates covariance | Use N of 10k or more |
| FID meaningless on faces or art | Inception trained on ImageNet | Domain extractor, for example FD-DINO |
| FID shifts across resolutions | 299×299 resize | Compare at matched resolution |
| CLIP score up, images not better | "high quality, 4k, masterpiece" | Check binding and saturation |
| Elo is meaningless | Models saw the benchmark prompts | Use held-out prompt sets |
| 5% WER hides 30% on accents | Aggregate WER | Report by demographic slice |
| Bad UTMOS on cloned audio | Trained on clean speech | Use a domain MOS panel |
| FAD not comparable | Different reference sets | Same reference set for all models |

## Rules
type: tips
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md

- Normalize text before WER. Report the normalization rule.
- Report distributions. P50/P95/P99 for latency, per class, per category.
- Run one public benchmark and one in-house held-out set.
- Cache the real features once as a `.npz` file.
- Batch eval generation with `num_images_per_prompt=8`.
- Use three metrics that agree, plus a qualitative review.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/08-generative-ai/14-evaluation-fid-clip-score/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/17-audio-evaluation-metrics/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md

- **Why CMMD?** It uses CLIP features and MMD. It is less biased and has no Gaussian assumption.
- **High SECS, low MOS?** The timbre is right but the voice is unnatural.
- **EER or minDCF?** minDCF is more production-relevant. It weights cost at an operating point.
- **What does 10k SDXL samples cost?** About 11 hours on one L4 at one request at a time.
- **Why does Show-o inpaint for free?** Its training predicts masked tokens.

type: troubleshooting
from: phases/00-setup-and-tooling/11-linux-for-ai/docs/en.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/10-terminal-and-shell/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Permission denied" | Permission bits | `chmod +x` or `sudo` |
| Run dies when the laptop closes | The SSH session ends | Run it inside tmux |
| `sed -i 's/a/b/' file` fails on macOS | macOS sed needs `''` after `-i` | `sed -i '' 's/a/b/' file` |
| Bash script breaks | Windows `\r\n` line endings | Run `dos2unix` |

| `pbcopy` not found | Not available over SSH | Use `cat` or `less` |
| No CUDA in WSL2 | Linux driver in WSL | Install the Windows NVIDIA driver |
| Disk full | Models and datasets | `du -sh *`, then clear caches |

type: concepts
from: phases/00-setup-and-tooling/10-terminal-and-shell/code/shell_aliases.sh, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/10-terminal-and-shell/docs/en.md

- **`ae`, `uvvenv`**: activate `.venv`, or make one with uv and activate it.
- **`watchloss`, `taillog <pattern>`**: follow `logs/*.log` for a pattern.
- **`trainenv <name>`**: tmux session with `nvidia-smi` and `htop` panes.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/00-setup-and-tooling/10-terminal-and-shell/docs/en.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/11-linux-for-ai/docs/en.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/02-git-and-collaboration/docs/en.md

- **`&`, `nohup` or tmux?** `nohup` and tmux survive a closed terminal. Only tmux lets you reattach.
- **`rsync` or `scp`?** `rsync` for anything large. It resumes and sends changed bytes.
- **Why fork the course repo?** Only maintainers can push. Your fork is `origin`.
- **Rebase or submodules?** The course does not need them.
- **Run as root?** No. Use `sudo` only when needed.

type: tips
from: phases/00-setup-and-tooling/02-git-and-collaboration/docs/en.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/10-terminal-and-shell/docs/en.md, phases/00-setup-and-tooling/11-linux-for-ai/docs/en.md

- Add `*.pt`, `*.pth` and `*.safetensors` to `.gitignore`.
- Run `sudo apt update` before each install.
- Use tmux for anything longer than a few minutes.
- Double-check the path before `rm -rf`.
- macOS defaults to `~/.zshrc`. Most Linux servers use `~/.bashrc`.
