## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/73-perplexity-calibration/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/41-eval-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/27-llm-evaluation-frameworks/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/28-long-context-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/74-leaderboard-aggregation/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Perplexity below 1 | Adapter returns log p, not -log p | Negate. The function rejects it |
| Perplexity too good | Padding counted in the denominator | Count only non-pad tokens |
| Judge scores go missing | Bad JSON gives NaN, mean drops it | Catch it as an explicit failure |
| Judge rates its own model high | Self-evaluation adds 10-20% | Judge with a different model family |
| Pairwise judge picks the first | Position bias | Randomize order and run both |
| Mean 0.85, users complain | Mean hides 5% catastrophic failures | Inspect the bottom quantile |
| Passes NIAH, fails real docs | NIAH tests retrieval only | Add RULER or a multi-hop test |
| One task dominates the mean | Score in [0, 100] | Return fractions in [0, 1] |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/27-llm-evaluation-frameworks/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/73-perplexity-calibration/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/10-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/28-long-context-evaluation/docs/en.md

- **EM**: Exact Match. 1 or 0 per task after normalization.
- **ECE**: Expected Calibration Error. Gap between confidence and accuracy.
- **MMLU**: Massive Multitask Language Understanding. 15,908 questions, 57 subjects.
- **HumanEval**: 164 Python function-completion problems.
- **SWE-bench**: 2,294 GitHub issues from 12 Python repos.
- **NIAH**: Needle in a Haystack. Plant a fact in filler, ask for it.
- **MRCR**: Multi-Round Coreference Resolution. 8, 24 or 100 needles.
- **RAGAS**: Retrieval-Augmented Generation ASsessment. Four RAG metrics.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/10-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/27-eval-harness-fixture-tasks/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/74-leaderboard-aggregation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/27-llm-evaluation-frameworks/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/28-long-context-evaluation/docs/en.md

- **How many test cases?** At least 200 for a deploy decision. 500 or more for close systems.
- **Why report pass@1 too?** pass@k hides a model that is right once in twenty tries.
- **When is a difference real?** When the bootstrap interval of the paired difference excludes zero.
- **When can I trust a judge?** Spearman rho against human labels of 0.7 or more.
- **How long is the real context?** Reasoning-effective is often 25-50% of the advertised window.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/10-evaluation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/27-llm-evaluation-frameworks/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/49-lm-eval-harness/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/28-long-context-evaluation/docs/en.md

- Anchor each rubric score to observable behavior. Judge variance drops 30-40%.
- Freeze the judge model and its version.
- Pin task files by hash in the leaderboard.
- Diff predictions, not only scores. Use `--include-per-example`.
- Keep eval cases apart from prompt and training examples.
- Test needle depths 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1.0.

title: End-to-End LLM and Fine-Tuning Pipeline
subtitle: Plan, run and gate a hashed stage DAG. Head swap, SFT loss mask and DPO loss from the capstones, with defaults.
markdown:
## Commands
type: command-table
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/07-end-to-end-fine-tuning-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/07-end-to-end-fine-tuning-pipeline/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/code/main.py

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `python code/main.py plan` | Validates the manifest, prints DAG and gates |
| `python code/main.py run` | Runs stages, prints the manifest JSON |
| `python code/main.py gate` | Applies eval gates. Prints `SHIP` or `HOLD` |
| `python code/main.py` | Demo: plan, run, a passing and a failing gate |
| `./pipeline.sh config/llama3.3-8b-domainX.yaml` | Capstone 07: data to model card |
| `run_demo()` | Capstones 38 to 40. Exits zero on success |

## Twelve-stage DAG
type: architecture
span: 2
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/code/main.py

```arch
node | tok | 1,1 | 01-02 Tokenizer | vocab, merges | store
node | data | 2,1 | 03 Dataset | sharded | store
node | base | 3,1 | 04-05 Checkpoint | pre-train, scale | gpu
node | sft | 4,1 | 06 SFT model | checkpoint + recipe | gpu
node | ppo | 4,2 | 07 Reward + PPO | policy | gpu
node | dpo | 3,2 | 08 DPO | policy | gpu
node | cai | 2,2 | 09 CAI / GRPO | refined policy | gpu
node | eval | 1,2 | 10 Eval report | scores, diffs | process
node | quant | 2,3 | 11 Quantized | weights + delta | store
node | srv | 3,3 | 12 Server spec | endpoint | process
node | gate | 1,3 | Ship gate | SHIP or HOLD | client
edge | tok | data |
edge | data | base |
edge | base | sft |
edge | sft | ppo |
edge | sft | dpo |
edge | ppo | cai |
edge | dpo | cai |
edge | cai | eval |
edge | cai | quant |
edge | quant | srv |
edge | eval | gate |
edge | srv | gate |
```

## What the orchestrator does
type: flow
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/code/main.py

1. **Orchestrator**: resolves the DAG from the manifest.
2. **Orchestrator**: skips a stage if its output already exists at the correct hash.
3. **Stage**: runs. The orchestrator measures wall clock and cost.
4. **Orchestrator**: checks the output hash against the next stage input hash.
5. **CostTracker**: halts with `halted_over_budget` when total cost passes the budget.
6. **On failure**: writes a partial manifest and exits nonzero.

## Manifest and gates
type: annotated-code
lang: yaml
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md

```yaml
pipeline_version: 1.2.3
seed: 42
git_commit: a1b2c3d4
stages:
  01_tokenizer:
    input_hash: sha256:...  # output hash of the stage before
    output_hash: sha256:...  # input hash of the next stage
gates:
  mmlu:      >= baseline + 0.5   # no regression
  humaneval: >= baseline + 1.0
  safety_refusal_rate: <= 0.05
  kl_from_reference: <= 25.0  # KL budget gate
  cost_total_usd: <= 50000
```

## Gate defaults in main.py
type: defaults
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `mmlu` | 65.0 | op `>=` |
| `humaneval` | 40.0 | op `>=` |
| `truthfulqa` | 50.0 | op `>=` |
| `safety_refusal_rate` | 0.05 | op `<=` |
| `kl_from_reference` | 25.0 | op `<=` |
| `cost_total_usd` | 50000.0 | op `<=` |
| `budget_usd` | 50000.0 | Run halts above it |
| `seed` | 42 | In `Manifest` |

## The three capstones side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch

| Factor | 38 Classifier head swap | 39 Instruction SFT | 40 DPO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Builds | Body + mean pool + 2-class head | `TinyGPT` trained on response tokens | Policy against a frozen reference |
| Data | 800 SMS, 640 train, 160 test | 200 pairs, 160 train, 40 test | 12 (prompt, chosen, rejected) triples |
| Model | hidden 64, 4 heads, 2 blocks, max 32 | hidden 96, 2 blocks | hidden 64, 2 blocks |
| Train | 20 epochs head-only, 20 full | 20 epochs, lr 5e-4 | 30 epochs, beta 0.2, lr 1e-3 |
| Metric | Precision, recall, F1, confusion | Exact-match per category | Chosen minus rejected margin |
| Check | Head-only and full both report | Exact-match rises over epochs | Loss falls, margin grows |

## Key calls in the capstones
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Freeze the body for head-only training | `freeze_body(model)` |
| Pool hidden states with the mask | `mean_pool(h, mask)` |
| Pad a batch and mask labels with -100 | `sft_collate(batch)` |
| Causal loss on response tokens | `shifted_loss(logits, labels)` |
| Score a completion under a model | `sequence_log_prob(...)` |
| DPO loss and implicit reward margin | `dpo_loss(lp_w_pol, lp_l_pol, lp_w_ref, lp_l_ref, beta=cfg.beta)` |
| Start the policy from the reference | `policy.load_state_dict(reference.state_dict())` |

## DPO loss
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/code/main.py

```python
diff_w = logp_w_pol - logp_w_ref  # chosen log-ratio
diff_l = logp_l_pol - logp_l_ref  # rejected log-ratio
margin = diff_w - diff_l  # implicit reward difference
z = beta * margin
loss = -F.logsigmoid(z)  # numerically stable
for p in reference.parameters():
    p.requires_grad = False  # reference never trains
reference.eval()
```

## Capstone 07 log lines
type: command-table
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/07-end-to-end-fine-tuning-pipeline/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `280k accepted (seed=7)` | Data stage rows kept |
| `val loss 1.42 -> 1.03` | SFT, 3 epochs on 8xH100 |
| `1 epoch, beta=0.08, 4xH100` | DPO run |
| `GPTQ-INT4 4.6 GB, AWQ-INT4 4.8 GB` | Quant sizes |
| `EAGLE-3 acceptance 0.74` | Speculative decoding check |
| `p99 126ms @ bs=8` | Tail latency at batch 8 |
| `MMLU-Pro +3.2, MT-Bench-v2 +0.41` | Eval gain over base |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/07-end-to-end-fine-tuning-pipeline/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `HOLD: missing metric <metric>` | Eval report has no value | Add the metric to the eval stage |
| `input hash missing for stage` | Upstream artifact not in store | Re-run the upstream stage |
| `halted_over_budget` | Total cost above `budget_usd` | Fix the cost estimate at plan time |
| DPO model sent through the SFT path | Untyped artifacts | Typed artifacts and stage signatures |
| Model learns to predict the instruction | No loss mask | `-100` on instruction, pad, boundary |
| Full fine-tuning overfits 800 examples | Small data washes out the body | Train the head only |
| MMLU-Pro accuracy jumps | Contamination in training data | MinHash check, reject any overlap |
| DPO prefers short completions | Length bias | Divide log-prob by completion length |

## Rollback and tips
type: tips
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/docs/en.md

- Run `plan` first every time. It is free. `run` is expensive.
- Cheap to re-run: tokenizer, eval, quantization, inference server.
- Medium: SFT, DPO, CAI. Keep the base model.
- Expensive: pre-training. Use the last good checkpoint.
- A failure at stage 06 invalidates 06 to 12. At stage 11, only 11 and 12.
- Address artifacts by hash. A filename like `latest.pt` is a foot-gun.
- Pre-training FLOPs: 6 x params x tokens.

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/13-building-complete-llm-pipeline/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/40-dpo-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

- **Which two gates catch most disasters?** A regression gate and a KL budget gate.
- **Reproducible or deterministic?** Reproducible. Floats differ at the 1e-5 level.
- **Why does log Z(x) drop out of DPO?** It is the same for chosen and rejected.
- **Why greedy for exact-match?** Temperature makes the metric stochastic.

title: LLM Routing and AI Gateways Compared
subtitle: Pick a gateway, set aliases and fallback chains, route cheap or frontier, and hedge slow safe reads.
markdown:
## AI gateways side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/outputs/skill-gateway-picker.md

| Factor | LiteLLM | Portkey | Kong AI Gateway | Cloudflare / Vercel |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Code | MIT OSS, Python | Apache 2.0 OSS since March 2026 | Built on Kong Gateway | Managed, zero-ops |
| Overhead | 5-15 ms | 20-40 ms | 3-8 ms | 1-3 ms at the edge |
| Scale | Breaks at ~2000 RPS, 8 GB | Control plane | 228% faster than Portkey | Edge advantage |
| Rate limit | Token-bucket | Tiered | Sliding-window | Limited |
| Guardrails | Optional | Opinionated guardrails, PII redaction | Opinionated guardrails | Limited |
| Price | $0 for OSS | $49/mo production tier | $100/model/month, max 5 on Plus | Managed only |
| Best fit | Python, <500 RPS, dev | Regulated industries | Already on Kong, >1000 RPS | Edge JavaScript apps |

## Use X when
type: concepts
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/outputs/skill-gateway-picker.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/outputs/skill-routing-config-designer.md

- **LiteLLM**: you have an SRE team, want data sovereignty and stay below 500 RPS.
- **OpenRouter**: managed SaaS, 300+ providers, credits. You want no infra.
- **Portkey**: you need guardrails and compliance out of the box.
- **Kong AI Gateway**: you already run Kong and need more than 1000 RPS.
- **Cloudflare / Vercel**: you serve JavaScript at the edge and need zero ops.
- **Self-host**: data residency forces it. Healthcare and finance default to self-host.
- **No gateway**: a single-model prototype. Direct API calls are simpler.

## Routing patterns
type: comparison
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/code/main.py

| Factor | Pre-route | Cascade | Ensemble |
|---|---|---|---|
| How | Classifier up front | Cheap first, escalate | Cheap and frontier in parallel |
| Latency | ~5-10ms added, fastest | ~1.2x median, ~2x escalated | Parallel runs |
| Quality | Depends on classifier | Best quality floor | Highest |
| Cost | Cheap for simple only | Cheap plus frontier on escalation | Highest cost |
| Use when | Classifier is accurate | Quality floor matters | Critical A/B only |

## Gateway request path
type: architecture
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/code/main.ts

```arch
node | client | 1,1 | Client | presented API key | client
node | auth | 2,1 | AuthService | 401 invalid api key | process
node | limit | 3,1 | TokenBucketLimiter | 429 rate limit exceeded | process
node | fb | 3,2 | callWithFallback | chain in order | process
node | retry | 2,2 | callWithRetry | backoff on retryable | process
node | prov | 1,2 | Providers | openai, anthropic, self-hosted | model
edge | client | auth | handle
edge | auth | limit | tenant
edge | limit | fb | allowed
edge | fb | retry | each provider
edge | retry | prov | call
```

## One request: route()
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/code/main.py

1. **redact_pii**: SSN and 16-digit card patterns become `[REDACTED]`.
2. **route**: `ROUTES.get(alias, [alias])` gives the fallback chain.
3. **provider_call**: a model in `OUTAGE` raises a simulated 5xx.
4. **route**: on `RuntimeError` it tries the next model in the chain.
5. **Cost**: `prompt_tokens` times `in_rate` plus `completion_tokens` times `out_rate`, over `1_000_000`.
6. **route**: when every model fails, `error` is "all providers failed".

## Alias routing gateway in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/code/main.py

```python
ROUTES = {"smart": [...], "fast": [...]}  # alias to fallback chain
PRICES = {"openai/gpt-4o": (5.0, 15.0)}   # per 1M tokens, in and out
inv = route("smart", [{"role": "user", "content": "<prompt>"}])
inv.chosen_model                          # first model that answered
inv.attempts                              # every model tried, in order
inv.input_tokens, inv.output_tokens       # from usage
inv.cost_usd                              # tokens times PRICES
inv.redacted                              # True when PII matched
inv.error                                 # "all providers failed"
OUTAGE.add("openai/gpt-4o")               # simulate a primary outage
```

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/code/main.ts, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/code/main.ts, projects/hedged-request-lab/solution/main.go

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Route an alias | `route(alias, messages)` |
| Scrub PII before dispatch | `redact_pii(text)` |
| Compare routing patterns | `simulate("CASCADE", reqs)` |
| Pick a model by policy | `router.pick(c.signals, c.policy)` |
| Gateway fallback simulator | `simulate_fallback(gateway, n=1000, seed=7)` |
| Retry one provider | `callWithRetry(provider, prompt, cfg)` |
| Try providers in order | `callWithFallback(chain, prompt, cfg)` |
| Hedge a safe read | `Hedged(ctx, client, endpoints, delay)` |

## Run the labs
type: command-table
span: 2
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/code/main.py, projects/hedged-request-lab/README.md, projects/hedged-request-lab/solution/main.go

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `python code/main.py` | Routing gateway: normal, outage, PII and all-down scenarios |
| `python3 scripts/project_test.py hedged-request-lab --init <dir>` | Creates a work folder. The starter fails until you implement it |
| `python3 scripts/project_test.py hedged-request-lab --stage 1 --path <dir> --strict` | Grades one stage |
| `python3 scripts/project_test.py hedged-request-lab --all --solution --strict` | Grades the reference solution |
| `go run . --samples 3 --delay-ms 10 --out /tmp/hedge-report.json` | In `solution`: baseline against hedged on loopback |
| `go run . --primary <url> --secondary <url>` | Hedges your own two safe read endpoints |
| `python3 scripts/project_test.py hedged-request-lab --all --path <dir> --strict --report <file>` | Writes the completion evidence |

## Defaults and limits
type: defaults
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/code/main.ts, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/code/main.ts, projects/hedged-request-lab/README.md, projects/hedged-request-lab/solution/main.go

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `hardSetThreshold` | 0.88 | At or above it, the router pins frontier |
| `maxAttempts` | 2 | Demo retry budget per provider |
| Free tier bucket | `capacity: 2` | `refillPerSec: 0.5`, third call gets 429 |
| `--delay-ms` | 10 | Hedge delay, allowed 0 to 1s |
| `--samples` | 3 | Samples per policy, 1 to 100 |
| `--out` | `/tmp/aiefs-hedge-report.json` | Receipt file |
| GET attempts | 2 | Body 64KiB, two-second ceiling, 100ms grace |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/outputs/skill-gateway-picker.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/outputs/skill-routing-config-designer.md, projects/hedged-request-lab/README.md, projects/hedged-request-lab/project.json, projects/hedged-request-lab/solution/main.go

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Cascading failures near 2000 RPS | LiteLLM at its ceiling | Migrate to Kong first |
| TTFT P99 over a 100 ms SLA | Portkey adds 20-40 ms | Use Kong or Cloudflare |
| Escalation rate over 30% | Cheap model is over-routed | Route less traffic to the cheap model |
| Quality drops with no alarm | Cheap-model drift | Gate routes by online quality metrics |
| Outage takes the alias down | Chain has one provider | Add a second failure domain |
| Fallback cascades raise cost | Retries without a budget | Count retries against a budget |
| A fast error wins the hedge | Winner not validated | Require HTTP 200 and nonempty `value` |
| Cancel shows no saved work | Server keeps working | Read `fixtureWork` counts |

## Numbers and questions
type: qa
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/16-model-routing/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/19-ai-gateways/outputs/skill-gateway-picker.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/21-llm-routing-layer/outputs/skill-routing-config-designer.md

- **What does fallback buy?** One provider at 3% error gives 97%. Two give 99.94%. Three give 99.997%.
- **What does routing save?** 20-60% at iso-quality in case studies.
- **What does a 70/30 split do?** The bill drops ~65% at the same product quality.
- **What does semantic caching save?** 30 to 60 percent on repeated agent loops.
- **Which online gates catch drift?** Thumbs per route, LLM-judge on a 5% sample, escalation and refusal rate.
- **Which metric to alert on first?** Fallback-use rate, then gateway latency P99.

type: flow
from: projects/subtitle-localization-desk/API.md, projects/subtitle-localization-desk/solution/main.py, projects/subtitle-localization-desk/solution/cli.py

1. **parse_vtt**: reads WebVTT into cues. It keeps timestamp strings and gives `cue-N` to cues with no id.

## Glossary publisher rules
type: concepts
from: projects/glossary-hovercard-publisher/solution/main.ts, projects/glossary-hovercard-publisher/README.md

- **Term id**: lower case, matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, and is unique.
- **Phrases**: a term or alias must not repeat across the glossary, in any case.
- **Matching**: `matchTerms()` tries the longest phrase first and needs word boundaries.
- **Skipped text**: text inside `pre`, `code` and `a` stays untouched.
- **Attributes**: only `class`, `id`, `title`, `lang` and `href` on `a`.
- **Links**: `href` must start with `https://`, `http://` or `#`.
- **Definition**: a native button with `aria-expanded` shows a `role="note"` span.

type: troubleshooting
from: projects/subtitle-localization-desk/solution/main.py, projects/subtitle-localization-desk/solution/cli.py, projects/ui-string-localization-workbench/solution/main.ts, projects/glossary-hovercard-publisher/solution/main.ts

| `resolve glossary or acknowledge reading-budget overflow` | Approved cue misses a term or the budget | Add the term or set `override_budget` to true |
| `STYLE and REGION are outside the supported subset` | VTT has STYLE or REGION blocks | Remove them. NOTE blocks are ignored |
| `Placeholder multiset changed` | Translation drops or adds a `{name}` | Keep every placeholder of the source |
| `Stale or invalid translation decision` | Review translation differs from the proposal | Download a new `locale-review.json` |
| `Resolve translation issues or context before approving` | Ambiguous key not acknowledged | Set `acknowledgeContext` to true |
| `Ambiguous repeated phrase` | Same phrase in two terms | Give each phrase one term |
| `Unsupported HTML element` | Tag outside the allowed subset | Use the listed tags only |

type: qa
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/18-multilingual-nlp/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/18-multilingual-nlp/code/main.py

- **Is English always the best source?** No. Language similarity predicts transfer better than corpus size.
- **Marathi target?** `rank_source_languages()` puts Hindi above English.
- **How many target labels?** 100 to 500 examples give 95 to 98 percent of the English baseline.
- **Why not a higher learning rate?** The multilingual alignment collapses to an English-only model.
- **What is the fertility tax?** Hindi can need 3 to 5 times the tokens of English.

type: tips
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/18-multilingual-nlp/docs/en.md, projects/subtitle-localization-desk/README.md, projects/ui-string-localization-workbench/README.md, projects/glossary-hovercard-publisher/README.md

- Report accuracy per language. An aggregate hides the long tail.
- Check tokenization fertility on target text before you train.
- Every translation needs a human review. The tools only flag problems.
- The UI workbench supports simple named placeholders, not ICU messages.
- Glossary phrases never cross elements or entity boundaries.
- The HTML runs locally and sends no data to a third-party service.

title: Fine-Tuning with LoRA
subtitle: Add LoRA adapters, load a 4-bit base for QLoRA, mask SFT labels, train, merge and debug. PyTorch, PEFT and bitsandbytes.
markdown:
## Tasks
type: task-table
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Add LoRA to a model | `model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)` |
| Show trainable share | `model.print_trainable_parameters()` |
| Load the base in 4-bit | `BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4")` |
| Count trainable params | `count_parameters(model)` |
| Save the adapter only | `model.save_pretrained("./lora-adapter")` |
| Merge the adapter into W | `merge_lora_weights(model)` |
| Skip masked labels in the loss | `F.cross_entropy(..., ignore_index=ignore_index)` |
| Head-only training | `freeze_body(model)` |

## LoRA path in one layer
type: architecture
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md

```arch
node | x | 1,1 | Input x |
node | w | 2,1 | Frozen W | out x in
node | a | 2,2 | A | r x in, Gaussian init
node | b | 3,2 | B | out x r, zero init
node | s | 4,2 | Scale | alpha / r
node | add | 4,1 | Add | Wx + scaled BAx
node | y | 5,1 | Output y |
node | m | 5,2 | Merged W' | W + (alpha/r) BA
edge | x | w |
edge | x | a |
edge | a | b |
edge | b | s |
edge | w | add |
edge | s | add |
edge | add | y |
edge | s | m | merge
```

## LoRA from scratch
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/code/lora.py

```python
class LoRALayer(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, in_features, out_features, rank=8, alpha=16):
        super().__init__()
        self.scaling = alpha / rank  # alpha / r
        self.A = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(in_features, rank) * (1 / math.sqrt(rank)))
        self.B = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(rank, out_features))  # BA starts at zero
    def forward(self, x):
        return (x @ self.A @ self.B) * self.scaling  # scaled low-rank update

class LinearWithLoRA(nn.Module):
    # __init__ wraps linear and builds self.lora
        for param in self.linear.parameters():
            param.requires_grad = False  # freeze W
    def forward(self, x):
        return self.linear(x) + self.lora(x)  # Wx + scaled BAx
```

## QLoRA with PEFT
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md

```python
bnb_config = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True,  # 4-bit base
    bnb_4bit_quant_type="nf4",  # NF4 levels
    bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
    bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True)  # quantize the scales too
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("<model>",
    quantization_config=bnb_config, device_map="auto")
lora_config = LoraConfig(task_type=TaskType.CAUSAL_LM, r=16,
    lora_alpha=32, lora_dropout=0.05,
    target_modules=["q_proj", "v_proj"])  # query and value
model = get_peft_model(model, lora_config)  # adds A and B
model.save_pretrained("./lora-adapter")  # 10-100MB adapter
```

## One SFT training step
type: flow
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/code/main.py

1. **Template**: each pair becomes `<INST> instruction <RESP> response`.
2. **Tokenize**: byte ids plus `INST_ID = 256`, `RESP_ID = 257`, `PAD_ID = 258`.
3. **Collate**: `sft_collate` pads each batch to its longest sequence.
4. **Mask**: labels get `-100` on instruction, padding and the boundary.
5. **Forward**: the model sees the full sequence, instruction included.
6. **Loss**: `shifted_loss` predicts position i+1 with `ignore_index=-100`.
7. **Step**: Adam updates the body. Exact-match runs every fifth epoch.

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/06-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

- **LoRA forward**: $y = Wx + BAx$ with $W$ frozen.
- **Scaled update**: $y = Wx + \frac{\alpha}{r} \cdot BAx$
- **Parameter count**: rank $r$ trains $2 \cdot r \cdot d$ parameters instead of $d^2$.
- **Example**: $r=16$ on 4096x4096 trains 131,072 of 16,777,216. That is 0.78%.
- **Merge**: $W' = W + (\alpha/r) \cdot BA$. Same size, no inference overhead.
- **Full fine-tune memory**: 8B in fp16 is about 56GB with gradients and Adam states.

## Defaults
type: defaults
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/skill-fine-tuning-guide.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/prompt-lora-advisor.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/06-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| r | 16 | safe start for most tasks |
| lora_alpha | 32 | 2 x rank, alpha = rank is conservative |
| lora_dropout | 0.05 | 0.1 below 5K examples |
| target_modules | q_proj, v_proj | add more only if quality is low |
| QLoRA learning rate | 2e-4 | higher than full fine-tuning |
| LoRA fp16 learning rate | 5e-5 | lower than QLoRA |
| Full SFT learning rate | 2e-5 | Llama 2 Chat, 15x below pre-training |
| Epochs | 1-3 | more risks overfitting |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/skill-fine-tuning-guide.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/06-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| NaN losses with Llama models | pad token not set | set the pad token |
| Loss does not decrease | learning rate too low for LoRA | try 2e-4 |
| Loss falls, eval quality bad | overfitting | fewer epochs, more dropout, more data |
| Weak on complex tasks | rank too low or wrong targets | try r=32 or add MLP layers |
| General skills drop after SFT | learning rate too high | use 1e-5 to 5e-5 and 1-3 epochs |
| Model predicts the instruction | no loss mask | set `-100` on instruction and padding |
| OOM on long sequences | optimizer states exceed GPU memory | use `optim="paged_adamw_8bit"` |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/06-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

- **LoRA**: Low-Rank Adaptation. Freeze W, train A and B.
- **QLoRA**: Quantized LoRA. 4-bit NF4 base, fp16 adapters.
- **NF4**: Normal Float 4. 16 levels at normal quantiles.
- **PEFT**: Hugging Face library for LoRA, QLoRA, DoRA and IA3.
- **TRL**: Hugging Face trainers for SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO and ORPO.
- **SFT**: Supervised Fine-Tuning on instruction and response pairs.
- **ChatML**: role format with `<|im_start|>` and `<|im_end|>` tokens.
- **Double quantization**: quantizes the per-block scales to fp8.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/39-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/skill-fine-tuning-guide.md

- **Why is B zero at init?** BA starts at zero. Training starts from the original behavior.
- **What does alpha do?** It scales the update by alpha / r, apart from the base learning rate.
- **Merge or keep separate?** Keep separate to serve many tasks. Merge for one model.
- **Why mask the instruction?** Unmasked, the model learns to predict the instruction and the response signal gets smaller.
- **When not to fine-tune?** When a prompt works, when you need facts (use RAG) or below 500 examples.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/skill-fine-tuning-guide.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/38-classifier-finetuning/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/06-instruction-tuning-sft/docs/en.md

- Try prompt engineering first, then RAG, then fine-tuning.
- Evaluate every 100 steps on a held-out set. Keep the best checkpoint.
- Compare base plus prompt against base plus LoRA on 200+ held-out examples.
- On 800 examples, train the head only with a frozen body.
- Track raw text loss. A rise above 10-15% means SFT is too aggressive.

## Choose a method
type: command-table
from: phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/outputs/prompt-lora-advisor.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/08-fine-tuning-lora/docs/en.md

| Choice | Use when |
|---|---|
| Full fine-tune, about 56GB for 7B | VRAM >= 2x model size in fp16 |
| LoRA on fp16 base, about 18GB | VRAM >= model size in fp16 |
| QLoRA on 4-bit base, about 6GB | VRAM >= model size / 4 |
| `r=16` | multi-domain tasks, instruction following, chat |
| `r=32` | code generation, complex reasoning, math |

## Use a hyperscaler when
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/01-managed-llm-platforms

- **Bedrock**: you need Claude, Llama and others behind one API and one IAM surface.
- **Bedrock**: you need cost per team, product or feature with no post-processing.
- **Azure OpenAI**: you need GPT models and TTFT P99 under 100 ms on PTUs.
- **Vertex AI**: you need 1M-token Gemini context or multimodal input.
- **Two providers**: every product-critical call runs on two hyperscalers.
- **Common pair**: Claude from Bedrock, GPT from Azure OpenAI, one gateway.

## Use a platform or self-host when
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/02-inference-platform-economics, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection

- **Custom silicon**: latency is critical. Groq is the pick for voice agents.
- **Fireworks**: you need low latency and LoRA at the base model rate.
- **Together**: you need new open models within days of release.
- **Baseten**: you need a fine-tuned model, dedicated GPUs, SOC 2 and HIPAA.
- **Modal**: your team writes Python and wants per-second billing.
- **Replicate**: you serve image, video and audio models per prediction.
- **Anyscale**: inference is one node in a larger Ray graph.
- **Self-host**: data residency, custom fine-tune, cost at scale or no hosted model.

## Pick a self-hosted engine
type: flow
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection

1. **Hardware CPU**: use llama.cpp. No other engine is competitive on CPU.
2. **Hardware AMD**: use vLLM with ROCm. TRT-LLM is NVIDIA-locked.
3. **Hardware Blackwell**: TRT-LLM leads on B200/GB200. vLLM and SGLang follow.
4. **Scale 1 user**: use Ollama. One command, first token in seconds.
5. **Scale 10-100 users**: use vLLM on a single GPU.
6. **Scale 100-10k users**: use vLLM production-stack or SGLang.
7. **Workload agentic or prefix heavy**: use SGLang RadixAttention.
8. **Pipeline**: dev Ollama, staging llama.cpp, prod vLLM. Convert GGUF to safetensors.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/01-managed-llm-platforms, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/10-cold-start-mitigation, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| P99 TTFT misses 100 ms on-demand | Shared capacity competes with other traffic | Buy PTUs or Provisioned Throughput |
| PTU bill high at low traffic | You pay for the reservation when idle | Reserve only at ~40-60% sustained utilization |
| Bedrock bill up 4x, same traffic | No per-feature attribution | Route calls through Application Inference Profiles |
| No per-request cost on Azure | Tags come from resource groups | Application Insights custom metrics or gateway headers |
| Product down in a provider outage | Single-vendor lock-in | Two-provider minimum behind one gateway |
| First token takes 3-8 minutes | Raw 70B cold start after scale to zero | Stack pre-seeded image, streamer, snapshot |
| Snapshot restore fails on new node | Snapshots are per GPU topology | Re-checkpoint on the new SKU |
| New project picks TGI | Maintenance mode since Dec 11, 2025 | Default to vLLM or SGLang |

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/01-managed-llm-platforms, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/02-inference-platform-economics, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/10-cold-start-mitigation, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection

- **Why is Bedrock ~25 ms slower?** Shared on-demand capacity. Azure PTUs reserve GPUs for your tenant.
- **When does per-minute beat per-token?** The docs say above ~30% sustained utilization. `main.py` says ~60-70% under reserved-minute billing.
- **When is a warm pool mandatory?** Typically at TTFT P99 < 60s on a 70B+ model.
- **What does a warm pool cost?** Five products with one warm replica use 3,600 GPU-hours/month.
- **Why does live migration move tokens?** Input is KB. KV cache is GB. Recompute is cheaper.
- **Why not Ollama in production?** 15-30% slower than llama.cpp, 3x gap under prod load.

## Glossary
type: glossary

subtitle: CTDE, value decomposition, self-play, domain randomization and VLA action formats. Formulas, numbers and fixes.

## Core ideas and formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/20-marl-maddpg-qmix-mappo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md

- **Markov game**: $(S, A_1, \ldots, A_n, P, R_1, \ldots, R_n)$. Each agent has its own reward.
- **Reward types**: identical is cooperative, zero-sum is adversarial, mixed is general-sum.
- **Non-stationarity**: $P(s' \mid s, a_i)$ depends on $\pi_{-i}$, and $\pi_{-i}$ changes.
- **CTDE**: critic $Q(s, a_1, \ldots, a_n)$ in training. Policy $\pi_i$ reads only $o_i$.
- **QMIX**: $Q_{\text{tot}} = f(Q_1, \ldots, Q_n)$ with $\partial f / \partial Q_i \ge 0$.
- **COMA**: advantage is my Q minus the expected Q over my own action.
- **Reality gap**: the shift between sim and real physics or sensing.
- **Control budget**: a 30 Hz loop gives 33ms for each action.

## MADDPG, QMIX, MAPPO
type: comparison
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/20-marl-maddpg-qmix-mappo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md

| Factor | MADDPG | QMIX | MAPPO |
|---|---|---|---|
| Year | 2017 | 2018 | 2022 |
| Idea | Per-agent critic sees all obs and actions | Monotonic mix of per-agent Qs | PPO with a centralized value function |
| Setting | Cooperative, competitive, mixed | Cooperative only | Cooperative |
| Testbed | Particle World | SMAC | Particle-world, SMAC, Football, Hanabi, MPE |
| Learning | Off-policy, DDPG | Value decomposition | On-policy, PPO |
| Key trait | Critic grows with N, ~10 agents | Monotonic constraint is strict | Stable, minimal tuning |
| Status | Introduced CTDE | Dominant on SMAC | Default cooperative baseline |

## CTDE: train central, act local
type: architecture

```arch
node | o2 | 1,2 | Agent 2 obs | local only | client
node | act1 | 2,1 | Actor 1 | maps own obs to action | model
node | act2 | 2,2 | Actor 2 | maps own obs to action | model
node | env | 3,1 | Environment | joint action, shared reward
node | critic | 3,2 | Centralized critic | all obs and actions, training only | process

edge | o2 | act2 |
```

## Sim-to-real recipe (quadruped)
type: flow
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md

1. **Sim**: massively parallel sim, with randomized gravity, friction, motor gains and payload.
2. **Teacher**: train with privileged info, terrain map and true body velocity.
3. **Student**: distill from the teacher with proprioception only.
4. **Adapt**: optional observation adaptation with an autoencoder on real IMU.
5. **Deploy**: zero-shot on 10+ environments.
6. **Fallback**: minutes of real fine-tuning with safety-constrained PPO.

## Independent against joint Q
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/code/main.py

```python
a1 = epsilon_greedy(Q1, s, rng, epsilon)       # each agent picks alone
a2 = epsilon_greedy(Q2, s, rng, epsilon)
s_next, r, done = step(s, (a1, a2))            # joint step, shared reward
target1 = r + gamma * max(Q1[s_next].values())
Q1[s][a1] += alpha * (target1 - Q1[s][a1])     # own Q table
reward = 10.0 if done else -1.0                # +10 when both arrive

ja = max(joint_actions, key=lambda a: Q[s][a]) # one greedy joint pick
```

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Agents chase each other | Each best response moves | Centralized critic, slow LR, freeze one |
| Replay makes it worse | Obsolete opponents in old data | Relabel, or weight by recency |
| No credit for shared reward | Credit assignment | COMA baseline or per-agent shaping |
| Self-play stuck in a cycle | Dominance cycle | League play with diverse opponents |
| DR policy too cautious | Too much randomization | Match the expected real distribution |
| DR does not help | Wrong parameter randomized | Profile the real robot first |
| Student cannot match teacher | Privileged info leakage | Keep the teacher realizable from obs |
| Policy breaks hardware | No safety envelope | Rate, torque and joint limits outside |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md

- **CTDE**: Centralized training, decentralized execution.
- **IPPO**: Independent PPO. Each agent runs PPO alone.
- **COMA**: counterfactual multi-agent. Isolates my contribution.
- **DR**: domain randomization. Random sim parameters in training.
- **SI**: system identification. Measure the real robot, fit the sim.
- **ADR**: Automatic Domain Randomization. Widens DR as the policy improves.
- **VLA**: vision-language-action. Image and instruction in, actions out.
- **FAST**: Frequency-domain Action Sequence Tokenizer. DCT, then quantize.

## Rules of thumb
type: tips
from: phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/20-marl-maddpg-qmix-mappo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md

- Start with MAPPO for cooperative MARL.
- Use independent Q only for loosely-coupled tasks.
- Use self-play for zero-sum games. Use league play for strategy cycles.
- Log the observation and action stream of every agent.
- Test on a held-out sim variant before you deploy.
- Flag a DR range wider than 3× the measured real variability.
- Close a VLA domain gap with LoRA on 100-1000 task demos.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/10-multi-agent-rl/docs/en.md, phases/16-multi-agent-and-swarms/20-marl-maddpg-qmix-mappo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/11-sim-to-real-transfer/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/21-embodied-vlas-openvla-pi0-groot/docs/en.md

- **Where does independent Q fail?** On tightly-coupled tasks, where one agent must wait.
- **Why does QMIX allow local argmax?** The mixer is monotonic in each per-agent Q.
- **What does narrow training do?** Slip 0.0 only drops hard as soon as real slip is above 0.
- **Why co-fine-tune a VLA?** Robot-only models fail on new instructions.
- **Why the GR00T split?** Slow planning does not block fast control.

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/07-bayes-theorem/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/09-information-theory/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/13-numerical-stability/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/14-norms-and-distances/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/11-singular-value-decomposition/docs/en.md

- **Chain rule**: $\frac{dy}{dx} = f'(g(x)) \cdot g'(x)$
- **Bayes**: $P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(B \mid A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}$
- **Entropy**: $H(P) = -\sum_{x} p(x) \log(p(x))$
- **Cross-entropy**: $H(P, Q) = -\sum_{x} p(x) \log(q(x))$
- **KL divergence**: $D_{KL}(P \,\|\, Q) = H(P, Q) - H(P)$. Not symmetric.
- **Log-sum-exp**: $\log \sum_i e^{x_i} = \max(x) + \log \sum_i e^{x_i - \max(x)}$
- **Cosine similarity**: $\frac{a \cdot b}{\lVert a \rVert_2 \, \lVert b \rVert_2}$, from -1 to +1
- **SVD**: $A = U \Sigma V^T$. Rank $k$: $A_k = U_k \Sigma_k V_k^T$

## Update rules
type: concepts
from: phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/04-calculus-for-ml/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/16-sampling-methods/docs/en.md

- **Gradient descent**: $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot \text{gradient}$
- **Momentum**: $v = \beta v + \text{gradient}$, then $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot v$
- **Adam moments**: $m = \beta_1 m + (1 - \beta_1) g$, $v = \beta_2 v + (1 - \beta_2) g^2$
- **Bias correction**: $\hat{m} = m / (1 - \beta_1^t)$, $\hat{v} = v / (1 - \beta_2^t)$
- **Adam step**: $w = w - \text{lr} \cdot \hat{m} / (\sqrt{\hat{v}} + \epsilon)$
- **Cosine schedule**: $\text{lr}_{\min} + 0.5 (\text{lr}_{\max} - \text{lr}_{\min})(1 + \cos(\pi t / T))$
- **Newton step**: $w_{\text{new}} = w_{\text{old}} - H^{-1} \cdot \text{gradient}$
- **Temperature**: $p_i = e^{z_i / T} / \sum_j e^{z_j / T}$

## Autograd in a few lines
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md

```python
x = torch.tensor(2.0, requires_grad=True)  # record operations on x
y = x ** 2 + 3 * x + 1                     # builds the graph
y.backward()                               # reverse mode pass
print(x.grad)                              # 7.0 = 2*x + 3
def __mul__(self, other):
    out = Value(self.data * other.data, (self, other), '*')
    def _backward():
        self.grad += other.data * out.grad  # local grad times upstream
        other.grad += self.data * out.grad  # += sums over all uses
    out._backward = _backward
    return out
self.grad = 1.0                            # seed dy/dy = 1
for v in reversed(topo):                   # output to inputs
    v._backward()                          # chain rule at each node
```

## Stable softmax and cross-entropy
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/01-math-foundations/13-numerical-stability/docs/en.md

```python
def softmax_stable(logits):
    max_logit = max(logits)                           # subtract the max first
    exps = [math.exp(z - max_logit) for z in logits]  # largest term is 1
    total = sum(exps)
    return [e / total for e in exps]
def cross_entropy_stable(true_class, logits):
    max_logit = max(logits)
    shifted = [z - max_logit for z in logits]
    log_sum_exp = math.log(sum(math.exp(s) for s in shifted))
    log_prob = shifted[true_class] - log_sum_exp     # stay in log space
    return -log_prob
```

## PCA with SVD
type: flow
from: phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/11-singular-value-decomposition/docs/en.md

1. **Center**: subtract the mean from each feature.
2. **Covariance**: $C = \frac{1}{n-1} X^T X$ for centered X.
3. **Decompose**: call `np.linalg.svd(A)` on the data. Avoid eig of $A^T A$.
4. **Components**: the right singular vectors V are the principal components.
5. **Variance**: component i explains $\sigma_i^2 / (n-1)$.
6. **Choose k**: keep components up to 90 to 95% cumulative variance.
7. **Project**: keep the top k directions and drop the rest.

type: defaults

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/01-math-foundations/13-numerical-stability/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/17-linear-systems/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/07-bayes-theorem/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Loss is NaN after a few epochs | softmax overflow or lr too high | stable softmax, lower lr, clip gradients |
| Loss stuck at log(num_classes) | near uniform outputs | check labels, loss function, dead ReLUs |
| Accuracy 1 to 3% low with float16 | gradient underflow | dynamic loss scaling or bfloat16 |
| Gradient norm 0.0 in some layers | dead ReLU or float16 underflow | LeakyReLU or GELU, gradient scaling |
| Results differ across GPUs | float addition is not associative | `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)` |
| `0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3` is False | 0.1 is not exact in binary | `math.isclose()` or a tolerance |
| Solution changes a lot for small input changes | large condition number | add $\lambda I$ or drop collinear features |
| One unseen word zeroes Naive Bayes | MLE gives probability zero | Laplace smoothing, add 1 to counts |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/01-math-foundations/05-chain-rule-and-autodiff/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/09-information-theory/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/13-numerical-stability/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/11-singular-value-decomposition/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/16-sampling-methods/docs/en.md

- **Why reverse mode?** Many inputs and one loss. One backward pass gives all gradients.
- **Why cross-entropy?** Minimizing it maximizes the likelihood of the data.
- **Why bfloat16 for training?** It has the float32 range, so values above 65,504 do not overflow.
- **Why SVD and not the eigenvectors of A.T @ A?** That product squares the condition number.
- **Why the reparameterization trick?** $z = \mu + \sigma \epsilon$ lets gradients flow through $\mu$ and $\sigma$.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/01-math-foundations/02-vectors-matrices-operations/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/13-numerical-stability/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/07-bayes-theorem/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/09-information-theory/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/08-optimization/docs/en.md

- Check shapes: `(m x n) @ (n x p) = (m x p)`.
- Sum log probabilities. Do not multiply many small probabilities.
- Never compare floats with `==`.
- Check gradients when you write a new layer or loss.
- Perplexity is the exponential of cross-entropy in nats.
- In a gradient check, a relative error below 1e-5 is acceptable.

type: flow

## Stamp every modern request
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/08-building-an-mcp-client/code/main.py

```python
def modern_request(request_id, method, params, version, capabilities=None):
    body_params = dict(params or {})
    body_params["_meta"] = request_meta(version, capabilities)  # new on each call
    return {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": request_id, "method": method, "params": body_params}
VERSION_KEY = "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"          # required
CAPABILITIES_KEY = "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"  # required
CLIENT_INFO_KEY = "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"           # client identity

```

## stdio or Streamable HTTP
type: comparison
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/09-mcp-transports/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/14-model-context-protocol/docs/en.md

| Factor | stdio | Streamable HTTP |
|---|---|---|
| Use it for | Client-launched subprocess | Network service |
| Framing | One UTF-8 JSON-RPC message per line | One JSON-RPC message per POST |
| Version context | `params._meta` | `params._meta` plus mirrored headers |
| Response | One line on stdout | JSON or request-scoped SSE |
| Notification | No response line | `202 Accepted`, no body |
| Diagnostics | stderr only | HTTP status plus JSON-RPC error |

## MRTR round for Sampling
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/11-mcp-sampling/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/11-mcp-sampling/code/main.py

1. **Client**: calls `tools/call`. Capabilities hold `sampling`.
2. **Server**: returns `input_required`, `inputRequests`, `requestState`.
3. **Client**: checks policy and asks its model.
4. **Client**: same method and arguments, new id, `inputResponses`, exact `requestState`.
5. **Server**: verifies HMAC, principal, arguments digest, expiry.
6. **Server**: last round returns `resultType: "complete"`.

## Status and error codes
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/09-mcp-transports/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/09-mcp-transports/code/main.py, phases/11-llm-engineering/14-model-context-protocol/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/11-mcp-sampling/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/22-jsonrpc-stdio-transport/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP 400, `-32020` | Header missing or differs from body | Build headers from the final body |
| HTTP 400, `-32022` | Version not supported | Retry with a value from `supported` |
| `-32021` | Client lacks a required capability | Read `data.requiredCapabilities` |
| `-32602` | Missing `_meta` or bad `requestState` | Send `_meta` and echo the state |
| HTTP 403 | `Origin` not in the allowlist | Use an exact origin match |
| HTTP 404, `-32601` | Unknown modern method | Do not treat it as legacy proof |

| `-32700`, id null | One stdio line is broken JSON | Loop continues with the next line |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/08-building-an-mcp-client/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/09-mcp-transports/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/11-mcp-sampling/docs/en.md

- **Is -32601 proof of a legacy server?** No. It only lets an allowlisted peer get one probe.
- **Can a stream resume?** No. `Last-Event-ID` is ignored. Send a new request with a new id.
- **Where does workflow state go?** In a server-minted handle that the client passes as an argument.
- **Can the server call the client?** No. It returns `input_required` and the client retries.
- **Do model preferences sum to one?** No. They are independent hints.

```python
controller = RegistryAdmissionController(clock=lambda: next(ticks))

controller.admit(sample_record("1.1.0"), active_meta,
    namespace_for_domain("example.com"),         # gives com.example
```

## Seven admission controls
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/30-mcp-registry-supply-chain-and-drift/docs/en.md

1. **Namespace**: compare the segment before `/` exactly with the verified namespace.
2. **Provenance**: join registry type, identifier, version, ownership and artifact digest.
3. **Pin**: store record, source, toolset and provenance digests. Never `^1.4` or latest.
4. **Live drift**: call `server/discover`. Any descriptor digest change quarantines the pin.
5. **Status**: read the official `_meta` status. Deprecated or deleted quarantines.
6. **Rollback**: route to an admitted pin that is active and not quarantined.
7. **Ledger**: append each decision with the previous hash and its own hash.

type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/17-mcp-gateways-and-registries/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/17-mcp-gateways-and-registries/docs/en.md

|---|---|---|
| 401 `-32001` | Bearer is not known | Authenticate the principal |
| 403 `-32003` | Tool is not in `RBAC` for the user | Grant the role or keep the deny |
| 429 `-32029` | `TokenBucket` is empty | Wait for refill |
| 409 `-32010` | Live descriptor differs from the pin | Review, then re-approve the pin |
| 400 `-32020` | Header and body disagree | Match `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` |
| 400 `-32022` | Matched version is not supported | Send a version in `supported` |
| 406 on `subscriptions/listen` | Accept has no `text/event-stream` | Accept SSE |
| 405 | GET or DELETE on the endpoint | Send each message as POST |

## Release failures
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/31-mcp-conformance-versioning-and-operations/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/30-mcp-registry-supply-chain-and-drift/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|

| SDK shows `resultType` the wire lacked | SDK synthesizes the discriminator | Validate the raw body |
| Origin 400 arrives as 500 | Proxy collapses the error | Compare ingress, origin and egress |
| Canary has zero errors and no traffic | No minimum sample count | Enforce `sampleCount` above 0 |
| New tool appears after approval | Runtime drift | Quarantine the route |
| Rollback target was never admitted | Route and approval state disconnected | Refuse, run a new admission |

## Rules
type: tips
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/17-mcp-gateways-and-registries/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/30-mcp-registry-supply-chain-and-drift/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/31-mcp-conformance-versioning-and-operations/docs/en.md

- Never pass the outer gateway token to a backend.
- Do not copy outer client capabilities to a backend. The gateway is its client.
- Key rate limits by principal, issuer, resource, tool, cost class and window.
- Preserve `requestState` byte for byte. Re-authorize every MRTR retry.
- Route `tasks/get`, `tasks/update`, `tasks/cancel` by `params.taskId` in `Mcp-Name`.
- Run admission before a server appears in `tools/list`.
- Redact before serialization, hashing, logs or upload.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/17-mcp-gateways-and-registries/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/30-mcp-registry-supply-chain-and-drift/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/31-mcp-conformance-versioning-and-operations/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/23-capstone-tool-ecosystem/docs/en.md

- **Does registry presence approve a server?** No. Admission policy decides.
- **Can `serverInfo` prove the publisher?** No. It is diagnostic data only.
- **Is an unknown field an unknown result?** No. Keep the field. Reject an unknown `resultType`.
- **Does rollback edit the old record?** No. It changes the active route.
- **Does a green capstone run prove the wire?** No. It validates the simulation only.

title: MCP Security and Authorization
subtitle: Find and fix token refusals, poisoned tool metadata and injected content. CIMD, PKCE, iss, audience and PVE checks.
markdown:
## Token refusals
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 401 `malformed` | Token does not decode | Send a valid JWT in `Authorization` |
| 401 `iss not allowed` | Issuer not in `allowed_issuers` | Trust only `authorization_servers` issuers |
| 401 `unknown kid` | Key missing after one refetch | Fix the JWKS refresh job |
| 401 `bad signature` | Signature does not verify | Reject. There is no fallback |
| 401 `audience mismatch` | Token is for another resource | Request it with this `resource` |
| 401 `expired` | `exp` is in the past | Get a new token |
| 403 `insufficient_scope` | Tool needs a larger scope | Step up with combined scopes, new id |
| Valid tokens fail after a key change | Stale JWKS cache | Scheduled refresh plus one refetch on a miss |

## Gateway and content findings
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/27-prompt-injection-defense/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `metadata_poisoning` finding | Scanner hit in a description | Block and review the full descriptor |
| `rug_pull` finding | Approved descriptor changed | Quarantine until re-approval |
| `unapproved` finding | No approved digest for the key | Quarantine until review |
| `shadowing` finding | Two servers expose one name | Namespace it, for example `notes.search` |
| `-32020` | `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` differs from the body | Reject before routing, RBAC and rate limits |
| `-32021` on a form request | Client declared URL-only elicitation | Declare `elicitation` form support |
| Retry refused after confirm | `requestState` bound to other arguments | Ask for a new confirmation |
| Agent obeys a web page | No source tag on retrieved content | Tag content and validate each tool call |

## Validation order on the resource server
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/code/main.py

1. **Decode**: `jwt_decode` fails. Return 401 malformed.
2. **Issuer**: `iss` not in `allowed_issuers`. Return 401 before any JWKS fetch.
3. **Key**: look up `kid` in `jwks_cache`. On a miss call `refresh_jwks` one time.
4. **Signature**: `jwt_verify` fails. Return 401 bad signature.
5. **Audience**: `aud` is not this resource. Return 401 audience mismatch.
6. **Expiry**: `exp` is in the past. Return 401 expired.
7. **Scope**: required scope is absent. Return 403 `insufficient_scope` with the scope.

## Authorization code with PKCE
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/code/main.py

1. **Client**: fetch protected-resource metadata. Pick an advertised issuer.
2. **Client**: make a `code_verifier` and its S256 `code_challenge` with `pkce_pair`.
3. **Client**: send `client_id`, `redirect_uri`, `scope`, `code_challenge` and `resource`.
4. **Authorization server**: returns `code` and `iss`.
5. **Client**: compare `iss` with the recorded issuer exactly. On mismatch, drop the response.
6. **Client**: exchange the code with `code_verifier`, the same redirect URI and `resource`.
7. **Client**: store the token under `(issuer, resource)` in `tokens_by_issuer_resource`.

type: task-table
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md

## PVE: validate before execute
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/14-agent-engineering/27-prompt-injection-defense/code/main.py

```python
validator = Validator(
    allowed_tools=("search", "send_message", "read_memory"),
    sensitive_tools=("send_message",))
call = ToolCall("search", {"query": "<query>"}, intent="research")
contents = [Content("<text>", "user_message")]  # user text is not scanned
ok, reason = validator.assess(call, contents)   # allowlist, args, retrieved text
if ok:
    executor.run(call)                          # runs only after approval
looks_like_directive("<text>")                  # first marker hit or None
memory_write_guard(MemoryWrite("<text>"))       # refuses directive-shaped writes
```

## Client enrollment paths
type: comparison
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md

| Factor | Pre-registered | CIMD | DCR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Status | Use first if it exists | Preferred | Deprecated fallback |
| Client id | From the operator | HTTPS URL with a path | Minted by `POST /register` |
| AS signal | Known relationship | `client_id_metadata_document_supported` | `registration_endpoint` |
| `application_type` | Not required | Optional | Required: `native` or `web` |
| New issuer | New credentials | URL stays portable | Register again |
| Main risk | Reuse at a new issuer | SSRF on the fetch | Registration spam, token theft |

## Seven attack surfaces
type: concepts
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/docs/en.md

- **Metadata poisoning**: a description holds instructions unrelated to the tool.
- **Descriptor rug pull**: an approved name, description, schema or annotation changes.
- **Cross-server shadowing**: two backends expose one unqualified name.
- **Header and body confusion**: `Mcp-Method` or `Mcp-Name` disagrees with the body.
- **Capability escalation**: a declared feature is read as authorization.
- **MRTR state tampering**: a changed `requestState` or reused confirmation.
- **Identity confusion**: a familiar display name is read as publisher proof.

## Rules
type: tips
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/docs/en.md

- Send the bearer token in the `Authorization` header on every request. Never in the URL.
- Do not add an OAuth flow to a local stdio server.
- Never forward the MCP token to a downstream API. Get a separate token.
- Compare `iss` exactly. No case folding, slash or port changes.
- The resource server refreshes JWKS. Only the authorization server rotates keys.
- Fail closed when introspection is down. Network failure is never `active: true`.
- Rule of two: one step never combines untrusted input, sensitive data and an external action.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/15-mcp-security-tool-poisoning/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/27-prompt-injection-defense/docs/en.md

- **Is `clientInfo` an identity?** No. It is self-reported.
- **Does a hash pin prove a tool is safe?** No. It proves stability only.
- **Does PKCE stop a mix-up attack?** No. The client must validate `iss`.
- **Do client capabilities grant access?** No. They declare compatibility only.
- **Is "ignore untrusted instructions" in the prompt enough?** No. That is not enforcement.

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/16-mcp-security-oauth-2-1/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/18-mcp-auth-production/docs/en.md, phases/14-agent-engineering/27-prompt-injection-defense/docs/en.md

- **CIMD**: Client ID Metadata Document. Its HTTPS URL is the client id.
- **DCR**: Dynamic Client Registration. RFC 7591, deprecated.
- **PKCE**: verifier and S256 challenge that protect the code.
- **JWKS**: JSON Web Key Set, fetched from `jwks_uri`, indexed by `kid`.
- **RFC 9728**: protected-resource metadata. Names the authorization servers.
- **RFC 8707**: resource indicator. Binds the token to one MCP resource.
- **RFC 9207**: `iss` in the authorization response. Stops mix-up.
- **PVE**: Prompt-Validator-Executor. Cheap validator before the main model.

## The dispatch loop
type: flow
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/code/main.py

1. **serve_stdio**: Reads one line from stdin. Bad JSON gives `-32700`.
2. **dispatch**: No `id` means a notification. The server sends no response.
3. **validate_request**: Checks `params._meta` for version and capabilities.
4. **HANDLERS**: Routes by `method`. An unknown method gives `-32601`.
5. **complete**: Adds `resultType` and serverInfo to the handler result.
6. **serve_stdio**: Writes one JSON line to stdout, flushes, forgets the metadata.

## Validate and wrap every request
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/code/main.py

```python
meta = params.get("_meta")                     # -32602 when missing
requested = meta.get(VERSION_KEY)              # protocolVersion key
if requested not in SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
    raise RpcProblem(-32022, "Unsupported protocol version",
        {"requested": requested, "supported": SUPPORTED_VERSIONS.copy()})
if not isinstance(meta.get(CAPABILITIES_KEY), dict):
    raise RpcProblem(-32602, f"{CAPABILITIES_KEY} is required")
result = {"resultType": "complete", **payload,
    "_meta": {SERVER_INFO_KEY: SERVER_INFO.copy()}}
if ttl_ms is not None:                         # lists, reads, discovery
    result["ttlMs"] = ttl_ms
    result["cacheScope"] = cache_scope         # default "private"
```

## Register a tool and its executor
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/code/main.py

```python
TOOL_EXECUTORS = {"notes_search": exec_notes_search}  # name to function
def handle_tools_list(params):
    return complete({"tools": sorted(TOOLS, key=lambda tool: tool["name"])},
                    ttl_ms=60_000, cache_scope="public")
def handle_tools_call(params):
    executor = TOOL_EXECUTORS.get(name)
    if executor is None:                      # result, not RPC error
        return complete({"content": [...], "isError": True})
    try:
        return complete({"content": executor(arguments), "isError": False})
    except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
        return complete({"content": [...], "isError": True})
```

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/10-mcp-resources-and-prompts/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/28-mcp-tool-contracts-and-content/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/13-mcp-server-with-registry/docs/en.md, projects/memory-server/solution

## Error codes
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/07-building-an-mcp-server/code/main.py, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/10-mcp-resources-and-prompts/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/28-mcp-tool-contracts-and-content/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `-32700` Parse error | Line is not JSON | Send one JSON object per line |
| `-32600` Invalid Request | No `jsonrpc` 2.0 or no method | Fix the envelope |
| `-32602` invalid params | `params._meta` missing | Send version and capabilities each time |
| `-32022` | Unsupported version string | Retry with a version from `supported` |
| `-32601` | Method not in `HANDLERS` | Add the handler or fix the name |
| `-32602` on `resources/read` | Unknown or invalid URI | Never return an empty read |
| HTTP `400` and `-32020` | `Mcp-Param-*` header differs from body | Reject before dispatch |
| Client parse fails | Logs on stdout | Write diagnostics to stderr |

## Tool contracts
type: concepts
from: phases/13-tools-and-protocols/28-mcp-tool-contracts-and-content/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/28-mcp-tool-contracts-and-content/code/main.py

- **inputSchema**: JSON Schema. With no `$schema`, the dialect is 2020-12.
- **No arguments**: `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false}`.
- **outputSchema**: Optional. Once published, every result carries conforming `structuredContent`.
- **structuredContent**: Any JSON value. Also send the JSON as a text block.
- **Content blocks**: `text`, `image`, `audio`, `resource_link`, `resource`.
- **x-mcp-header**: Mirrors a top-level argument to `Mcp-Param-{name}`. String, integer or boolean only.
- **Header encoding**: Non-ASCII or padded values use `=?base64?{Base64UTF8}?=`.
- **Cursors**: Opaque. An empty `nextCursor` is valid. Stop only on `None`.
