## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/09-reward-modeling-rlhf/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/07-rlhf/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/08-dpo/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/03-direct-preference-optimization-family/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Reward climbs, human eval flat | Reward hacking | Stop early, raise β, broaden RM data |
| Responses get longer | Length hacking | Length-normalized reward, or SimPO |
| Mean KL past ~5-10 | Policy drifted from SFT | Adaptive β that targets a fixed KL |
| Policy barely changes | β too high | Lower β |
| Chosen log-prob falls in DPO | Degraded Chosen Response | BPO penalty on the chosen response |
| DPO gap blows up | Implicit reward gap is unbounded | IPO, gap capped at 1/(2 beta) |
| RM scores unreliable | RM smaller than the policy | RM at least as large as the policy |
| ~30% noisy labels | Ambiguous preferences | Agreement-filtered data, BT temperature |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/07-rlhf/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/09-reward-modeling-rlhf/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/08-dpo/docs/en.md, phases/18-ethics-safety-alignment/03-direct-preference-optimization-family/docs/en.md

- **Why pairs, not absolute scores?** People rank two answers well. They score one answer badly.
- **Why the KL term?** It keeps the policy near the data where the RM was trained.
- **Why does the RM read the last token?** The causal mask lets it see the whole sequence.
- **How many forward passes per DPO pair?** Four: two models times two responses.
- **Do DAAs escape over-optimization?** No. They over-optimize the reference ratio instead.

title: RNNs, Seq2Seq and N-gram Models
subtitle: TextCNN, LSTM and GRU, encoder-decoder with teacher forcing, beam search, BLEU, Kneser-Ney and why attention won.
markdown:
## Seq2seq encoder-decoder
type: architecture
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md

```arch
node | src | 1,1 | Source tokens | src ids | client
node | enc | 2,1 | Encoder GRU | outputs, hidden | model
node | ctx | 3,1 | Context vector | final hidden state | store
node | bos | 1,2 | bos_id token | then the last token | client
node | dec | 2,2 | Decoder GRU | one step at a time | model
node | out | 3,2 | Vocabulary logits | argmax or beam | process
edge | src | enc |
edge | enc | ctx | bottleneck
edge | ctx | dec | init hidden
edge | bos | dec | input_token
edge | dec | out |
edge | out | bos | feed back
```

## Core formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/01-why-transformers/docs/en.md

- **RNN**: $h_t = f(W x_t + U h_{t-1} + b)$. W, U and b are shared across time.
- **LSTM**: input, forget and output gates plus a cell state. Stable gradients.
- **GRU**: two gates. Similar accuracy, fewer parameters.
- **TextCNN**: a width-k filter is a learnable k-gram. Global max-pool per filter.
- **N-gram**: $P(w \mid \mathrm{ctx}) = \mathrm{count}(\mathrm{ctx}, w) / \mathrm{count}(\mathrm{ctx})$
- **Perplexity**: $\exp(-\frac{1}{N} \sum_i \log P(w_i \mid \mathrm{ctx}_i))$. Lower is better.
- **Kneser-Ney**: absolute discount plus continuation probability for the lower order.
- **BLEU**: n-gram precision for n of 1 to 4, geometric mean, brevity penalty. 0 to 100.

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/code/main.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/code/main.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/01-why-transformers/code/main.py

| Task | Code |

| Gradient left after N steps | `vanishing_gradient_sim(seq_len, recurrent_weight=0.9)` |
| Decode without a teacher | `greedy_decode(encoder, decoder, src, bos_id, eos_id, max_len=50)` |
| Toy BLEU | `simple_bleu(hypothesis, reference, max_n=4)` |
| Character F-score | `chrf(hypothesis, reference, n=6, beta=2)` |
| Count trigrams | `train_ngram(corpus_tokens, n=3)` |
| Smoothed bigram model | `kneser_ney_bigram_model(corpus_tokens, discount=0.75)` |
| Score held-out text | `perplexity(prob_fn, sentences)` |
| Serial vs parallel depth | `rnn_style(xs, decay=0.9)` vs `attention_style(xs)` |

## Train with teacher forcing
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md

```python
_, hidden = encoder(src)                        # context vector
input_token = torch.full((batch_size, 1), bos_id, dtype=torch.long)
loss_fn = nn.CrossEntropyLoss(ignore_index=0)   # skip padding
for t in range(tgt_len):
    logits, hidden = decoder(input_token, hidden)
    loss += loss_fn(logits.squeeze(1), tgt[:, t])
    use_teacher = torch.rand(1).item() < teacher_forcing_ratio
    if use_teacher:
        input_token = tgt[:, t].unsqueeze(1)    # ground truth at t-1
    else:
        input_token = logits.argmax(dim=-1)     # own prediction
loss.backward()
```

## TextCNN forward pass
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md

```python
x = self.embed(token_ids).transpose(1, 2)  # [batch, embed_dim, seq_len]
for conv in self.convs:                    # one per width in (2, 3, 4)
    c = F.relu(conv(x))
    p = F.max_pool1d(c, c.size(2)).squeeze(2)  # strongest activation
    pooled.append(p)
h = torch.cat(pooled, dim=1)               # fixed size for any length
out, _ = self.lstm(x)                      # LSTM classifier instead
pooled = out.max(dim=1).values             # max-pool beats last state
```

## Translate and score
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md

```python
model_id = "facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id, src_lang="eng_Latn")
out = model.generate(**inputs,
    forced_bos_token_id=tok.convert_tokens_to_ids("fra_Latn"),  # target
    num_beams=5, length_penalty=1.0, max_new_tokens=64)
print(tok.batch_decode(out, skip_special_tokens=True)[0])
bleu = sacrebleu.corpus_bleu(hypotheses, references)
chrf = sacrebleu.corpus_chrf(hypotheses, references)
```

## Defaults and numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `teacher_forcing_ratio` | 0.9 | Start at 1.0, anneal to ~0.5 |
| Beam width | 3-5 | MT uses 4-5 for general content |
| KN `discount` | 0.75 | Subtracted from every bigram count |
| TextCNN filters | 64 | Widths (2, 3, 4), dropout 0.3 |
| `0.9 ^ 100` | 2.7e-5 | Gradient left after 100 steps |
| Copy accuracy at length 40 | 23% | 98% at length 5. The bottleneck |
| BLEU bands | 30 | 40 is good, 50 exceptional, under 1 is noise |
| 4-gram KN perplexity, Brown | 140 | A transformer LM gets 15-30 |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Drift on long outputs | Exposure bias | Scheduled sampling, anneal the ratio |
| Long inputs lose detail | One fixed context vector | Attention over all encoder states |
| Plain RNN learns no long range | Vanishing gradient | Use an LSTM or GRU |
| Greedy output repeats and loops | Commits to each token | Beam search, width 4-5 |
| Output in the wrong language | Off-target generation | Check `forced_bos_token_id`, run language ID |
| Short input gives long output | Length penalty under ~5 tokens | Cap length by source length |
| Fluent output with new facts | Hallucination | Constrained decoding, human review |
| N-gram gives probability 0 | Unseen n-gram | Smooth with Kneser-Ney |

## Use X when
type: qa
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/01-why-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md

- **TextCNN?** Edge and on-device. It is 10-100x smaller than a transformer.
- **LSTM?** Streaming text, one token at a time. BiLSTM-CRF for 1k-10k labeled sentences.
- **RNN seq2seq?** Almost never. Streaming translation or on-device generation only.
- **N-gram LM?** On-device autocomplete, rescoring, and a baseline before any neural LM.
- **Transformer?** Everything else. Serial depth is 1, not N. Memory is $O(N^2)$.
- **BLEU or chrF?** Report both. chrF counts better on morphologically rich languages.

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/08-cnns-rnns-for-text/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/09-sequence-to-sequence/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/01-why-transformers/docs/en.md

- **LSTM**: gated RNN with input, forget and output gates and a cell state.
- **GRU**: gated RNN with two gates.
- **NMT**: neural MT. Transformer encoder-decoder trained on parallel text.
- **NLLB**: No Language Left Behind. A 200-language MT model family.
- **chrF**: character-level F-score.
- **SSM**: state-space model. Recurrence with parallel training.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/11-machine-translation/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/16-text-generation-pre-transformer/docs/en.md

- Always use `sacrebleu`. Your own BLEU code gives scores you cannot compare.
- Ship at least two metric families. COMET is the default where quality matters.
- Calibrate each metric on 50-100 human-labeled examples.
- Compare perplexity only under identical tokenization.
- A few thousand clean parallel pairs beat a few hundred thousand noisy ones.

## How sbx decides
type: concepts
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-3-sbx-policy-init-allow-deny-and-check-network.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-4-sbx-policy-log-and-the-proxy.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-5-sbx-secret-set-import-and-set-custom.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/7-2-org-policies-profiles-and-the-audit-log.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-1-sbx-diagnose-and-the-microvm-boundary.md

- **Deny wins**: a deny beats an allow for the same hostname or CIDR.
- **deny_kind**: `implicit` means no rule matched. `explicit` names the rule.
- **check network**: host and port only, port 443 by default. It exits 1 on a denial.
- **forward-bypass**: a tunnel with no inspection and no credential injection.
- **Secrets**: the agent sees `proxy-managed` or `sbx-cs-<rand>`, never the value.
- **SSH agent**: forwarding is on by default. Keys stay on the host.
- **Governance**: only organization allow rules grant. Local deny rules still apply.
- **Boundary**: the hypervisor, not in-VM privilege separation.

type: comparison
from: manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/5-5-permissions-safety-and-hooks.md

| Factor | `strict` | `balanced` | `restricted` | `autonomous` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `safe` label | ask | allow | allow | allow |
| `destructive` label | ask | ask | deny | allow |
| `unknown` label | ask | ask | deny | allow |

## Refusals and fixes
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/26-sandbox-runner-denylist/code/main.py, projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/cli.py, projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/stage3.rs, projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/main.rs, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-3-sbx-policy-init-allow-deny-and-check-network.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-4-sbx-policy-log-and-the-proxy.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `is on the denylist` | Basename of argv[0] is in `DEFAULT_DENYLIST` | Use another tool or change `denylist` |
| `use a script file instead of -c/-e` | Interpreter with an inline code flag | Write the code to a script file |
| `set shell=True to opt in` | Metachar in argv with shell off | Split the command into argv |
| `resolves outside project root` | `../`, an absolute path or a symlink out | Keep paths under `project_root` |
| `Limit` error from the planner | No sufficient profile within the budget | Raise `--budget`. A kernel needs 5 |
| `Docker probe cannot establish independent guest kernel` | `--docker-image` with `host_kernel=true` | Use the policy simulation only |
| `conflicts with existing allow rule` | Deny over an allow in one scope | `sbx policy rm network` first |
| `403 Forbidden`, 90-byte body | No rule matched, approval required | Add an allow rule. It is not a network fault |

## Q&A
type: qa
from: projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/main.rs, projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/stage2.rs, projects/sandbox-ladder/README.md, projects/sandbox-ladder/solution/cli.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/26-sandbox-runner-denylist/docs/en.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/5-5-permissions-safety-and-hooks.md

- **Does `network=true` grant network?** No. It means network denial is required.
- **All four needs at budget 4?** `Limit`. Only `microvm-fixture` has a kernel, at cost 5.
- **Does the Docker probe prove a microVM?** No. It tests root write and the default route only.
- **Is the lesson sandbox an OS boundary?** No. It uses no namespaces, cgroups or seccomp.
- **Are agent permissions a boundary?** No. They run client-side. Use a sandbox for isolation.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/26-sandbox-runner-denylist/docs/en.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/5-5-permissions-safety-and-hooks.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-5-sbx-secret-set-import-and-set-custom.md, manuals/docker-sandboxes-101/sections/3-4-sbx-policy-log-and-the-proxy.md

- Run unattended agents with `--safety restricted`.
- Put destructive commands in `deny`. No mode or hook allow overrides it.
- Store keys with `sbx secret set`, never with `-e KEY`.
- Turn off `ssh.agentForwardingEnabled` for an agent you would not let sign.
- A host allow passes any body. Narrow an API with a kit HTTP rule.
- In production, add a container or microVM, drop capabilities, mount the root read-only.

title: Scaling Laws and Pre-Training
subtitle: Chinchilla math, over-training, the data pipeline from raw text to packed batches, and a mini GPT training loop.
markdown:
## Data pipeline
type: architecture
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md

```arch
node | raw | 1,1 | Raw text | Common Crawl ~250 TB raw | store
node | html | 2,1 | HTML strip | visible text only | process
node | lang | 3,1 | Language detection | lid.176.bin, 0.8 confidence | process
node | qual | 4,1 | Quality filter | perplexity or heuristics | process
node | dedup | 4,2 | Deduplication | MinHash + LSH | process
node | pii | 3,2 | PII removal | regex and NER | process
node | pack | 2,2 | Tokenize + pack | EOS between docs | process
node | load | 1,2 | DataLoader | shuffled batches | queue
edge | raw | html |
edge | html | lang |
edge | lang | qual |
edge | qual | dedup |
edge | dedup | pii |
edge | pii | pack |
edge | pack | load | sequences, masks
```

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md

- **Compute**: $C \approx 6 \times N \times D$ FLOPs for a standard transformer.
- **Hoffmann loss**: $L(N, D) = \frac{A}{N^\alpha} + \frac{B}{D^\beta} + E$
- **Fitted constants**: $\alpha \approx 0.34$, $\beta \approx 0.28$, $E \approx 1.69$, $A \approx 406$, $B \approx 411$.
- **Compute-optimal**: $N_{\text{opt}} \sim C^{0.5}$, $D_{\text{opt}} \sim C^{0.5}$, $D/N \approx 20$.
- **Jaccard**: shared shingles over all shingles. Remove a copy above 0.8.
- **Compression ratio**: characters per token. English is about 3-4.
- **Start loss**: about $\ln(V)$. A 256-token byte vocab starts at 5.55.
- **Attention scale**: divide by $\sqrt{d_k}$. For 64 dims that is 8.

## Models against Chinchilla
type: comparison
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md

| Factor | GPT-3 | Chinchilla | Llama 3 8B |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parameters | 175B | 70B | 8B |
| Tokens | ~300B | 1.4T | 15T |
| Tokens per param | About 1.7 | About 20 | 1,875 |
| Verdict | Undertrained | Compute-optimal by design | 94× past optimal |
| Why | Kaplan laws: push N hard | Minimize loss per FLOP | Cheap to serve at scale |

## Compute-optimal against over-trained
type: comparison
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/code/main.py

| Factor | Chinchilla-optimal | Over-trained |
|---|---|---|
| Minimizes | Training loss per training FLOP | Total cost with inference |
| Tokens per param | About 20 | 100 to 500, by serving volume |
| Cost paid | Once, at training | Extra pretrain FLOPs once |
| Inference cost | Higher, N is larger | Lower, N is smaller |
| Code check | `compute_optimal(C)` | `chinchilla_loss(N_under, D_over)` |
| Example | Chinchilla 70B on 1.4T | Llama 3 8B on 15T |

type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/code/main.py

```python
cleaned_docs = [clean_text(doc) for doc in raw_docs]   # strip HTML, URLs, spaces
filtered_docs = [doc for doc in cleaned_docs if quality_filter(doc)]   # length, caps, symbols
```

## One training step
type: flow
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/code/main.py

1. **Batch**: take `seq_len + 1` tokens. Inputs drop the last token. Targets drop the first.
2. **Mask**: `np.triu(np.full((seq_len, seq_len), -1e9), k=1)` blocks future positions.
3. **Forward**: embeddings, all blocks, final LayerNorm. Logits use `token_embed.T`.
4. **Loss**: `cross_entropy_loss(logits, target_ids)` with a max-subtracted log-softmax.
5. **Backward**: compute gradients for all parameters.
6. **Update**: `block.ffn.W1 -= lr * gW1` and the same for each tensor.
7. **Schedule**: GPT-2 warms up over 2,000 steps, then cosine decay.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Model repeats passages verbatim | Duplicates in the data | MinHash dedup, about 38% of web data |
| Output has HTML tags | Raw web text | Strip HTML before training |
| Docs leak into each other | Packed docs share attention | Use a block-diagonal mask |
| Sequence utilization below 90% | Padding waste | Pack docs with EOS between them |
| English score below 0.8 confidence | Not clean English | Filter the document out |
| Model diverges early | High learning rate at start | Warm up the learning rate |
| `exp` overflows to infinity | Large logits | Subtract the max before exp |
| Gradients vanish near block 1 | No residual path | Add `x + sublayer(x)` |

## GPT-2 Small numbers
type: concepts
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md

- **Total**: 124,438,272 parameters with weight tying.
- **Token embeddings**: (50257, 768) is 38,597,376.
- **Per block**: 7,080,960. Attention 2,359,296 and FFN 4,718,592.
- **Heads**: 12 heads of 64 dims. FFN goes 768 to 3,072.
- **Weight tying**: the head reuses the token embedding. Saves 38M.
- **KV cache**: 18,432 values per token. About 75MB at 1024 tokens in FP32.
- **Init**: weights use a 0.02 standard deviation.

## Use scaling laws to decide
type: tips
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md

- Below 20 tokens per base-model param, expect a fine-tune to saturate.
- When inference takes most of the budget, pick a smaller model trained longer.
- Beyond 1000× Chinchilla-optimal, log-loss changes become noise.
- Plan budgets against continuous loss. Benchmark jumps are often scorer artifacts.
- Better data, Muon and MoE shift the constants, not the shape.
- Expect a data ceiling: ~5 to 10 trillion high-quality English tokens.
- Llama 3 mix: 50% web, 25% code, 13% books and papers, 8% math, 4% multilingual.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/03-data-pipelines/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md

- **What is $E$?** The irreducible loss. The entropy of the data itself.
- **Why over-train?** You pay training cost once and inference cost forever.
- **Why not pad each doc?** Padding wastes compute. Pack docs and mask.
- **Why is decode slow?** It is memory-bound. Prefill is compute-bound.

## PII scrubbing
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/25-security-secrets-audit/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/25-security-secrets-audit/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/26-compliance-frameworks/docs/en.md

- **Order**: entity recognition, mask, consistent tokenization, optional reverse mapping.
- **Lab patterns**: `SSN`, `EMAIL` and `PHONE` regexes in `scrubber.scrub`.
- **Consistent tokens**: the same value maps to the same placeholder every time.
- **Regex and NER**: regex catches basic patterns. NER catches more. Use both.
- **When**: before the LLM call. Post-processing cleanup is not defensible.
- **Storage**: only redacted prompts plus consented opt-in raw.
- **Output guardrail**: regex scrub for leaked API key patterns.

## Webhook receiver path
type: flow
from: projects/signed-webhook-inbox/solution/main.go, projects/signed-webhook-inbox/README.md

1. **ReadDelivery**: needs POST, a valid `X-Delivery-ID` and an integer `X-Timestamp`. Else 400.
2. **Verify**: rejects a timestamp outside the 5 minute window with 401.
3. **Verify**: compares the `v1=` HMAC-SHA256 of timestamp, ID and body with `hmac.Equal`. Else 401.
4. **Accept**: writes with fsync and an atomic hard link. A new delivery returns 202.
5. **Retry**: the same ID with the same body returns 200.
6. **Conflict**: the same ID with a different body returns 409.
7. **Replay**: an explicit `--run` ID writes one processing receipt. A second replay reuses it.

title: Self-Taught Reasoning and Self-Improvement
subtitle: Generate, grade, keep, retrain. STaR, GRPO, AlphaEvolve and DGM loops, their numbers, and the evaluator traps.
markdown:
## Core ideas
type: concepts
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/04-darwin-godel-machine/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/07-recursive-self-improvement/docs/en.md

- **STaR**: fine-tune on own rationales that reach correct answers. Repeat.
- **Rationalization**: give the correct answer as a hint on failed problems.
- **Constitutional AI**: the model critiques and revises against written principles.
- **GRPO**: PPO with no value function. The group is the baseline.
- **AlphaEvolve**: LLM edits programs. A machine-checkable evaluator scores them.
- **DGM**: the agent edits its own scaffolding. A benchmark scores it.
- **RSI**: system `S_n` proposes the edit that makes `S_{n+1}`.
- **Answer-conditioned gradient**: the loop rewards final answers, not steps.

## One recipe: generator plus evaluator
type: architecture
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/04-darwin-godel-machine/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md

```arch
node | gen | 1,1 | Generator | LLM, policy or agent | model
node | cand | 2,1 | Candidates | G samples or variants |
node | eval | 3,1 | Evaluator | rule, test or benchmark | process
node | arch | 3,2 | Archive | MAP-elites, score keyed | store
node | train | 1,2 | Retrain or parent | SFT, GRPO or mutate | gpu
node | human | 2,2 | Human data | small fraction | client
edge | gen | cand | sample
edge | cand | eval | score
edge | eval | arch | keep best
edge | arch | train | select
edge | train | gen | next round
edge | human | train |
```

## STaR loop
type: flow
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/code/main.py

1. **Model**: samples a reasoning trace plus answer for each problem.
2. **Filter**: keeps the trace only if the final answer is correct.
3. **Rationalize**: on failed problems, hints the correct answer and samples again.
4. **Fine-tune**: trains on the kept and rationalized traces.
5. **Repeat**: the next round uses the new model.
6. **V-STaR**: trains a DPO verifier on correct and incorrect traces. Picks best-of-N.

## GRPO in the code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/code/main.py

```python
def group_relative_advantage(rewards: list[float]) -> np.ndarray:
    r = np.array(rewards, dtype=float)
    if r.std() < 1e-8:  # same reward for all: no signal
        return np.zeros_like(r)
    return (r - r.mean()) / (r.std() + 1e-8)  # z-score in the group

ratios = np.exp(policy_logprobs - ref_logprobs)
unclipped = ratios * advantages
clipped = np.clip(ratios, 1 - clip_eps, 1 + clip_eps) * advantages
policy_loss = -np.minimum(unclipped, clipped).mean()  # PPO clipped surrogate
kl = (ref_logprobs - policy_logprobs).mean()
total_loss = policy_loss + beta * kl  # KL to the reference stays
```

## STaR family side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/docs/en.md

| Factor | STaR | STaR + rationalization | V-STaR | Quiet-STaR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Training signal | keep (rationale, answer) if correct | above + correct-answer hinted retries | STaR + DPO verifier from both classes | per-token rationale + mixing weight |
| Inference cost | 1x | 1x | Nx (best-of-N) | 1.5-3x |
| Data waste | discards all incorrect rationales | less | minimal | minimal |
| Failure mode | shortcut rationales | rationalized rationales may be implausible | verifier can reinforce confident wrongness | still answer-conditioned gradient |

## Code search and self-edit loops
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/code/main.py, phases/15-autonomous-systems/04-darwin-godel-machine/docs/en.md

| Factor | AlphaEvolve | Darwin Godel Machine | Godel Machine (2003) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edit target | A program in a database | The agent scaffolding | Any self-modification |
| Evaluator | correctness + benchmark | SWE-bench / Polyglot | Formal proof |
| Acceptance rule | Score beats the cell incumbent | empirical score delta + archive | formal proof of net benefit |
| Example win | 48-mul 4x4 matmul | 20% → 50% SWE-bench | no known non-trivial instance |
| Failure mode | Reward hacking on a weak evaluator | accepts reward-hacked variants | never triggers |

type: troubleshooting
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/04-darwin-godel-machine/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/07-recursive-self-improvement/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Reward std falls to zero | Mode collapse | Stop the run |
| Lost diversity after 3-5 rounds | Self-generated data is narrower | Mix in fresh human data |
| Advantage zero for a prompt | Same reward in the whole group | Skip the prompt |
| Good in distribution, OOD breaks | Shortcut rationales kept | Process rewards and held-out OOD eval |
| Low train MSE, loose test MSE | Train-only evaluator | Held-out inputs made at eval time |
| Reported score above true score | Agent edits its scorer | Evaluator firewall |
| Gap C - A crosses the threshold | Capability rate above alignment rate | Pause for human review |

## Use X when
type: tips
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md

- Pure CAI: subjective behavior such as tone, safety and refusal style.
- GRPO + ORM: verifiable tasks with sparse and binary reward.
- DPO on self-generated pairs: constitution makes pairs, DPO trains.
- Full RLHF: multi-objective tradeoffs a rule cannot express.
- AlphaEvolve: only where the evaluator is fast, deterministic and hard to game.

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/15-autonomous-systems/02-star-family-reasoning/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/04-darwin-godel-machine/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/07-recursive-self-improvement/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md

- **STaR gain on GSM8K?** GPT-J went from 5.8% to 10.7%.
- **DGM gains?** SWE-bench 20.0% → 50.0%, Polyglot 14.2% → 30.7%.
- **Alignment faking rate?** 12% of basic tests, up to 78% after training it away.
- **Can self-improvement add a capability?** No. It amplifies signal already in the model.
- **Healthy run curves?** Mean reward up, std stable, KL bounded.

## Glossary
type: glossary
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/09-constitutional-ai-self-improvement/docs/en.md, phases/15-autonomous-systems/03-alphaevolve-evolutionary-coding/docs/en.md

- **ORM**: Outcome Reward Model. One reward on the final answer.
- **PRM**: Process Reward Model. One reward for each step.
- **RLAIF**: RL from AI Feedback. PPO or DPO on model preferences.
- **SL-CAI**: stage 1 of CAI. SFT on (prompt, revised) pairs.
- **MAP-elites**: grid keyed by feature vectors. Best variant per cell.

title: Self-Supervised Vision, CLIP and Retrieval
subtitle: Pretrain without labels, align images and text, classify zero-shot, shape embeddings and search them. PyTorch.
markdown:
## Families and models
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/docs/en.md

- **Contrastive (SimCLR, MoCo, CLIP)**: pull two views together. Push the rest of the batch away.
- **Teacher-student (DINO, BYOL, iBOT)**: the student matches an EMA teacher. No negatives.
- **Masked (MAE, BEiT, SimMIM)**: mask 75% of patches. Reconstruct the pixels.
- **CLIP**: image and text towers in one space. 400M web pairs, no labels.
- **SigLIP**: per-pair sigmoid. No all-gather. Trains better at small batches.
- **Linear probe**: frozen encoder plus one linear layer. Measures feature quality.
- **Probe top-1**: SimCLR ~71%, DINO ~77%, MAE ~76%, DINOv2 ~86%.
- **Category or instance retrieval**: off-the-shelf embeddings work for category. Instance needs metric learning.

## CLIP two towers
type: architecture
from: phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/docs/en.md

```arch
node | img | 1,1 | Image | batch of N | client
node | ienc | 2,1 | Image encoder | ViT or ResNet | model
node | inorm | 3,1 | L2 normalise | (N, D)
node | txt | 1,2 | Caption | N captions | client
node | tenc | 2,2 | Text encoder | transformer | model
node | tnorm | 3,2 | L2 normalise | (N, D)
node | sim | 4,1 | Similarity S | N x N, over tau
node | loss | 4,2 | Symmetric CE | (i2t + t2i) / 2
edge | img | ienc |
edge | ienc | inorm |
edge | txt | tenc |
edge | tenc | tnorm |
edge | inorm | sim |
edge | tnorm | sim |
edge | sim | loss | diagonal targets
```

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/docs/en.md

- **InfoNCE**: $-\log \frac{\exp(\mathrm{sim}(z_i, z_j)/\tau)}{\sum_{k \ne i} \exp(\mathrm{sim}(z_i, z_k)/\tau)}$
- **CLIP matrix**: $S_{ij} = \cos(f(x_i), g(y_j)) / \tau$. Shape N x N.
- **CLIP loss**: CE over rows plus CE over columns, divided by 2.
- **SigLIP**: $\log(1 + \exp(-y_{ij} \, \mathrm{sim}_{ij}))$ per pair, with $y_{ij} = \pm 1$.
- **DINO EMA**: $\theta_t \leftarrow m \, \theta_t + (1 - m) \, \theta_s$
- **Triplet**: $\max(0, \lVert f(a) - f(p) \rVert^2 - \lVert f(a) - f(n) \rVert^2 + \mathrm{margin})$
- **Cosine and L2**: $\lVert a - b \rVert^2 = 2 - 2 \cos(a, b)$ for unit vectors.
- **Recall@K**: fraction of queries with one correct match in the top K.

## InfoNCE and MAE masking
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/code/main.py

```python
def info_nce(z1, z2, tau=0.1):                   # z1, z2 L2-normalised
    N, D = z1.shape
    z = torch.cat([z1, z2], dim=0)               # (2N, D)
    sim = z @ z.T / tau                          # (2N, 2N)
    mask = torch.eye(2 * N, dtype=torch.bool, device=z.device)
    sim = sim.masked_fill(mask, float("-inf"))   # no self match
    targets = torch.cat([torch.arange(N, 2 * N), torch.arange(0, N)]).to(z.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(sim, targets)
num_patches = 196
visible, masked = random_mask_indices(num_patches, mask_ratio=0.75)  # keep 25%
```

## CLIP loss and zero-shot
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/code/main.py

```python
sim = logit_scale * image_emb @ text_emb.T       # (N, N)
targets = torch.arange(N, device=sim.device)     # match on the diagonal
l_i = F.cross_entropy(sim, targets)              # image to text
l_t = F.cross_entropy(sim.T, targets)            # text to image
loss = (l_i + l_t) / 2                           # random init: near log(N)
i = F.normalize(model.image_proj(image_feats), dim=-1)
t = F.normalize(model.text_proj(class_text_feats), dim=-1)
pred = (i @ t.T).argmax(dim=-1)                  # one class per image
```

## Triplet loss and recall@K
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/code/main.py

```python
def triplet_loss(anchor, positive, negative, margin=0.2):
    d_ap = F.pairwise_distance(anchor, positive, p=2)
    d_an = F.pairwise_distance(anchor, negative, p=2)
    return F.relu(d_ap - d_an + margin).mean()
pos_idx, neg_idx = semi_hard_negatives(emb, y)   # hardest positive, semi-hard negative
loss = triplet_loss(emb, emb[pos_idx], emb[neg_idx])
sim = query_emb @ gallery_emb.T                  # cosine on unit vectors
_, top_k = sim.topk(k, dim=-1)
matches = (gallery_labels[top_k] == query_labels[:, None]).any(dim=-1)
matches.float().mean().item()                    # recall@K
```

## Zero-shot classification
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/outputs/skill-clip-zero-shot.md

1. **Prompts**: write "a photo of a {class}" for each class.
2. **Ensemble**: average many templates per class for 1-3% more top-1.
3. **Text tower**: encode the prompts. `T` has shape (C, d).
4. **Image tower**: encode the image. `I` has shape (1, d).
5. **Normalise**: make both sides unit length.
6. **Score**: `I @ T.T` gives shape (1, C).
7. **Predict**: argmax gives the class. Warn when the top-1 score is below 0.2.

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/code/main.py

| Task | Code |

| Contrastive loss on two views | `info_nce(z1, z2, tau=0.1)` |
| DINO teacher with centring | `DinoHead().teacher(x, temp=0.04)` |
| CLIP symmetric loss | `clip_loss(i, t, logit_scale)` |
| Zero-shot labels | `zero_shot_classify(model, image_feats, class_text_feats, class_names)` |
| Mine semi-hard negatives | `semi_hard_negatives(emb, labels, margin=0.2)` |
| Recall at K | `recall_at_k(query_emb, gallery_emb, query_labels, gallery_labels, k=1)` |
| Symmetric InfoNCE in pure Python | `infonce_loss(S)` |

## Defaults and numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/code/main.py

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SimCLR `tau` | 0.1 | Lower is sharper, needs more negatives |
| CLIP `tau` init | 0.07 | Learned. `logit_scale` starts at ln(1/0.07) |
| SimCLR batch | 512-8192 | Many negatives per positive |
| MAE `mask_ratio` | 0.75 | BERT masks 15% of tokens |
| MAE decoder | 8-layer, 512-dim | Encoder sees visible patches only |
| DINO EMA m | 0.996 | Teacher is an EMA of the student |
| DINO teacher `temp` | 0.04 | Student `temp` 0.1 |
| Triplet `margin` | 0.2 | Same margin for semi-hard mining |

## Pick a FAISS index
type: command-table
from: phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `IndexFlatIP` | Exact inner product. Cosine on 100k vectors |
| `IndexFlatL2` | Exact L2, brute force, no training |
| `IndexIVFFlat` | K cells, searches the closest few. Needs training. 10M |
| `IndexHNSW` | Graph index. Fastest for many queries. Large index |
| `IndexIVFPQ` | Adds product quantisation. 100M+ vectors |
| DINOv2 + FAISS | General visual retrieval, off-the-shelf |
| CLIP + FAISS | Queries are text |
| Fine-tuned DINOv2 + FAISS | Instance retrieval, re-ID, e-commerce |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/20-image-retrieval-metric/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| InfoNCE fails at batch 32 | Too few negatives | Batch 512-8192 or a momentum queue |
| DINO gives a constant vector | Representation collapse | Centre and sharpen the teacher |
| Masked task too easy | Mask ratio too low | Mask 75% of patches |
| High recall@10, low recall@1 | Noisy ranking | Longer fine-tune or re-rank |
| Nearest neighbours change | Cosine and L2 mixed | Match the embedding training |
| Instance search misses | Off-the-shelf features | Fine-tune with metric learning |
| Triplet loss near 0 | Easy triplets | Semi-hard mining |
| Softmax loss slow on many GPUs | All-gather of embeddings | Use the sigmoid loss |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/17-self-supervised-vision/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/18-open-vocab-clip/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/02-clip-contrastive-pretraining/docs/en.md

- **Why 75% for MAE but 15% for BERT?** Image patches have low entropy. Neighbours give the pixels away.
- **InfoNCE on random pairs?** About log(2N - 1). That is 3.4 for 16 pairs.
- **CLIP loss at random init?** Close to log(N). For N = 8 it is 2.08.
- **Linear probe or fine-tune?** Fine-tuning adds 2-5 points. The probe measures the features only.
- **DINOv2 embedding?** `outputs.last_hidden_state[:, 0]`, the CLS token, 768-dim.
- **Zero-shot, probe or fine-tune?** A probe beats zero-shot in domain. Fine-tuning can hurt zero-shot transfer.

title: NER, POS Tagging and Coreference
subtitle: BIO tags, CRF and HMM taggers, Viterbi, dependency parses, coreference clusters and entity linking to a KB.
markdown:
## Extraction pipeline
type: architecture
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md

```arch
node | text | 1,1 | Document | | client
node | ner | 2,1 | NER | BIO token labels to spans | model
node | coref | 3,1 | Coref | mention clusters | model
node | cand | 3,2 | Candidate generation | alias index, 10-30 per mention | store
node | dis | 2,2 | Disambiguation | prior + context or embeddings | process
node | kb | 1,2 | KB id per entity | or NIL | store
edge | text | ner | tokens
edge | ner | coref | mentions
edge | coref | cand | each mention
edge | cand | dis | candidates
edge | dis | kb | top-1
```

## Core ideas
type: concepts
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md

- **BIO**: `B-X` begins, `I-X` continues, `O` is outside. `New B-GPE`, `York I-GPE`.
- **BILOU**: adds `L-X` (last) and `U-X` (unit) for cleaner boundaries.
- **HMM**: $P = \prod_i P(t_i \mid t_{i-1}) \, P(w_i \mid t_i)$. Transition times emission.
- **CRF**: discriminative. Mixes word shape, case and neighbor features. Enforces valid tag sequences.
- **Viterbi**: dynamic programming for the best tag sequence over the tag lattice.
- **Dependency parse**: each word has one head and a relation label.
- **Mention types**: named entity, nominal, pronominal, appositive.
- **Prior + context**: `P(entity | mention) × context-similarity(entity, text)`.

## Rule-based pronoun resolver
type: flow
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/code/main.py

1. **extract_mentions**: capitalized spans, pronouns by lookup, definite "the X" phrases.
2. **resolve**: for each pronoun, take the earlier named and nominal mentions.
3. **agreement_score**: +1 for number match. Gender clash costs 2.
4. **recency_score**: closer candidates score higher.
5. **resolve**: link the candidate with the highest sum.
6. **clusters**: union-find over the links gives one cluster per entity.

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
span: 2
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/code/main.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/code/main.py, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Spans to BIO labels | `spans_to_bio(tokens, spans)` |
| BIO labels back to spans | `bio_to_spans(tokens, labels)` |
| Capitalization shape | `word_shape(word)` |
| Gazetteer baseline | `rule_based_ner(tokens)` |
| Most-frequent-tag baseline | `predict_mft(tokens, word_best, default_tag)` |
| Train the bigram HMM | `train_hmm(examples, alpha=0.01)` |
| Decode tags | `viterbi(tokens, transitions, emissions, tags, vocab, alpha=0.01)` |
| Link a mention | `disambiguate(mention, context, use_prior=True)` |

## CRF and transformer NER
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md

```python
crf = sklearn_crfsuite.CRF(algorithm="lbfgs",
    c1=0.1, c2=0.1,                   # L1 and L2 regularization
    max_iterations=100,
    all_possible_transitions=True)    # learns I-ORG after O is unlikely
X_train = [to_features(s) for s in sentences_tokenized]
crf.fit(X_train, bio_labels_train)    # ~84 F1 on CoNLL-2003
ner = pipeline("ner", model="dslim/bert-base-NER",
               aggregation_strategy="simple")  # merges B-X, I-X into spans
print(ner("Apple sued Google over its iPhone in the US."))
```

## spaCy: tags, parse, entities, clusters
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md

```python
nlp = spacy.load("en_core_web_sm")
doc = nlp("The cats were running at 3pm.")
for token in doc:
    print(token.tag_, token.pos_, token.dep_, token.head.text)  # Penn, UD, relation
for ent in doc.ents:
    print(f"{ent.text:20s} {ent.label_}")   # iPhone comes out ORG in sm
nlp = spacy.load("en_coreference_web_trf")   # experimental model
doc = nlp("<text>")                          # rerun with the coref model
for cluster in doc._.coref_clusters:
    print(cluster, "->", [m.text for m in cluster])
```

## Numbers to expect
type: defaults
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Most-frequent-tag on Brown | ~85% | The floor for any tagger |
| Bigram HMM on Brown | ~93% | Gain comes from transitions |
| CRF with features | ~97% | BiLSTM-CRF or transformer ~98%+ |
| Annotator agreement, PTB | 97% | Past 98% is likely overfitting |
| Tagsets | 36 | PTB has 36 tags. UD has 17 |
| Coref SOTA, CoNLL-2012 | ~83 F1 | Mean of MUC, B³, CEAF |
| Candidates per mention | 10-30 | From the alias index |
| Classical NER latency | 50ms | Under it, classical NER wins |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| CoNLL model fails on contracts | Domain shift | Fine-tune on your domain |
| ORG and FACILITY overlap | BIO cannot nest spans | Span-based or multi-pass NER |
| Long entity split in two | Token-level labels | `aggregation_strategy` or post-process |
| F1 looks too high | Token-level F1 | Entity-level F1 with `seqeval` |
| Every mention its own cluster | Singleton explosion | Check MUC, B³ and CEAF together |
| Coref drops on long docs | ~15 F1 loss over 2,000 tokens | Sliding window plus merge |
| Wrong famous entity picked | Popularity bias | Domain fine-tune, check NIL |
| EL recall drops | NER cut the span short | Fix mention boundaries upstream |

## Use X when
type: qa
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md

- **Classical NER or an LLM?** Classical under 50ms, at 98%+ F1, or on-prem. Else start with an LLM zero-shot baseline.
- **PTB or UD?** PTB for English-only legacy pipelines. UD for multilingual work.
- **Which parser?** spaCy for most production, stanza for multilingual, trankit for top UD accuracy.
- **Which EL method?** BLINK or REL for English Wikipedia. Exact-match prior for the lowest latency.
- **LLM coref?** Easy cases only. It over-merges and drops mentions in long docs.

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/06-named-entity-recognition/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md

- **NER**: named entity recognition. Label token spans with types.
- **CRF**: Conditional Random Field. Models label transitions.
- **PTB / UD**: Penn Treebank and Universal Dependencies tagsets.
- **EL**: entity linking. Map a mention to one KB entry.
- **NIL**: no KB entry matches the mention.
- **CoNLL F1**: mean of MUC, B³ and CEAF-φ4 F1.
- **Cataphora**: the pronoun comes before its referent.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/25-entity-linking/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/24-coreference-resolution/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/07-pos-tagging-parsing/docs/en.md

- Report mention recall and disambiguation accuracy. 99% on 80% recall is an 80% pipeline.
- Merge coref clusters into NER entities. Emit one KB id per entity, not per mention.
- Constrain LLM entity linking to valid KB ids.
- Test noun-verb ambiguity (`saw`, `book`, `can`) on 20 sampled outputs.

title: Serving Engines Compared
subtitle: vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM and llama.cpp side by side. Schedulers, KV reuse, precision, offload and the pick.

## Engines side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/04-vllm-serving-internals, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/07-tensorrt-llm-blackwell, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection

| Factor | vLLM | SGLang | TRT-LLM | llama.cpp |

| Core idea | PagedAttention, continuous batching, chunked prefill | RadixAttention, cache-aware scheduler | NVFP4 weights, FP8 KV, MTP | Fastest on CPU, widest model support |
| Scheduling | V1 scheduler, FCFS | Depth-first dispatch, branch-level LRU | Disaggregated prefill/decode | Full control over threading |

| Weight format | HF safetensors | HF safetensors | Compiled per GPU SKU | GGUF |
| Weak spot | Prefix-heavy traffic | Unique prompts, back to vLLM level | No AMD, no Intel, no ARM | Not the prod stage of the pipeline |

## Use each engine when
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/28-self-hosted-serving-selection, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/07-tensorrt-llm-blackwell, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/18-vllm-production-stack-lmcache

- **vLLM**: general chat, 100+ users, AMD GPUs or mixed hardware.
- **SGLang**: agents, RAG and chat that share long prefixes.
- **TRT-LLM**: NVIDIA-only infra and cost-dominant work on Blackwell.
- **llama.cpp**: CPU, edge or Apple Silicon.
- **Ollama**: one user on a dev laptop. Not shared production.
- **TGI**: existing deployments only. Maintenance mode since Dec 11, 2025.
- **Native CPU offload**: one engine has HBM pressure.
- **LMCache**: several engines share prefixes, or preemption is heavy.

## The vLLM scheduler loop
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/04-vllm-serving-internals/docs/en.md

```python
while True:
    finished = [s for s in RUNNING if s.is_done()]
    for s in finished: release_blocks(s); RUNNING.remove(s)  # free blocks
    while WAITING and have_free_blocks_for(WAITING[0]):  # admit on free KV
        s = WAITING.pop(0)
        allocate_initial_blocks(s)
        RUNNING.append(s)
    batch = []
    for s in RUNNING:
        if s.in_prefill:
            batch.append(next_prefill_chunk(s))  # e.g. 512 tokens
        else:
            batch.append(decode_one_token(s))  # 1 token
    run_forward(batch)  # one fused GPU call
```

## One request in the radix tree
type: flow
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention/docs/en.md

1. **Request**: system prompt plus "Context: <doc A>" plus "Question: Carol".
2. **Scheduler**: walks the tree. The system prefix matches, 124 blocks reused.
3. **Scheduler**: the doc A branch matches, 31 blocks reused.
4. **Allocator**: gives fresh blocks only to "Question: Carol", 4 blocks.
5. **Result**: prefill of 4 blocks, not 160. About 40x less prefill.
6. **Eviction**: removes whole branches from the shortest-used leaves.

from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/18-vllm-production-stack-lmcache/docs/en.md


## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/04-vllm-serving-internals, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/07-tensorrt-llm-blackwell, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/18-vllm-production-stack-lmcache

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Decode stalls during a long prompt | Prefill freezes decode | Chunked prefill. P99 ITL ~50 ms to ~15 ms |
| Hit rate 7% on shared prompts | Dynamic content in the prefix | Immutable parts first. 7% to 74% |
| 6.4x gain gone | Template order changes per request | Fix one component order |
| HBM 100%, same prompt prefilled again | Preemption evicts KV | Native CPU offload or LMCache |
| 3-5% slower with LMCache | Small HBM pressure | Turn LMCache off |
| Accuracy drops after NVFP4 | FP4 weights on reasoning tasks | FP8 weights plus FP4 activations |
| Attention collapses at FP4 KV | KV needs dynamic range | Keep KV cache in FP8 |
| Features break together | Combination not in the matrix | Check the matrix for your version |

## Q&A
type: qa
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/04-vllm-serving-internals, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/07-tensorrt-llm-blackwell, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/18-vllm-production-stack-lmcache

- **Why is FCFS wrong for prefix traffic?** It evicts the hot branch to admit a short-prefix request.
- **What does chunked prefill protect?** The TTFT tail and ITL, not mean throughput.
- **Where does the 7x TRT-LLM gap come from?** HBM bandwidth, NVFP4 weights, MTP and disaggregation.
- **LMCache for prompts under 1K tokens?** No. Transfer time is more than re-prefill.
- **Do you enable PagedAttention?** No flag. It is the only allocator vLLM ships.
- **Does vLLM reuse prefixes?** Yes, with `--enable-prefix-caching`. SGLang is radix-first.

## Glossary
type: glossary
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/04-vllm-serving-internals, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/06-sglang-radixattention, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/07-tensorrt-llm-blackwell, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/18-vllm-production-stack-lmcache

- **ITL**: inter-token latency. Time between two decode tokens.
- **TTFT**: first token time. Prefill plus queue plus network.
- **FCFS**: first-come first-served. Breaks prefix locality.
- **NVFP4**: NVIDIA 4-bit microscaling format for weights and activations.
- **MTP**: multi-token prediction. TRT-LLM integrated draft.
- **MXFP8**: microscaling FP8 variant on Blackwell Tensor Cores.
- **Connector API**: vLLM 0.9.0+ pluggable KV store interface.
- **Preemption**: KV cache shuffle when HBM is full.

## Start a server

```bash
export HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1   # no Hub contact once the models are cached
```

## Requests and checks
type: task-table

from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/5-1-sglang-benchmark-serving.md

## Defaults that matter
type: defaults
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/r-1-flags-and-defaults.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-2-the-scheduler-loop-and-schedule-policy.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-3-admission-and-retraction.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-5-eviction-policies-and-hicache.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/6-4-sgl-model-gateway.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `--schedule-policy` | `fcfs` | `lpm` is the paper's order, not the default |
| `--schedule-conservativeness` | 1.0 | Raise it when the log shows retractions |
| `--radix-eviction-policy` | `lru` | Change only after a measured hit rate |

## Fix these errors
type: troubleshooting
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-2-mem-fraction-static-and-startup-sizing.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-3-admission-and-retraction.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/6-1-tp-size-dp-size-and-attn-dp-size.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/4-1-forwardmode-and-cuda-graphs.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-4-prefix-friendly-prompts.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `RuntimeError: [METAL] Command buffer execution failed` at 32 requests | Pool sized at 87 percent of free memory | Pass `--mem-fraction-static 0.4` and restart |
| Median TTFT near 28 s with free GPU memory | Admission queues requests for a full pool | Raise `--schedule-conservativeness` or lower `--max-running-requests` |
| `KV cache pool is full. Retract requests.` in a loop | The forecast is too bold | Raise `--schedule-conservativeness` and send realistic `max_new_tokens` |
| `RuntimeError: The memory capacity is unbalanced` | One TP card shares memory with other pods | Free the other card and restart. No flag disables the check |
| `cuda graph: False` on decode lines under load | Decode batch above the graph limit | Set `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` to peak concurrency |
| `ambiguous option: --cuda-graph-max-bs` | The flag was split at v0.5.22 | Use `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill` |
| `#cached-token: 0` on every repeat | Random ID at the start of the system prompt | Move the ID to the end or remove it |

## Tune in this order
type: flow
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/7-1-operating-sglang.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/5-1-sglang-benchmark-serving.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/6-1-tp-size-dp-size-and-attn-dp-size.md

1. **Measure**: run `sglang.benchmark.serving` at three caps with `--random-range-ratio 1.0`.
2. **Memory**: set `--mem-fraction-static` on any shared machine.
3. **Prompts**: put shared text first and keep request IDs out of the start.
4. **Cap**: set `--max-running-requests` at the knee you measured.
5. **Kernels**: change graph and attention settings one at a time.
6. **Parallelism**: add `--tp-size` or `--dp-size` only when one replica saturates.

## Numbers to watch
type: concepts
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/5-2-the-metrics-endpoint.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/1-3-what-the-server-does-with-your-request.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-5-streaming-stop-strings-and-the-openai-api.md

- **sglang:token_usage**: near 1.0 means the KV pool is full.
- **sglang:num_queue_reqs**: above 0 for minutes means the server is past its knee.
- **sglang:cache_hit_rate**: a gauge over one interval. Compute the rate from `sglang:prefill_effective_tokens_total`.
- **cached_tokens**: the count of prompt tokens reused from the cache.
- **Goodput**: requests per second that meet the TTFT and TPOT targets together.

## Incidents on record
type: concepts
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-2-the-scheduler-loop-and-schedule-policy.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/4-2-attention-backend.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/4-4-speculative-decoding.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-4-prefix-friendly-prompts.md

- **Issue #36889**: a Mamba cap set the request limit to 2, and only an info line said so.
- **Issue #17411**: a FlashInfer upgrade made Hopper decode seven times slower.
- **Issue #5274**: EAGLE-3 doubled batch-1 speed and cut concurrency 20 by a quarter.
- **Issue #35129**: removing a per-session hash raised the hit rate from 66.8 to 94.4 percent.

## Glossary
type: glossary
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/1-3-what-the-server-does-with-your-request.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-1-kv-bytes-per-token-and-the-kv-pool.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/6-2-moe-serving-deepep-and-eplb.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/6-3-prefill-decode-disaggregation.md

- **ITL**: inter-token latency, the gap between tokens.
- **MLA**: multi-head latent attention, a compact KV layout used by DeepSeek.
- **MoE**: mixture of experts, where each token uses a few experts.
- **EPLB**: expert placement load balancing across GPUs.
- **PD**: prefill-decode disaggregation, with prefill and decode on separate servers.

## Questions
type: qa
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-1-sglang-serve-and-the-three-processes.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/3-2-mem-fraction-static-and-startup-sizing.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/7-1-operating-sglang.md

- **Where do I look when time to first token is high and the GPU is idle?** Check the tokenizer process before the kernels.
- **Why does a bigger pool add no throughput?** The pool was never full at 64 users in our runs.
- **Should I deploy `latest`?** No. Pin a tag such as `v0.5.22`.

## Tips
type: tips
from: manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-5-streaming-stop-strings-and-the-openai-api.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/2-1-sglang-serve-and-the-three-processes.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/5-2-the-metrics-endpoint.md, manuals/sglang-101/sections/7-1-operating-sglang.md

- Start servers with `--enable-cache-report` and `--enable-metrics`.
- Read the pool size in the startup log before you size clients.
- Send SIGTERM to the main process only.
- Set `SGLANG_ENABLE_HEALTH_ENDPOINT_GENERATION=false` for liveness probes.

## Cooley-Tukey FFT, 8 points
type: architecture
from: phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md

```arch
node | x | 1,1 | x[0..7] | 8 samples
node | even | 2,1 | Even half | x[0,2,4,6]
node | odd | 2,2 | Odd half | x[1,3,5,7]
node | ek | 3,1 | E[0..3] | 4-pt FFT
node | ok | 3,2 | O[0..3] | 4-pt FFT
node | out | 4,1 | X[0..7] | E[k] +/- twiddle * O[k]
edge | x | even | split
edge | x | odd | split
edge | even | ek |
edge | odd | ok |
edge | ek | out | combine
edge | ok | out | twiddle
```

## Waveform to log-mel and MFCC
type: flow
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/code/main.py

1. **Frame**: cut 25 ms windows with a 10 ms hop. At 16 kHz that is 400 and 160 samples.
2. **Window**: multiply each frame by `hann(N)`. It tapers the edges to zero.
3. **STFT**: take the FFT magnitude of each frame. Shape is `(n_frames, n_freq_bins)`.
4. **Mel**: multiply by the triangular filterbank. 80 mels over 0 to 8 kHz is the ASR standard.
5. **Log**: `log(mel_spec + 1e-10)` compresses the dynamic range.
6. **MFCC**: apply `dct_ii` to each log-mel frame. Keep the first 13 coefficients.

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/01-math-foundations/19-complex-numbers/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/code/fourier.py, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md

## Spectra in NumPy and SciPy
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/01-math-foundations/19-complex-numbers/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md

```python
waveform, sr = sf.read("clip.wav", dtype="float32")  # float32 in [-1, 1]
spectrum = np.fft.fft(signal)
freqs = np.fft.fftfreq(256, d=1/256)  # frequency of each bin
power = np.abs(spectrum) ** 2  # power spectrum
window = windows.hann(256)  # from scipy.signal
result = fftconvolve(signal, kernel, mode='full')
frequencies, times, Zxx = stft(signal, fs=sample_rate, nperseg=256)
spectrogram = np.abs(Zxx) ** 2  # (n_frequencies, n_time_frames)
print(cmath.exp(1j * cmath.pi))  # Euler: close to -1
```

## Mel features from scratch
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/code/main.py

```python
def hz_to_mel(f):
    return 2595.0 * math.log10(1.0 + f / 700.0)
mag = stft_magnitude(signal, frame_len=400, hop=160)  # Hann + DFT per frame
fb = mel_filterbank(n_mels, n_fft, sr)  # 80 mels, n_fft=400 gives (80, 201)
mel_spec = apply_filterbank(cmag, fb)  # one weighted sum per mel bin
lm = log_transform(mel_spec)  # eps=1e-10
mfcc = dct_ii(lm[len(lm) // 2], 13)  # coefficient 0 is overall energy
```

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/01-math-foundations/19-complex-numbers/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md

- **Multiply**: $(a + bi)(c + di) = (ac - bd) + (ad + bc)i$. Magnitudes multiply, angles add.
- **Polar**: $r = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ and $\theta = \mathop{\mathrm{atan2}}(b, a)$.
- **Euler**: $e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i \sin\theta$. Multiply by it to rotate by $\theta$.
- **DFT**: $X[k] = \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} x[n] \, e^{-2\pi i k n/N}$.
- **Inverse DFT**: positive exponent and a $1/N$ factor. Reconstruction is exact.
- **Bins**: $f_k = k \cdot f_s / N$, resolution $f_s / N$, maximum $f_s / 2$.
- **Convolution theorem**: $x * h = \text{IFFT}(\text{FFT}(x) \cdot \text{FFT}(h))$.
- **Mel**: $m = 2595 \cdot \log_{10}(1 + f / 700)$.

type: command-table
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |

| 8 kHz | Telephony. Nyquist at 4 kHz kills consonants. Avoid for ASR |
| 16 kHz | ASR standard. A 10 s clip is 160,000 floats |
| 22.05 kHz | TTS vocoder training for older models |
| 24 kHz | Modern TTS |
| 44.1 kHz | CD audio, music |
| 48 kHz | Film, pro audio, high-fidelity TTS |

type: command-table
from: phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |

| Rectangular | No window. Side lobes -13 dB. Signal exactly periodic in N |
| Hann | 0.5 (1 - cos(2 pi n / (N-1))). -31 dB. General purpose |
| Hamming | 0.54 - 0.46 cos(2 pi n / (N-1)). -42 dB. Speech analysis |
| Blackman | Wide main lobe. -58 dB. Side lobe suppression is critical |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/01-audio-fundamentals/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Garbage output that looks like a model bug | Sample rate mismatch | Match sample rate first. 16 kHz mono float32 |
| 7 kHz tone peaks at 3 kHz | Aliasing above Nyquist | Low-pass filter before downsampling |
| Spurious high frequencies | Spectral leakage at the frame edges | Apply a Hann or Hamming window |
| Silent failure at inference | Mel count mismatch, 80 against 128 | Log the feature shape at both ends |
| Wrong input for Whisper | dB-mel, not log-mel | Feed log-mel |
| WER doubles in production | Normalization drift | Use the same normalization in training and inference |
| Flat spectrum in the last frames | Zero padding at the end | Pad symmetrically or replicate |
| FFT convolution wraps around | The DFT computes circular convolution | Zero-pad to N + M - 1 |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/01-math-foundations/19-complex-numbers/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md

- **Does zero-padding add resolution?** No. Resolution needs $T = 1 / \Delta f$ seconds of data.
- **Why keep only the first N/2 + 1 bins?** For real input, $X[N-k]$ is the conjugate of $X[k]$.
- **Why is i a rotation?** Multiply by i to turn 90 degrees. Two turns give $i^2 = -1$.
- **How does RoPE use this?** It rotates queries and keys. Relative position becomes an angle.
- **Why mel, not Hz?** People hear pitch on a log scale. 100 to 200 Hz sounds like 1000 to 2000 Hz.
- **What does Parseval say?** Energy is the same in the time and frequency domains.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/01-math-foundations/19-complex-numbers/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/20-fourier-transform/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/02-spectrograms-mel-features/docs/en.md

- Start with 80 log-mels unless you work on music.
- A larger FFT gives better frequency resolution and worse time resolution.
- Use a power of 2 length for the FFT. Zero-pad to the next power of 2.
- The N roots of unity have magnitude 1 and sum to zero.
- Check `idft(dft(x))` against x. It must match to machine precision.
- MFCC coefficient 0 encodes overall energy. Models usually drop it.

title: Speculative Decoding: Draft, EAGLE, MTP
subtitle: Draft and verify with no quality loss. Vanilla, Medusa, EAGLE-3 and MTP drafts, speedup math, vLLM config, gates.
markdown:
## Draft types side by side
type: comparison
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/18-multi-token-prediction/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/16-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md

| Factor | Vanilla draft | Medusa | EAGLE-3 | MTP (DeepSeek-V3) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Draft | Separate small LLM | Extra LM heads on verifier | Multi-layer feature fusion + TTT | 1 transformer block + projection |
| Trained when | Reuse an existing model | SFT stage on the verifier | Post-pre-training | During pre-training |
| Training cost | None | ~1B SFT tokens | ~60-200B tokens | About 10% slower pre-training |
| `α` | 0.55-0.70 | 0.65-0.75 | 0.88-0.92 | 0.80+ at depth 1 |
| Speedup | 1.8-2.3× | 2-3× | 3.5-6.5× | 1.8× |
| Second model | Yes | No | Tiny draft head | No, part of the model |
| Existing weights | Yes | Needs fine-tune | Yes | No, re-train |

## One speculative step
type: flow
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/16-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md

1. **Draft**: the cheap model $M_p$ proposes $N$ tokens with probabilities $p_1 \ldots p_N$.
2. **Verify**: the verifier $M_q$ runs once on prefix plus drafts. It returns $q_1 \ldots q_{N+1}$.
3. **Accept**: walk left to right. Accept with probability $\min(1, q_i(d_i) / p_i(d_i))$.
4. **Reject**: at the first rejection, sample from $(q_j - p_j)_+$ normalized. Discard later drafts.
5. **Bonus**: when all $N$ accept, sample one more token from $q_{N+1}$.
6. **Roll back**: set the KV cache to the accepted prefix length.
7. **Result**: output is identically distributed to the verifier alone.

## The loop in code
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/code/main.py

```python
for i, d in enumerate(drafts):
    u = rng.random()
    ratio = q_prob / p_prob if p_prob > 0 else float("inf")   # q verifier, p draft
    if u < min(1.0, ratio):
        emitted.append(d)
        kv.extend(1)   # accepted: cache grows by one
    else:
        correction = sample(residual(q, p), rng)   # (q - p)+ renormalized
        emitted.append(correction)
        kv.truncate_to(prefix_len + len(emitted))   # KV rollback
        return emitted, 1   # one verifier forward
bonus = sample(q, rng)   # all N accepted: free token
emitted.append(bonus)
```

## Speedup math
type: concepts
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/25-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/18-multi-token-prediction/docs/en.md

- **Tokens per verify**: $\mathbb{E}[\text{accepted}] = \frac{1 - \alpha^{N+1}}{1 - \alpha}$
- **Example**: `α = 0.8, K = 4` gives 3.36 tokens per forward.
- **Wall time per token**: `(N * c + 1) / E[accepted]`, with `c = cost(draft) / cost(verifier)`.
- **Biggest lever**: acceptance rate `α` moves the speedup more than draft length `N`.
- **Production form**: `S(alpha, K) = (1 + K*alpha) / (1 + verify_overhead)`
- **Break-even**: `alpha_breakeven = verify_overhead / K`. It rises with concurrency.
- **MTP loss**: $L_{\text{MTP}} = \frac{\lambda}{D} \sum_{k=1}^{D} L_k$, `lambda` 0.3 then 0.1.

type: defaults
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/25-speculative-decoding/code/main.py, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/code/main.py

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/16-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/25-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| No speedup after deploy | Spec decode is opt-in | Set `speculative_config` explicitly |
| Mean ITL drops, P99 ITL rises | Rejected drafts take two passes | Watch P99 ITL, tune before ship |
| `α` below 0.55 on traffic | Draft trained on general data | Train a domain draft or disable |
| `α` collapses | High-temperature creative sampling | Fall back to plain decode |
| No gain at high concurrency | Batching already fills the FLOPs | Measure break-even at that concurrency |
| Cache wrong after a reject | Entries past `j-1` stay written | Truncate to the accepted prefix |
| Gain is small on a tiny model | Draft not much cheaper | Skip spec decode under 3B |

## Use each draft when
type: tips
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/16-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/18-multi-token-prediction/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md

- Use a vanilla draft for a fast prototype with no training.
- Use Medusa heads when you can fine-tune the verifier.
- Use EAGLE-2 or EAGLE-3 in production for maximum speed.
- Use lookahead when you want no draft, no training and no extra params. Expect 1.3 to 1.6×.
- Use MTP when you control pre-training and hidden size is at least 4096.
- Use spec decode for chat latency, code and JSON output, and long generations.
- Skip it for outputs under 50 tokens and batch-1 offline jobs.

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/18-multi-token-prediction/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/14-speculative-decoding-server/docs/en.md

- **α**: acceptance rate. Per-token chance that the verifier accepts a draft.
- **K or N**: draft length. Typical 4-8 tokens per target forward.
- **EAGLE**: tiny draft conditioned on the verifier's hidden states.
- **TTT**: training-time test. The draft sees its own outputs during training.
- **MTP**: multi-token prediction. A module predicts a token `k` positions ahead.
- **P99 ITL**: the tail metric to watch after you enable spec decode. Not P50.
- **HPA**: autoscales the server on queue wait, not CPU.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/16-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/15-speculative-decoding-eagle3/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/18-multi-token-prediction/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/05-eagle3-speculative-decoding/docs/en.md

- **Does spec decode change output quality?** No. The output matches the verifier distribution exactly.
- **Why does decode leave room for this?** Decode is memory-bound. Compute sits idle.
- **How do I read alpha in vLLM V1?** Divide `spec_decode_metrics.accepted_tokens_per_request` by draft length.
- **What did EAGLE-3 change?** It drops the feature loss and trains with training-time test.
- **Why is MTP a good draft?** Sequential modules keep the causal chain, like a decoder.

## Multi-agent triage
type: flow
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/23-sre-for-ai/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/23-sre-for-ai/code/main.py

1. **Supervisor**: breaks the incident into sub-queries.
2. **Log agent**: log search. Finds the most common error pattern.
3. **Metric agent**: PromQL. Finds the GPU memory spike before the errors.
4. **Runbook agent**: doc retrieval. Matches a known runbook.
5. **Supervisor**: groups root causes. Two or more agents in agreement means confidence.
6. **Human**: approves or redirects the hypothesis and evidence.
7. **Action**: a narrow safe action only, for example restart pod.

```python
def score(self) -> float:
    recency_w = max(0.0, 1.0 - self.recency_mins / 60.0)  # 0 after 60 min
    path_w = 1.0 / (1 + self.path_len)  # short graph path wins
    return (recency_w * 0.35 +
```

title: Structured Outputs and Constrained Decoding
subtitle: Get valid JSON every time. Schemas, strict mode, logit masks, validators, retries and the output guard project.
markdown:
## Output guard pipeline
type: architecture
from: projects/json-schema-output-guard/solution/main.ts, projects/json-schema-output-guard/README.md

```arch
node | gen | 1,1 | generate | feedback, attempt | model
node | parse | 2,1 | parseJSON | 100_000 byte cap | process
node | check | 2,2 | checkSchema | preflight, depth 32 | process
node | val | 3,1 | validate | Issue[] with paths | process
node | ok | 4,1 | accepted | value plus trace | client
node | rep | 3,2 | repair | maxAttempts budget | queue
node | out | 4,2 | exhausted | every attempt in trace | client
edge | gen | parse | raw string
edge | check | val | schema
edge | parse | val | value
edge | val | ok | no issues
edge | val | rep | issues
edge | rep | gen | Issue[]
edge | rep | out | budget spent
```

## One constrained decoding step
type: flow
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/20-structured-outputs-constrained-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/20-structured-outputs-constrained-decoding/code/main.py

1. **Model**: emits a logit vector over the full vocabulary (~100k tokens).
2. **FSM**: `fsm.valid_tokens(state, tokenizer)` lists the tokens that keep an accepting path.
3. **Mask**: `mask_logits` sets every other logit to `float("-inf")`.
4. **Sample**: softmax puts all probability on valid tokens. Pick one.
5. **Advance**: `fsm.transition(state, tok)`. Stop when `fsm.is_accept(state)`.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/20-structured-outputs-constrained-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/13-tools-and-protocols/04-structured-output/docs/en.md, projects/json-schema-output-guard/README.md, projects/json-schema-output-guard/stages/04-bounded-repair/docs/en.md

- **Should a refusal trigger a retry?** No. Log it and return a typed refusal.
- **Is constrained decoding slower?** Often faster. Forced tokens skip generation.
- **Does it need a big model?** No. A 3B model with grammar beats a 70B model with prompts.
- **Does acceptance prove the answer?** No. It does not establish factual correctness.
- **Why call checkSchema first?** A broken schema then cannot spend provider budget.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/20-structured-outputs-constrained-decoding/docs/en.md, phases/11-llm-engineering/03-structured-outputs/docs/en.md, projects/json-schema-output-guard/README.md, projects/json-schema-output-guard/stages/04-bounded-repair/docs/en.md

- Local model, flat schema: Outlines. Recursive schema: XGrammar or llguidance.
- Self-hosted server: vLLM `guided_json`, `guided_regex`, `guided_choice`.
- Use tool use when the model must pick one of many schemas.
- Send structured `Issue[]` back to the model, not free text.
- Keep every attempt in the trace. A late success does not hide earlier failures.
- The guard rejects `$ref`, format and combinators.
- In the project commands, `<ws>` is `learning-artifacts/json-schema-output-guard`.

## Pydantic schema with Instructor
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/20-structured-outputs-constrained-decoding/docs/en.md

```python

    vendor: str
    total_usd: float = Field(ge=0)       # numeric bound
    line_items: list[str]

client = instructor.from_anthropic(Anthropic())
invoice = client.messages.create(
    model="claude-opus-4-7",
    max_tokens=1024,
    response_model=Invoice,              # retries on validation failure
```
