## MultiHeadSelfAttention forward
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/33-multihead-self-attention/code/main.py

```python
self.qkv_proj = nn.Linear(d_model, 3 * d_model, bias=True)  # Q, K, V in one matmul
causal_mask = torch.tril(torch.ones(max_context_length, max_context_length))
self.register_buffer("causal_mask", causal_mask, persistent=False)  # no grad
qkv = self.qkv_proj(x)                          # (B, T, 3D)
q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)                  # three (B, T, D) views
q = self._split_heads(q)                        # (B, H, T, d_head)
k = self._split_heads(k)
v = self._split_heads(v)
scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(self.d_head)
mask_slice = self.causal_mask[:t, :t]           # top left (T, T)
scores = scores.masked_fill(mask_slice == 0, float("-inf"))
weights = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)             # rows sum to 1
context = self._merge_heads(torch.matmul(weights, v))  # (B, T, D)
out = self.out_proj(context)                    # mixes the heads
```

## Defaults and numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/04-positional-encoding/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/34-transformer-block/code/main.py, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/03-multi-head-attention/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/35-gpt-model-assembly/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/35-gpt-model-assembly/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/12-kv-cache-flash-attention/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/13-scaling-laws/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sinusoidal and RoPE base | 10000 | raise RoPE base for longer context |
| mlp_expansion | 4 | MLP is D to 4D to D |
| d_head | 64 | 64 or 128 in production |
| Init std | 0.02 | Linear and Embedding weights |
| Residual projection scale | 1 / sqrt(2 * num_layers) | out_proj and fc2 |
| GPT-2 small d_model | 768 | 12 heads, 12 layers, about 124M |
| KV bytes per token per layer | `2 * n_kv_heads * d_head * dtype_size` | all KV heads, K and V |
| Compute optimal ratio | 20 | tokens per parameter |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/33-multihead-self-attention/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/33-multihead-self-attention/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/34-transformer-block/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/35-gpt-model-assembly/docs/en.md, phases/10-llms-from-scratch/04-pre-training-mini-gpt/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/10-attention-mechanism/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/04-positional-encoding/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ValueError` on d_model and n_heads | D is not divisible by H | pick H that divides D |
| `seq_len` exceeds max_context_length | T is larger than the mask | crop to the last context_length tokens |
| Model cheats on next token | no causal mask | mask the upper triangle with `-inf` |
| Softmax gives `inf` | `exp` of a large number | subtract the row max first |
| Learning stalls | scores not scaled | divide by `sqrt(d_head)` |
| Deep stack diverges | post-LN on the residual path | use pre-LN |
| Weight tying saves nothing | weights copied, not shared | assign the same parameter |
| Bad output past trained length | positions do not extrapolate | use RoPE with base scaling |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/03-multi-head-attention/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/04-positional-encoding/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/05-full-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/12-kv-cache-flash-attention/docs/en.md

- **MHA**: Multi-head attention. N query heads, N K/V heads.
- **MQA**: Multi-Query Attention. One shared K/V projection.
- **GQA**: Grouped-Query Attention. Fewer K/V heads, repeated to match Q.
- **MLA**: Multi-head Latent Attention. K and V in a low rank latent.
- **RoPE**: Rotary Position Embeddings. Rotates Q and K by position.
- **ALiBi**: Attention with Linear Biases. Distance penalty on scores.
- **RMSNorm**: LayerNorm without the mean.
- **KV cache**: stored K and V of every prefix token.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/02-self-attention-from-scratch/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/07-gpt-causal-language-modeling/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/04-positional-encoding/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/03-multi-head-attention/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/12-kv-cache-flash-attention/docs/en.md

- **Why divide by sqrt(d_k)?** Large dot products saturate softmax and gradients vanish.
- **Why -inf in the mask?** exp(-inf) = 0, so future positions get zero weight.
- **Why add positions?** Attention alone is permutation invariant.
- **Why GQA?** It cuts KV cache memory by N/G with nearly full quality.
- **Is Flash Attention approximate?** No. A running (max, sum) keeps it exact.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/33-multihead-self-attention/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/33-multihead-self-attention/code/tests/test_attention.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/34-transformer-block/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/35-gpt-model-assembly/docs/en.md, phases/05-nlp-foundations-to-advanced/10-attention-mechanism/docs/en.md

- Test that weight rows sum to 1.
- Test that future tokens do not change past outputs.
- Expect a loss near log(V) at random init.
- Count parameters against the reference model.
- Put dropout after the softmax and after the second MLP linear.
- Do not use attention weights as proof of reasoning.

title: Text-to-Speech, Voice Cloning and Codecs
subtitle: Text to phonemes to mel to waveform, clone with consent and a watermark, and tokenize audio with RVQ codecs.
markdown:
## TTS and cloning pipeline
type: architecture
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md

```arch
node | text | 1,1 | Text | normalize first | client
node | g2p | 2,1 | Phonemizer | espeak, G2P fallback | process
node | ac | 3,1 | Acoustic model | text to mel, 80 channels | model
node | voc | 4,1 | Vocoder | HiFi-GAN, mel to waveform | model
node | ref | 2,2 | Reference clip | 5 s plus its transcript | store
node | spk | 3,2 | Speaker encoder | speaker embedding | model
node | wm | 4,2 | Watermark | ~32 bits of payload | process
edge | text | g2p |
edge | g2p | ac | phonemes
edge | ac | voc | mel
edge | ref | spk |
edge | spk | ac | embedding
edge | voc | wm | waveform
```

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/code/main.py
span: 2

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Phonemize | `phonemize("Hello world", language="en-us", backend="espeak")` |
| Kokoro on CPU | `KPipeline(lang_code="a")`, then `tts(text, voice="af_bella")` |
| Zero-shot clone | `F5TTS().infer(ref_file=<wav>, ref_text=<text>, gen_text=<text>)` |
| Voice conversion | `vc.convert(source=<wav>, target_pool=[<wav>, <wav>])` |
| Embed a watermark | `sc.embed(wav, sr=24000, message=payload)` |
| EnCodec at 6 kbps | `model.set_target_bandwidth(6.0)` |
| Mimi semantic split | `semantic = codes[:, 0]`, `acoustic = codes[:, 1:]` |
| Toy RVQ | `rvq_encode(values, codebook_size=8, n_codebooks=4)` |

## Clone and watermark
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md

```python
from f5_tts.api import F5TTS
tts = F5TTS()
wav = tts.infer(ref_file="my_voice_5s.wav",                    # 5 s reference
    ref_text="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",    # must match exactly
    gen_text="Please remind me to water the plants.")
sc = SilentCipher(model="2024-06-01")
payload = b"consent_id:abc123;ts:1745353200"
watermarked = sc.embed(wav, sr=24000, message=payload)  # ~32 bits
detected = sc.detect(watermarked, sr=24000)             # payload bytes
```

## Encode with a codec
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md

```python
model = EncodecModel.encodec_model_24khz()
model.set_target_bandwidth(6.0)            # kbps, 8 codebooks
with torch.no_grad():
    encoded = model.encode(wav)
codes, scale = encoded[0]                  # (1, n_codebooks, n_frames)
wav_recon = model.decode([(codes, scale)])
mimi = loaders.get_mimi()                  # from moshi.models
codes = mimi.encode(wav)                   # (1, 8, frames@12.5Hz)
semantic = codes[:, 0]                     # content, WavLM-aligned
acoustic = codes[:, 1:]                    # timbre, prosody, noise
```

## Consent gate
type: flow
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md

1. **Gate**: `verify_signature(consent_record)` must pass. Else "Signed consent required".
2. **Speaker**: `consent_record["speaker_id"]` must equal `hash_speaker(ref_audio)`.
3. **Clone**: `tts.infer(ref_file=ref_audio, gen_text=text)`.
4. **Mark**: `watermark(wav, payload=consent_record["id"])`.
5. **Log**: store the consent record in a tamper-evident log.

## Formulas and numbers
type: concepts
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/code/main.py, phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/code/main.py

- **RVQ**: codebook 1 quantizes the encoder output. Each next one quantizes the residual.
- **Decode**: the decoder sums the chosen codes per frame.
- **Vocabulary**: 8 codebooks of 1024 codes give $1024^8 = 10^{24}$.
- **LM tokens**: $10 \times 12.5 \times 8 = 1000$ tokens for 10 s of Mimi.
- **Toy RVQ bits**: 8 codes are 3 bits. Bits per frame is 3 times the codebooks.
- **Mel hop**: 12.5 ms at 24 kHz is 300 samples.
- **HiFi-GAN**: upsample rates 8, 8, 2, 2 give 256x, mel rate to audio rate.

## Codec numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| EnCodec-24k frame rate | 75 Hz | Default 4 codebooks @ 1.5 kbps |
| DAC-44.1k frame rate | 86 Hz | Highest fidelity, full-band |
| SNAC-24k coarse rate | ~12 Hz | Detail at 50 Hz |
| Mimi frame rate | 12.5 Hz | 8 codebooks @ 4.4 kbps |
| Codes per codebook | 1024 | Each code is 0-1023 |
| Codebook count | 8-12 | More adds fidelity and sequence length |
| Kokoro output | 24 kHz | Resample for 16 kHz consumers |

## Models
type: concepts
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md

- **Tacotron 2**: autoregressive seq2seq. Slow, wobbly on long text.
- **FastSpeech 2**: duration predictor, 1-pass, 10× faster than Tacotron.
- **VITS**: encoder, flow duration and HiFi-GAN, trained end-to-end. 25M.
- **F5-TTS**: flow-matching diffusion transformer. Clones from 5 s. 335M.
- **Kokoro**: 82M, CPU-runnable, English only.
- **KNN-VC**: swaps each WavLM source frame for its nearest target-pool frame.
- **Mimi**: codebook 0 is distilled from WavLM. Codebooks 1-7 are acoustic.

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md

- **TTS**: Text-to-Speech. Text frontend, acoustic model, vocoder.
- **VC**: Voice conversion. Speech of A rewritten in the voice of B.
- **PPG**: Phonetic posteriorgram. Per-frame ASR posteriors as content.
- **RVQ**: Residual Vector Quantization. A cascade of small codebooks.
- **SECS**: speaker embedding cosine. Above 0.70 is indistinguishable for most listeners.
- **UTMOS**: reference-free MOS predictor. Ground truth scores 4.08.
- **CMOS**: Comparative MOS. An A-vs-B preference.
- **PESQ / ViSQOL**: objective metrics that correlate with MOS.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Dr." reads as "Drive" | No text normalizer | Normalize before the phonemizer |
| Proper noun mispronounced | OOV token | Ship a fallback G2P model |
| Output overshoots ±1.0 | Mel scaling mismatch | `np.clip(wav, -1, 1)` |
| Aliasing downstream | 24 kHz Kokoro into a 16 kHz pipeline | Resample |
| Clone alignment breaks | Reference text differs from audio | Match it exactly, punctuation included |
| Echo in the clone | Reverberant reference | Record dry, close-mic |
| French clone keeps the accent | Language leakage | XTTS or VALL-E X |
| LM fails silently | 12.5 Hz Mimi, then 50 Hz EnCodec | Keep one frame rate |

## Use X when
type: tips
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/07-text-to-speech/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md

- Real-time English on CPU: Kokoro.
- Clone from a 5 s reference: F5-TTS or OpenVoice v2.
- Rewrite speech into a target voice: KNN-VC or Diff-HierVC.
- Generative model over audio: start with Mimi or SNAC.
- Compression pipeline: use Opus. It wins per bit.
- Highest-fidelity reconstruction: DAC-44.1k.
- Every clone: a watermark and a consent record.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/06-speech-and-audio/13-neural-audio-codecs/docs/en.md, phases/06-speech-and-audio/08-voice-cloning-conversion/docs/en.md

- **Why split semantic and acoustic tokens?** Pure reconstruction tokens give blurry speech from text.
- **Why RVQ, not one codebook?** One big codebook needs millions of codes.
- **Which Mimi codebook matters?** Codebook 0. Losing it destroys intelligibility.
- **Cloning or conversion?** Cloning takes text. Conversion takes source speech.
- **Few-shot fine-tune?** 5-30 minutes of the target voice, LoRA for an hour.

title: Unified Multimodal Models
subtitle: Pick a unified design. Discrete NTP, two-loss diffusion, masked diffusion, decoupled encoders, next-scale, any-to-any.
markdown:
## Four unified designs side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/15-janus-pro-decoupled-encoders/docs/en.md

| Factor | Chameleon, Emu3 | Transfusion | Show-o | Janus-Pro |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Image form | Discrete VQ tokens | Continuous 16x16 patches | Discrete VQ tokens | SigLIP in, VQ tokens out |
| Image loss | Next-token cross-entropy | Flow matching MSE | Cross-entropy on masked tokens | Next-token on VQ tokens |
| Image attention | Causal | Bidirectional in the image block | Bidirectional in the image block | Text-style shared body |
| Image decode | 1024-4096 passes, token by token | 10-30 diffusion steps | ~16 parallel steps | Token by token |
| Visual encoders | One VQ tokenizer | Linear patch projection | One VQ tokenizer | SigLIP plus VQ tokenizer |
| Weak point | Tokenizer ceiling, slow inference | Loss weights need tuning | Lossy by tokenizer | Two tokenizers to train |
| Key number | Emu3 FID 5.4 vs SDXL 5.6 | 3-5 FID points over Chameleon-style at 7B | ~16 steps vs ~1000 | GenEval 0.80 vs DALL-E 3 0.67 |

## Use X when
type: tips
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/15-janus-pro-decoupled-encoders/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/16-mio-any-to-any-streaming/docs/en.md

- Chameleon family: you need image generation and mixed-modality output from one decoder.
- Adapter VLM (LLaVA family): you need understanding only. It reuses more pretrained compute.
- Emu3: you want image gen, perception and video from one checkpoint with prompt templates.
- Transfusion: quality comes first and you can afford the two-loss plumbing.
- Show-o: you want T2I, inpainting and VQA in one open model with reasonable speed.
- Janus-Pro: you need both understanding and generation. Pick SD3 or Flux for generation only.
- VAR: you want class-conditional images in about 10 passes, against 28-50 for DiT.
- MIO: you need speech in and speech out from one model, under 500ms TTFAB.

## Janus-Pro decoupled routing
type: architecture
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/15-janus-pro-decoupled-encoders/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/15-janus-pro-decoupled-encoders/code/main.py

```arch
node | img | 1,1 | Input image | | client
node | prompt | 1,2 | Text prompt | task tag picks the path | client
node | siglip | 2,1 | SigLIP-SO400m | then 2-layer MLP
node | vqin | 2,2 | VQ tokenizer | optional image condition
node | body | 3,1 | Shared body | init DeepSeek-MoE-7B | model
node | vqout | 3,2 | Image VQ tokens | predicted by the body
node | text | 4,1 | Text out | autoregressive
node | dec | 4,2 | VQ decoder | pixels
edge | img | siglip | understand
edge | img | vqin | generate
edge | prompt | body | text tokens
edge | siglip | body |
edge | vqin | body |
edge | body | text |
edge | body | vqout |
edge | vqout | dec |
```

## Show-o masked sampling loop
type: flow
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md

1. **Start**: every image token is `MASK`. The toy uses `SEQ_LEN` 16 and `VOCAB` 8.
2. **Schedule**: `cosine_schedule(T)` gives one mask ratio for each of T=8 steps.
3. **Predict**: the transformer predicts all masked tokens in parallel.
4. **Commit**: keep the most confident tokens. `keep_ratio = max(0.15, 1 - ratios[step])`.
5. **Repeat**: the other tokens stay masked for the next step.
6. **Finish**: `step_unmask(tokens, prompt_seed, 1.0)` fills any token that is still masked.

## Residual multi-scale tokenizer (VAR)
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/code/main.py

```python
SCALES = (1, 2, 4, 8)                       # 4 scales over an 8x8 image
CODEBOOK = 16                               # entries per scale
residual = img.copy()
for scale, book in zip(SCALES, codebooks):
    coarse = downsample(residual, scale)    # pool to scale x scale
    tok = encode(coarse, book)              # nearest code index
    recon = book[tok]
    residual = residual - upsample(recon, IMG)  # what is still missed
    tokens.append(tok)
out = out + upsample(book[tok], IMG)        # decoder sums every scale
```

## Two-loss step (Transfusion)
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/code/main.py

```python
weights = {"text_scale": 0, "img_scale": 0, "text_w": 1.0, "img_w": 0.1}
mask = build_mask(tokens)                   # causal text, bidirectional image
text_loss = sum(cross_entropy_toy(p) for p in text_probs) / len(text_probs)
t = random.random()                         # one timestep per image
xt = (1 - t) * x + t * n                    # noisy patch
target_vel = n - x                          # velocity target
img_loss = mse(pred_flat, tgt_flat)         # flow matching MSE
total = weights["text_w"] * text_loss + weights["img_w"] * img_loss
```

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/code/main.py, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md

- **Residual VQ**: $f \approx \sum_k \mathrm{upsample}(\mathrm{embed}(z_k))$. Scale k holds what scales 1 to k-1 missed.
- **Flow matching**: $x_t = (1-t) x_0 + t \epsilon$. Loss is MSE of $v_\theta(x_t, t)$ against $\epsilon - x_0$.
- **CFG**: mixed = uncond + gamma times (cond minus uncond).
- **Cosine mask ratio**: $\cos(\pi t / 2T)$. Ratio 1.0 at step 0, no mask at step T.
- **Show-o loss**: cross-entropy on masked tokens. Text NTP masks only the last token.
- **Chameleon vocab**: 32000 text plus 8192 image ids gives 40192.
- **Emu3 video**: 32 * 32 * 8 = 8,192 tokens for 4 s at 8 FPS, 256x256.

## Numbers to keep
type: defaults
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/16-mio-any-to-any-streaming/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Chameleon codebook K | 8192 | 1024 tokens per 512x512 image |
| Emu3 codebook | 32768 | 4096 tokens per 512x512, 30.5 dB PSNR |
| CFG guidance weight | 3.0-7.0 | Generate with and without the caption |
| Emu3 temperature | 0.8 | 1.0 for perception |
| Transfusion denoise steps | 10-30 | Conditioned on the prior text |
| MaskGIT iterations | 8-16 | Cosine schedule works well |
| VAR scales K | 10 | 10 passes for a 256x256 image |
| TTFAB target | <500ms | Conversational feel |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/16-mio-any-to-any-streaming/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 34B early-fusion run diverges | Logit magnitude explodes at depth | QK-Norm, dropout after every residual-add |
| Image PSNR stays near 26-28 dB | VQ-VAE tokenizer ceiling | Better tokenizer, or continuous patches |
| One loss head dominates | NTP and diffusion schedules mismatch | Tune the loss weights |
| Image artifacts | Temperature too high | Use 0.8 for image generation |
| Mode collapse | Temperature too low | Raise the temperature |
| ~2 minutes per 512x512 image | 4096 tokens at 30 tok/s | Speculative decoding, KV-cache work |
| No cross-modality context | Interleaved stage 2 skipped | Train all four curriculum stages |
| Poor speech | Speech-enhanced stage 3 skipped | Add stage 3 audio data |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/11-chameleon-early-fusion-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/12-emu3-next-token-for-generation/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/16-mio-any-to-any-streaming/docs/en.md

- **VAR**: Visual AutoRegressive. Next-scale prediction over a pyramid of VQ grids.
- **VQ-VAE**: vector-quantized variational autoencoder. Maps features to codebook indices.
- **NTP**: next-token prediction. Predict token i+1 from tokens 0 to i.
- **CFG**: classifier-free guidance. Mixes conditional and unconditional logits.
- **IBQ**: Inverse Bottleneck Quantizer. Emu3 tokenizer class, codebook 32768+.
- **MMDiT**: Multimodal DiT. SD3 backbone with joint attention.
- **TTFAB**: time-to-first-audio-byte. User voice to first audio output.
- **Residual-VQ**: stacked codebooks. Base layer is content, later layers add prosody.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/15-janus-pro-decoupled-encoders/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/14-show-o-discrete-diffusion-unified/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/19-visual-autoregressive-var/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/13-transfusion-autoregressive-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/16-mio-any-to-any-streaming/docs/en.md

- **Why does one visual encoder fail?** VQ codes have weak semantics. SigLIP features do not reconstruct well.
- **Why is inpainting free in Show-o?** Training predicts masked tokens. Mask a region and predict it.
- **Why is VAR fast?** One transformer pass predicts a whole scale in parallel.
- **What does Transfusion text attend to?** Earlier text and previous images. Images see preceding text.
- **Why did Janus-Pro beat Janus?** 7B against 1.3B params and 72M stage 2 pairs against 26M.
- **How does MIO keep IDs apart?** Each modality gets a disjoint ID range in one vocabulary.

title: Clustering, Dimensionality Reduction and Anomalies
subtitle: Cluster, reduce and flag outliers without labels. K-Means, DBSCAN, GMM, PCA, Isolation Forest, LOF.
markdown:
## Three jobs without labels
type: architecture
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

```arch
node | raw | 1,2 | Raw data | no labels
node | pca | 2,1 | PCA | keep 90-95% variance
node | clu | 3,1 | Clustering | K-Means, DBSCAN, GMM
node | det | 2,3 | Detector | Isolation Forest, LOF
node | rec | 3,2 | Reconstruction error | high error is an outlier
node | score | 3,3 | Anomaly score | rank, then threshold
node | flag | 4,2 | Flagged points | human review
edge | raw | pca |
edge | pca | clu | reduced
edge | pca | rec |
edge | raw | det |
edge | det | score |
edge | rec | flag |
edge | score | flag |
```

## From-scratch calls
type: task-table
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/code/clustering.py, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/code/dim_reduction.py, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/code/anomaly_detection.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| K clusters, hard labels | `kmeans(data, k=3)` |
| Inertia and silhouette per K | `find_best_k(data, max_k=6)` |
| Dense regions, noise is -1 | `dbscan(data, eps=1.5, min_samples=5)` |
| Soft labels with EM | `gmm(data, k=3)` |
| Project to 2 axes | `PCA(n_components=2).fit_transform(X)` |
| Separate rings | `kernel_pca(X, n_components, kernel="rbf", gamma=1.0)` |
| Flag by standard deviations | `zscore_detect(X, threshold=3.0)` |
| Flag outside the fences | `iqr_detect(X, factor=1.5)` |

## The same in sklearn
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

```python
km = KMeans(n_clusters=3, random_state=42).fit(data)
db = DBSCAN(eps=1.5, min_samples=5).fit(data)
gmm_model = GaussianMixture(n_components=3, random_state=42).fit(data)
sklearn_pca = SklearnPCA(n_components=2)          # explained_variance_ratio_
tsne = TSNE(n_components=2, perplexity=30, random_state=42)
reducer = UMAP(n_components=2, n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, random_state=42)
iso = IsolationForest(n_estimators=100, contamination=0.05, random_state=42)
iso.fit(X_train)                                  # fit on normal data
lof = LocalOutlierFactor(n_neighbors=20, contamination=0.05, novelty=True)
oc_svm = OneClassSVM(kernel="rbf", gamma="auto", nu=0.05)
```

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

- **Inertia**: sum of squared distances from each point to its centroid. Lower is tighter.
- **Silhouette**: $(b - a) / \max(a, b)$, from -1 (wrong cluster) to +1.
- **Z-score**: $(x - \text{mean}) / \text{std}$. Flag when the absolute value passes the threshold.
- **IQR fences**: $Q1 - \text{factor} \cdot IQR$ and $Q3 + \text{factor} \cdot IQR$, with $IQR = Q3 - Q1$.
- **Isolation score**: $2^{-\text{average\_path\_length}(x) / c(n)}$. Near 1 is an anomaly, near 0.5 is normal.
- **c(n)**: `2 * H(n-1) - 2*(n-1)/n`, expected path length of a failed search.
- **Explained ratio**: $\text{eigenvalue}_k / \sum \text{all eigenvalues}$
- **PCA fraction lost**: dropped eigenvalues over all eigenvalues.

## Clustering: use X when
type: command-table
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| K-Means | Large data, spherical clusters, known K. Hurt by outliers |
| DBSCAN | Unknown K, any shape, finds noise. Fails on varying density |
| Hierarchical | Small data, needs a dendrogram. $O(n^2)$ memory |
| GMM | Overlapping, elliptical clusters, soft assignments |
| Ward linkage | Merge with the smallest rise in within-cluster variance |

## Reduce and detect: use X when
type: command-table
from: phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| PCA | Preprocessing and compression. Fast, global variance |
| t-SNE | 2D plots of local neighborhoods. Below 10k samples |
| UMAP | 2D plots at scale. Some global structure |
| Kernel PCA | Nonlinear manifold. Kernel matrix is n by n |
| Z-score / IQR | One feature at a time. Very fast |
| Isolation Forest | No assumptions. Works in high dimensions |
| LOF | Local anomalies, clusters of different density. Slow |
| One-Class SVM | Small to medium data. Kernel matrix grows quadratically |

## Anomaly detection pipeline
type: flow
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md

1. **Baseline**: collect a period with no or very few anomalies.
2. **Features**: add rolling statistics, time features and ratios.
3. **Train**: fit the detector on the baseline. It learns normal.
4. **Score**: give each new observation an anomaly score.
5. **Threshold**: pick the cutoff from the cost of false alarms and misses.
6. **Alert**: send flagged points to human review.
7. **Feedback**: record true anomalies and false alarms. Tune the threshold.

## Defaults and numbers
type: defaults
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/code/anomaly_detection.py, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Z-score `threshold` | 3.0 | 99.7% of Gaussian data is inside |
| IQR `factor` | 1.5 | 3.0 flags fewer points |
| `n_estimators` | 100 | Isolation trees. Usually enough |
| `max_samples` | 256 | Rows per tree, from the original paper |
| `predict` threshold | 0.5 | Score above it is an anomaly |
| `contamination` | 0.05 | Sets the cutoff only, not the scores |
| t-SNE perplexity | 30 | Typical range 5-50 |
| Variance kept | 0.95 | Or 0.90 for the PCA cutoff |

## Failures and fixes
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| K-Means splits moons badly | Clusters are not spherical | Use DBSCAN with eps=0.3 |
| K-Means results change per run | Local minimum of inertia | Fix the seed or use K-Means++ |
| Z-score misses points | Multimodal data or outliers in training | Use IQR or Isolation Forest |
| Per-feature methods miss a point | Unusual only in the joint space | Use Isolation Forest |
| 99.9% accuracy, no catches | 0.1% anomalies, accuracy is useless | Precision@k and AUPRC |
| Operators ignore alerts | Too many false alarms | Start with a high threshold |
| Median score drifts up | Data changed or model is stale | Retrain on recent normal data |
| t-SNE cluster gaps differ | Distances between clusters mean nothing | Read only the clusters |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

- **DBSCAN**: density-based clustering. Core, border and noise points.
- **GMM**: Gaussian Mixture Model. K Gaussians with soft assignments.
- **EM**: Expectation-Maximization. E-step probabilities, M-step parameters.
- **PCA**: Principal Component Analysis. Axes of maximum variance.
- **t-SNE**: t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding. Keeps neighbors.
- **UMAP**: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection. Faster, more global.
- **LOF**: Local Outlier Factor. Above 1.0 is lower density than neighbors.
- **AUPRC**: area under the precision-recall curve. Better than AUROC here.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/02-ml-fundamentals/07-unsupervised-learning/docs/en.md, phases/02-ml-fundamentals/16-anomaly-detection/docs/en.md, phases/01-math-foundations/10-dimensionality-reduction/docs/en.md

- **How do I pick K?** Find the elbow in inertia. Check the silhouette score.
- **Why model normal data?** Anomalies are rare and change. Deviations from normal include novel types.
- **What is the best training setup?** Semi-supervised: fit on a clean set of normal data only.
- **Few labeled anomalies?** Use them for evaluation, not training.
- **Why is Isolation Forest fast?** Each tree uses a small subsample.
- **Why reduce dimensions?** Distances converge in high dimensions. Nearest-neighbor search stops working.

title: Value Methods against Policy Methods
subtitle: Q-learning, SARSA, DQN, REINFORCE, A2C and PPO side by side. Targets, defaults, diagnostics and fixes.
markdown:
## Four methods side by side
type: comparison
span: 2
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

| Factor | Q-learning, SARSA | DQN | REINFORCE | A2C, PPO |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Learns | Q table | Neural $Q(s, a; \theta)$ | Policy $\pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ | Actor $\pi_\theta$ plus critic $V_\phi(s)$ |
| Picks actions | ε-greedy on Q | ε-greedy on Q | Sample from $\pi_\theta$ | Sample from $\pi_\theta$ |
| Data | Q-learning off-policy, SARSA on-policy | Off-policy, replay buffer | On-policy, one update | A2C one update, PPO K epochs |
| Target | $r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a')$ | Same, from target net $\theta^-$ | Return $G_t$ | GAE advantage |
| Bias and variance | Bootstrap bias, low variance | Max bias upward | Unbiased, high variance | Critic bias, far lower variance |
| Continuous actions | No | No, route to SAC or TD3 | Yes, Gaussian policy | Yes, Gaussian policy |
| Toy GridWorld | ~2,000 episodes | ~500 episodes | ~500 episodes with a baseline | PPO with ε 0.2, K 4 |

## Use X when
type: tips
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

- Q-learning: small tabular environments. It learns the optimal policy directly.
- SARSA or Expected SARSA: on-policy safety-critical tasks. They stay conservative during exploration.
- DQN: high-dimensional state with discrete actions. It is the reference off-policy algorithm.
- REINFORCE: read it, rarely run it. `loss = -advantage * log_prob` is REINFORCE with a baseline.
- A2C: batched parallel envs on a GPU. GPU-based A2C dominates A3C in 2026.
- PPO: the default for MuJoCo, Atari and RLHF for LLMs.
- SAC or TD3: continuous control. DQN has no policy network.
- GRPO: reasoning LLMs. It is a PPO variant without a critic.

## DQN training loop
type: architecture
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/code/main.py

```arch
node | env | 1,1 | Environment | 4x4 GridWorld | client
node | buf | 2,1 | Replay buffer | capacity 2000 | store
node | online | 3,1 | Online net | weights theta | model
node | target | 3,2 | Target net | frozen copy | model
node | loss | 4,1 | train_step | squared TD error | process
edge | env | buf | transitions
edge | buf | online | minibatch 32
edge | online | env | ε-greedy action
edge | target | loss | y = r + γ max
edge | online | loss | q[a]
edge | online | target | clone every 200 steps
```

## PPO training loop
type: flow
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/code/main.py

1. **Rollout**: collect N times T transitions across N parallel envs.
2. **Snapshot**: store `log_pi_old` for each action at rollout time.
3. **GAE**: compute advantages, freeze them, normalize per batch.
4. **Epochs**: for K epochs, shuffle the buffer into minibatches.
5. **Ratio**: `ratio = exp(logp - rec["log_pi_old"])`.
6. **Clip**: a sample past 1 ± ε on the beneficial side gets zero gradient.
7. **Losses**: add value MSE and the entropy bonus. Take the gradient step.
8. **Discard**: drop the rollout and collect a new one.

## Value side: TD targets
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/code/main.py

```python
a = epsilon_greedy(Q, s, rng, epsilon)     # behaviour action
s_next, r, done = step(s, a)
best_next = max(Q[s_next].values())        # Q-learning: greedy max
target = r + gamma * best_next
a_next = epsilon_greedy(Q, s_next, rng, epsilon)
target = r + gamma * Q[s_next][a_next]     # SARSA: the next action taken
Q[s][a] += alpha * (target - Q[s][a])      # same TD update for both
Q[s][a] += alpha * (r - Q[s][a])           # terminal step, no bootstrap
```

## Policy side: gradient, GAE, clip
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/code/main.py

```python
G = r + gamma * G                           # reward-to-go, walked backwards
grad = (1.0 if i == a else 0.0) - probs[i]  # onehot minus probs
theta[i][j] += lr * adv * grad * x[j]       # REINFORCE ascent
delta = traj[t]["r"] + gamma * next_v - traj[t]["v"]  # TD residual
gae = delta + gamma * lam * gae             # GAE with lam=0.95
ratio = math.exp(logp - rec["log_pi_old"])  # PPO importance ratio
clipped = (adv > 0 and ratio > 1 + eps) or (adv < 0 and ratio < 1 - eps)
pg_scale = 0.0                              # clipped sample, no gradient
```

## Tasks in code
type: task-table
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/code/main.py, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/code/main.py

| Task | Code |
|---|---|
| Tabular SARSA | `sarsa(episodes, alpha=0.1, gamma=0.99)` |
| Tabular Q-learning | `q_learning(episodes, alpha=0.1, gamma=0.99)` |
| One DQN gradient step | `train_step(online, target, mb, gamma, lr)` |
| Sync the target net | `target = clone(online)` |
| REINFORCE with baseline | `reinforce(episodes, use_baseline=True)` |
| GAE advantages | `gae_advantages(traj, gamma=0.99, lam=0.95)` |
| Train A2C | `actor_critic(episodes, lam=0.95)` |
| PPO update with diagnostics | `mean_kl, clip_frac = ppo_update(...)` |

## Key formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

- **TD error**: $\delta = r + \gamma V(s') - V(s)$
- **SARSA target**: $r + \gamma Q(s', a')$ with the action taken next.
- **DQN loss**: $(r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta^-) - Q(s, a; \theta))^2$
- **Double DQN**: $r + \gamma Q(s', \arg\max_{a'} Q(s', a'; \theta); \theta^-)$
- **Policy gradient**: $\nabla J = \mathbb{E}[G_t \nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t)]$
- **Advantage**: $A = G - \hat{V}(s)$. Same expectation, lower variance.
- **GAE**: $A_t = \sum_l (\gamma \lambda)^l \delta_{t+l}$. λ 0 is TD, λ 1 is MC.
- **PPO clip**: $\min(r_t A_t, \mathrm{clip}(r_t, 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) A_t)$

## Defaults
type: defaults
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Tabular α and ε | 0.1 | Pin α in [0.05, 0.3] |
| Discount γ | 0.99 | Default in the lesson code |
| DQN target sync | 10,000 | Atari env steps |
| GAE λ | 0.95 | The 2026 default |
| Value weight `c_v` | 0.5 | A2C and PPO |
| Entropy weight `c_e` | 0.01 | A2C and PPO |
| PPO clip ε | 0.2 | 0.1 is timid, 0.3+ is unstable |
| PPO epochs K | 10 | Minibatches of 64 |

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Q values overestimate | `max` over noisy Q is biased up | Double DQN or Double Q-learning |
| DQN diverges | Deadly triad | Keep the target net and the replay buffer |
| DQN overfits early | Gradients on ~20 samples | Wait for a few thousand transitions |
| Policy stops exploring | Entropy collapse | Entropy bonus, `c_e` above 0 |
| Policy gradient explodes | Huge returns | Normalize G to ~N(0, 1) per batch |
| Actor learns noise | Critic is still random | Warm up the critic, slow actor LR |
| PPO mean KL past 0.1 | Too many epochs or high LR | Reduce `K_EPOCHS` or `LR` |
| Clip fraction near 0 | Clip never triggers | Raise `LR` or `K_EPOCHS` |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/05-dqn/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md

- **TD**: temporal difference. Update after every step from a bootstrapped target.
- **SARSA**: the tuple (s, a, r, s', a'). On-policy TD.
- **GLIE**: Greedy in the Limit with Infinite Exploration. The ε condition.
- **DQN**: Q-learning with a neural Q, replay buffer and target network.
- **GAE**: Generalized Advantage Estimation. Weighted sum of n-step advantages.
- **A2C, A3C**: synchronous batched, or asynchronous threaded, actor-critic.
- **TRPO**: Trust Region Policy Optimization. KL constraint, conjugate gradients.
- **PPO**: Proximal Policy Optimization. Clipped importance ratio.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/09-reinforcement-learning/04-q-learning-sarsa/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/06-policy-gradients-reinforce/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/08-ppo/docs/en.md, phases/09-reinforcement-learning/07-actor-critic-a2c-a3c/docs/en.md

- **Why is Q-learning off-policy?** The `max` assumes the greedy policy, whatever action the agent takes.
- **Why is SARSA safer on the cliff?** It puts exploration noise into its Q values.
- **Why are value methods weak on continuous actions?** `argmax` over a 10-dimensional torque is hard.
- **Why is a baseline unbiased?** The expected baseline times the log-policy gradient is 0.
- **Why can PPO reuse a rollout?** The clip stops the update once the policy drifts too far.
- **Most common PPO bug?** A flipped sign. Minimize the negative of the clipped surrogate.

title: Video and 3D Generation
subtitle: Video DiT patches and divided attention, world models, Gaussian splats, NeRF and multi-view 3D. Formulas and fixes.
markdown:
## Video diffusion pipeline
type: architecture
from: phases/08-generative-ai/10-video-generation/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/28-world-models-video-diffusion/docs/en.md

```arch
node | vid | 1,1 | Video | T frames | client
node | vae | 2,1 | 3D VAE | spatiotemporal compression | model
node | patch | 3,1 | Patchify | t_p, h_p, w_p patches | process
node | txt | 1,2 | Prompt | dense re-captions | client
node | te | 2,2 | Text encoder | T5-XXL | model
node | dit | 3,2 | Video DiT | 3D positions, divided attention | gpu
node | lat | 4,2 | Denoised latent | ε or v prediction | store
node | out | 4,1 | Frames | VAE decode | client
edge | vid | vae |
edge | vae | patch | latent
edge | patch | dit | tokens
edge | txt | te |
edge | te | dit | cross-attention
edge | dit | lat | each step
edge | lat | out |
```

## Render and fit Gaussian splats
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/22-3d-gaussian-splatting/docs/en.md

1. **Project**: map each 3D Gaussian to 2D with camera extrinsics and intrinsics.
2. **Tile**: assign each 2D Gaussian to 16x16 screen tiles.
3. **Sort**: sort the Gaussians by depth in each tile.
4. **Composite**: blend front-to-back into the pixel colour.
5. **Loss**: compare the render with the ground-truth photo.
6. **Backprop**: update `(mu, q, s, alpha, c_lm)` by gradient descent.
7. **Densify**: clone small Gaussians and split large ones where the gradient is high.
8. **Prune**: remove Gaussians with low opacity. Train for ~30,000 iterations.

## Formulas and numbers
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/22-3d-gaussian-splatting/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/28-world-models-video-diffusion/docs/en.md, phases/08-generative-ai/10-video-generation/docs/en.md

- **Covariance**: $\Sigma = R S S^T R^T$ from the quaternion and the scales.
- **Projection**: $\Sigma' = J W \Sigma W^T J^T$, a 2 × 2 covariance.
- **Composite**: $C = \sum_i \alpha_i T_i c_i$ with $T_i = \prod_{j < i} (1 - \alpha_j)$. NeRF uses the same equation.
- **SH colour**: degree L gives $(L+1)^2$ terms per channel. Degree 3 gives 16 terms.
- **Gaussian size**: about 60 floats. Five million Gaussians use 240 MB.
- **Video tokens**: $(T / P_t) \cdot (H / P_h) \cdot (W / P_w)$
- **Divided attention**: $(HW) \cdot T^2 + T \cdot (HW)^2$ instead of $O((THW)^2)$.
- **Raw video**: 10 s of 1080p at 24 fps is 240 frames, about 1.5 GB.

type: annotated-code
lang: python

```python
model = TinyVideoDiT(in_channels=4, dim=64, depth=2, heads=2)

tokens, grid = self.patch(x)                      # Conv3d, stride equals kernel
xt = x.view(n, T, H * W, d).permute(0, 2, 1, 3).reshape(n * H * W, T, d)
a, _ = self.time_attn(self.ln1(xt), self.ln1(xt), self.ln1(xt), need_weights=False)
xs = xt.view(n, T, H * W, d).reshape(n * T, H * W, d)
a, _ = self.space_attn(self.ln2(xs), self.ln2(xs), self.ln2(xs), need_weights=False)
xs = xs + self.mlp(self.ln3(xs))                  # MLP after time and space
```

markdown:
## Video models
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/12-video-understanding/docs/en.md

- **2D + pool**: CNN per frame, mean over time.
- **3D conv**: (T, H, W) kernels. Models motion.
- **I3D**: inflate 2D kernels along time.
- **(2+1)D**: 2D spatial, then 1D temporal conv.
- **Divided**: attention over time, then space.
- **Uniform**: T frames evenly. 2D+pool default.
- **Dense**: random contiguous window. 3D convs.
- **Clip / video acc**: one clip or mean of clips.

## Pick a 3D, depth or tracking model
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/13-3d-vision-nerf/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/22-3d-gaussian-splatting/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/26-monocular-depth/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/27-multi-object-tracking/docs/en.md

- **NeRF**: an MLP is the scene. Hours to train.
- **3DGS**: explicit Gaussians. Minutes to train.
- **Depth Anything V3**: relative, frozen DINOv2.
- **ZoeDepth**: metric. Sensitive to intrinsics.
- **Marigold**: diffusion depth. 10-50 steps.
- **ByteTrack**: cars and people at 30+ fps.
- **DeepSORT**: heavy occlusion, ReID features.
- **SAM 3.1 Multiplex**: crowds of one class.

## Tracking by detection
type: architecture
from: phases/04-computer-vision/27-multi-object-tracking/docs/en.md

```arch
node | frame | 1,1 | Frame t | video input | client
node | det | 2,1 | Detector | detections at t | model
node | assoc | 3,1 | Hungarian assignment | IoU, cosine, motion
node | upd | 4,1 | Update | matched tracks
node | prev | 1,2 | Tracks up to t-1 | | store
node | kal | 2,2 | Kalman predict | constant velocity
node | born | 3,2 | Birth | new tracks
node | age | 4,2 | Age unmatched | delete after N
edge | frame | det |
edge | det | assoc | detections
edge | prev | kal |
edge | kal | assoc | predicted boxes
edge | assoc | upd | matched
edge | assoc | born | unmatched detections
edge | assoc | age | unmatched tracks
```

## Formulas
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/13-3d-vision-nerf/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/22-3d-gaussian-splatting/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/26-monocular-depth/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/27-multi-object-tracking/docs/en.md

- **PointNet**: $f(P) = \max_{p \in P} \mathrm{MLP}(p)$. Point order does not change it.
- **Positional encoding**: $\sin(2^l \pi p), \cos(2^l \pi p)$ up to $L = 10$ levels.
- **Volume render**: $C = \sum_i T_i (1 - e^{-\sigma_i \delta_i}) c_i$, $T_i = e^{-\sum_{j<i} \sigma_j \delta_j}$
- **3DGS shape**: $\Sigma = R S S^T R^T$. On screen $\Sigma' = J W \Sigma W^T J^T$.
- **3DGS pixel**: $C = \sum_i \alpha_i T_i c_i$, $T_i = \prod_{j<i} (1 - \alpha_j)$
- **Pinhole lift**: $X = (u - c_x) d / f_x$, $Y = (v - c_y) d / f_y$, $Z = d$
- **AbsRel**: mean of $|d_{pred} - d_{gt}| / d_{gt}$. Lower is better.
- **MOTA**: $1 - (FN + FP + \mathrm{IDSW}) / GT$

## Render one NeRF ray
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/13-3d-vision-nerf/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/13-3d-vision-nerf/code/main.py

```python
y = positional_encoding(x, L=10)                   # (5, 3) to (5, 60)
t_vals = torch.linspace(2.0, 6.0, N)               # N = 64 samples on the ray
delta = torch.cat([t_vals[1:] - t_vals[:-1], torch.full_like(t_vals[:1], 1e10)])
alpha = 1.0 - torch.exp(-sigma * delta)            # opacity of each sample
trans = torch.cumprod(torch.cat([torch.ones_like(alpha[..., :1]), 1.0 - alpha + 1e-10], dim=-1), dim=-1)[..., :-1]
weights = alpha * trans                            # transmittance times opacity
rendered = (weights.unsqueeze(-1) * rgb).sum(dim=-2)  # pixel colour
depth = (weights * t_vals).sum(dim=-1)             # depth along the ray
```

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/12-video-understanding/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/13-3d-vision-nerf/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/26-monocular-depth/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/27-multi-object-tracking/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Open door" equals "close door" | Temporal pooling is order-invariant | Use 3D conv or (2+1)D |
| BN breaks after inflation | Weights not scaled | Divide by `time_kernel` |
| NeRF looks blurry | No positional encoding | Add Fourier features |
| Right order, wrong metres | Relative depth model | Metric model plus intrinsics |
| Wrong depth on glass, mirrors | Reflective surfaces | Do not trust those pixels |
| High AbsRel on MiDaS output | Scale and shift not aligned | `align_scale_shift` first |
| ID switches near crowds | IoU-only association | ByteTrack second pass or ReID |
| Track lost in a short occlusion | No motion model | Add a Kalman predict step |

## Questions
type: qa
span: 2
from: phases/04-computer-vision/12-video-understanding/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/22-3d-gaussian-splatting/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/26-monocular-depth/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/27-multi-object-tracking/docs/en.md

- **Why does 3DGS match NeRF quality?** Both use the same compositing equation.
- **Why start with 2D + pool?** It reuses ImageNet weights. It is often within 5-10 points.
- **Which tracking metric?** IDF1 for who is who. HOTA for sports and comparisons.
- **What can one image not give?** Absolute scale without intrinsics, and occluded geometry.
- **Why keep low-confidence boxes?** ByteTrack matches them second. This recovers short occlusions.

type: flow
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/18-long-video-million-token/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/18-long-video-million-token/code/main.py

1. **LLM**: reads the question.
2. **LLM**: calls `find_clips(keyword='<word>')` for relevant clips.
3. **Tool**: returns matching clip timestamps.
4. **VLM**: encodes 3 x 30s clips (~7290 tokens total).
5. **LLM**: composes the answer or asks follow-up queries.

## Token math
type: concepts
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/17-video-language-temporal-grounding/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/18-long-video-million-token/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/18-long-video-million-token/code/main.py

- **Budget**: `tokens(duration_s, fps, per_frame)` is duration times FPS times tokens per frame.
- **Raw**: 1 minute at 30 FPS and 196 tokens per frame is 352k tokens.
- **3x3 pool**: 64 tokens per frame. 5 minutes at 1 FPS is 19,200 tokens.
- **384 native**: ~729 tokens per frame. 3x3 pooling gives 81.
- **30 min**: 1 FPS at 81 tokens is 145,800 tokens. 2 FPS is 291,600.
- **2 hours**: 1 FPS at 81 tokens is 583k tokens.
- **Retrieval**: `3 * 30 * 81 + 200` tokens for 3 clips. 99% cheaper.

## Video model families (vision)
type: concepts
from: phases/04-computer-vision/12-video-understanding/docs/en.md

- **2D + pool**: 2D CNN per frame, average over time. Cannot model motion.
- **3D conv**: kernels over (T, H, W). C3D, I3D, SlowFast.
- **I3D inflation**: copy a 2D kernel along time. 3x3 becomes 3x3x3.
- **(2+1)D**: 2D spatial conv, then 1D temporal conv. Fewer parameters.
- **Joint attention**: one attention over (t, h, w). Quadratic in `T*H*W`.
- **Divided attention**: one attention over time, one over space, per block.
- **Factorised attention**: time and space attention alternate across blocks.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
span: 2
from: phases/04-computer-vision/12-video-understanding/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/17-video-language-temporal-grounding/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/18-long-video-million-token/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/12-video-understanding-pipeline/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "open door" equals "close door" | Temporal pooling is order-invariant | Use 3D conv or a transformer |
| Near-chance on motion classes | Appearance alone is insufficient | Train R(2+1)D, not FramePool |
| Inflated model breaks batch norm | Activation scale grows | Divide by `time_kernel` |
| Joint attention runtime balloons | Quadratic in `T*H*W` | Use divided attention |
| Uniform sampling misses the action | Loses motion peaks | Use dynamic FPS with a max-frame cap |
| Answer says "early in the clip" | No absolute time position | Use time-aligned M-RoPE and JSON output |

## Measure latency correctly
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md

```python
model = model.to(device).eval()
with torch.no_grad():
    for _ in range(warmup):                 # 5 in code, 10 in the docs
        model(x)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()                # before and after, on cuda only
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    model(x)
    times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)  # milliseconds
times.sort()
p50 = times[len(times) // 2]
p95 = times[int(len(times) * 0.95)]         # report percentiles, not the mean
```

## Quantise and export
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md

```python
import torch.ao.quantization as tq
model.qconfig = tq.get_default_qconfig(backend)  # backend="x86"
tq.prepare(model, inplace=True)                  # inserts observers
for x, _ in calibration_loader:
    model(x)                                     # calibrate with real data
tq.convert(model, inplace=True)                  # fuse and quantise
torch.onnx.export(model, sample_input, path,
    input_names=["input"], output_names=["output"],
```

## Measurement discipline
type: flow
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md

1. **Warm up**: run 5-10 dummy forward passes. Ignore them.
2. **Synchronise**: call `torch.cuda.synchronize()` before and after the timed block.
3. **Fix input size**: use the production resolution. 224x224 is not 512x512.
4. **Time**: use `time.perf_counter()` around each pass.
5. **Report**: give p50, p95 and p99. The mean hides the tail.
6. **Decide**: use FLOPs for architecture search. Use on-device latency to ship.

type: defaults
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/16-vision-pipeline-capstone/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/16-vision-pipeline-capstone/code/main.py

## Edge targets and formats
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md

- **Apple ANE**: 38 TOPS, unified memory. INT4 weights + FP16 activations through Core ML.
- **Qualcomm Hexagon**: 45 TOPS. QNN INT8 / INT4 through AI Hub converters.
- **WebGPU / WebLLM**: Q4 MLC (`q4f16_1`) with `mlc_llm convert_weight`. GGUF is not supported.
- **Jetson Orin Nano**: Q4 GGUF or TRT-LLM INT4. Memory-bound.
- **Jetson AGX / Thor**: NVFP4 + FP8 KV on the Edge-LLM path.
- **Vision runtimes**: export PyTorch to ONNX, then pick ONNX Runtime, TensorRT, Core ML or TFLite.

## Bandwidth sets the decode ceiling
type: concepts
from: phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md

- **Ceiling**: $\text{tok/s} = \frac{\text{bandwidth (GB/s)}}{\text{model size (GB)}}$. Decode reads all weights per token.
- **Mobile**: 3.5 GB at 50 GB/s takes 70 ms. The ceiling is ~14 tok/s.
- **Datacenter**: HBM3 at 3 TB/s clears 3.5 GB in 1.2 ms. The ceiling is 830 tok/s.
- **Gap**: datacenter to edge bandwidth is 30-50x.
- **Phone context**: 4 GB model + 2 GB KV cache for 32K tokens on 8 GB RAM = OOM. Keep 4K-8K.
- **Conv FLOPs**: $2 \, c_{in} \, c_{out} \, k_h \, k_w \, h \, w$ for one conv layer.
- **INT8**: model size and memory bandwidth drop 4x. Compute drops 2-4x.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/16-vision-pipeline-capstone/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| First timings are slow | Cold caches and JIT compilation | Warm up 5-10 passes |
| GPU latency looks tiny | You measure kernel dispatch | Synchronise around the timed block |
| Crops come back empty | Boxes in (cx, cy, w, h) | Validate (x1, y1, x2, y2) with Pydantic |
| Crop fails at the edge | Out-of-bounds boxes | Clamp to the image size |
| Corrupt upload gives 500 | No decode check | Return 400 with a named error |
| First request fails | Model loads late | Load at service startup |
| Phone OOM on long context | KV cache for 32K tokens | Keep context at 4K-8K |
| PTQ accuracy loss too high | Static PTQ is not enough | Use QAT with labelled data |

## Abbreviations
type: glossary
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md

- **PTQ**: post-training quantisation. Quantise a trained model without retraining.
- **QAT**: quantisation-aware training. Best accuracy. Needs labelled data.
- **ONNX**: the neutral model format. Every mainstream runtime reads it.
- **FLOPs**: floating-point operations per forward pass. A rough proxy for compute.
- **ANE**: Apple Neural Engine. On-device NPU with unified memory.
- **QNN**: Qualcomm Neural Network SDK. Gives access to Hexagon.
- **Unified memory**: CPU and NPU see the same RAM. No copy overhead.

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/16-vision-pipeline-capstone/docs/en.md, phases/17-infrastructure-and-production/12-edge-inference/docs/en.md

- **Which model for under 3M params?** MobileNetV3-Small. It compiles everywhere.
- **Which model for 10-20M params?** ConvNeXt-Tiny. It is CPU-friendly.
- **Why can more FLOPs run faster?** Depthwise convs compile well. Large 7x7 convs do not.
- **Where does pipeline latency go?** Preprocessing on CPU. The detector takes 70-90% of GPU time.
- **Why is edge decode slow?** Decode is memory-bound. Compute is secondary.

## Tips
type: tips
from: phases/04-computer-vision/15-real-time-edge/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/16-vision-pipeline-capstone/docs/en.md

- Quantise every edge model to INT8 unless you have a specific reason not to.
- Measure every table cell on the target device, not the workstation.
- Log the model name and weights hash in each response.
- Log every stage timing with a per-request trace ID.
- If the classifier times out, return detections without classifications.

title: Vision Transformers and Patch Tokens
subtitle: Patchify, embed, add CLS and position, run pre-LN blocks. Token counts, parameter math and any-resolution packing.
markdown:
## ViT pipeline
type: architecture
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

```arch
node | img | 1,1 | Image | (3, 224, 224) | client
node | patch | 2,1 | Patch embedding | conv 16x16 s=16 | process
node | flat | 3,1 | Flatten | (196, 768) tokens | process
node | cls | 4,1 | Prepend [CLS] | 197 tokens | store
node | pos | 4,2 | Add learned position | (197, 768) | store
node | enc | 3,2 | N encoder blocks | pre-LN | gpu
node | take | 2,2 | Take [CLS] output | | process
node | head | 1,2 | MLP classifier | | model
edge | img | patch |
edge | patch | flat |
edge | flat | cls |
edge | cls | pos |
edge | pos | enc |
edge | enc | take |
edge | take | head |
```

## Shape and cost math
type: concepts
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/01-vision-transformer-patch-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/58-vision-encoder-patches/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/59-vit-transformer/docs/en.md, phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

- **Grid**: $(H/P) \times (W/P)$ patches. 224 at patch 16 gives 14x14 = 196 tokens.
- **Patch vector**: $3P^2$ values. At P = 16 that is 768.
- **Projection**: `nn.Conv2d(3, D, kernel_size=P, stride=P)` equals unfold then linear.
- **Sequence**: patches + 1 CLS + registers. ViT-B/16 at 224 is 197.
- **Attention cost**: $n^2$. 196 tokens give 38,416 scores. 150,528 pixels give 22.6 billion.
- **Head dim**: `head_dim = hidden / num_heads`. 768 / 12 = 64.
- **Block params**: $12 D^2$ + 3k. About 7.1M at D = 768. 12 blocks are 85M.
- **Patch embed params**: `3 * P * P * hidden + hidden`. 590,592 for ViT-Base/16.

## Tiny ViT forward
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/code/main.py, phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md

```python
vit = ViT(image_size=64, patch_size=16, num_classes=10, dim=192, depth=6, num_heads=3)
x = self.patch(x)                                 # (N, 16, 192)
cls = self.cls_token.expand(x.size(0), -1, -1)
x = torch.cat([cls, x], dim=1)                    # (N, 17, 192)
x = x + self.pos_embed                            # learned, trunc_normal std=0.02
for blk in self.blocks:
    x = blk(x)                                    # pre-LN attention, then MLP
return self.head(self.ln(x[:, 0]))                # classify from [CLS] only
```

## Pre-LN block at ViT-B scale
type: annotated-code
lang: python
from: phases/19-capstone-projects/59-vit-transformer/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/59-vit-transformer/docs/en.md

```python
cfg = ViTConfig()                                 # 224, 16, hidden 768, depth 12, heads 12
qkv = self.qkv(x).reshape(b, n, 3, h, hd).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
q, k, v = qkv[0], qkv[1], qkv[2]
scores = (q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)) * self.scale   # scale = 1 / sqrt(head_dim)
attn = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)                  # no mask. Encoder is bidirectional
x = x + self.attn(self.ln1(x), store_attn=store_attn)
x = x + self.ffn(self.ln2(x))                     # hidden to 4 * hidden to hidden
tokens, cls = encoder(img)                        # (1, 197, 768) and (1, 768)
```

## Patch size and token count
type: defaults
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/01-vision-transformer-patch-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/06-any-resolution-patch-n-pack/docs/en.md

| Setting | Default | Note |

| 224, patch 16 | 196 tokens | Standard |
| 224, patch 32 | 49 tokens | Faster, lower resolution |
| 224, patch 8 | 784 tokens | Finer, quadratic cost |
| SigLIP 2 SO400m/14 at 384 | 729 patch tokens | 2026 default VLM tower |
| NaFlex budgets | 256, 729, 1024 | One checkpoint, pick at inference |
| AnyRes 672x672, 2x2 + thumbnail | 2880 | 4 * 576 + 576 |
| OCR and documents | 1024-4096 tokens | Natural photos need 256-576 |

## Patch-n'-pack a mixed batch
type: flow
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/06-any-resolution-patch-n-pack/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/06-any-resolution-patch-n-pack/code/main.py

1. **Grid**: compute each native patch grid at patch size 14.
2. **Flatten**: each image becomes its own variable-length sequence.
3. **Concat**: join all sequences into one. Offsets give `cu_seqlens`.
4. **Mask**: build a block-diagonal mask. Patches attend only inside their image.
5. **Position**: give each patch 2D RoPE or fractional positions.
6. **Result**: 576 + 256 + 768 tokens give one 1600-token sequence. No padding.

## Pooling and position choices
type: concepts
from: phases/12-multimodal-ai/01-vision-transformer-patch-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/09-vision-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/58-vision-encoder-patches/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/06-any-resolution-patch-n-pack/docs/en.md

- **[CLS] token**: its final hidden state is the image. Original ViT and CLIP use it.
- **Mean pool**: average of patch outputs. SigLIP and DINOv2 use it.
- **Register tokens**: 4 to 16 extra tokens absorb high-norm artifacts. Drop them before the LLM.
- **Learned 1D position**: ties the model to the training resolution.
- **2D sinusoidal**: fixed, 0 parameters. Half the dim is row, half is column.
- **2D-RoPE, M-RoPE**: rotate q and k by (row, col). No position table.
- **VLM handoff**: skip pooling. Every patch becomes an LLM input token.

## Troubleshooting
type: troubleshooting
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/01-vision-transformer-patch-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/06-any-resolution-patch-n-pack/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/58-vision-encoder-patches/code/main.py, phases/19-capstone-projects/59-vit-transformer/code/main.py

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| ViT loses to ResNet on ImageNet-1k | No CNN priors, too little data | DeiT recipe or MAE pretraining |
| Deep stack fails to train | Post-LN past 6-8 layers | Use pre-LN |
| New resolution breaks positions | Learned 1D table | Interpolate, or use 2D-RoPE |
| Squished text, lost chart labels | Square resize | Encode at native resolution |
| 50%+ of tokens are padding | Pad to the longest side | Patch-n'-pack with a mask |
| High-norm artifact patches | No sink token | Add register tokens |
| ValueError on the grid | `patch_size` does not divide `image_size` | Pick a dividing patch size |
| `sinusoidal_2d` raises | dim not divisible by 4 | Use a dim that is a multiple of 4 |

## Questions
type: qa
from: phases/04-computer-vision/14-vision-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/07-transformers-deep-dive/09-vision-transformers/docs/en.md, phases/12-multimodal-ai/01-vision-transformer-patch-tokens/docs/en.md, phases/19-capstone-projects/58-vision-encoder-patches/docs/en.md

- **Why patches, not pixels?** A 224x224 image is 150,528 pixel tokens. Attention is quadratic.
- **Why pre-LN?** It trains deep stacks stably without warmup.
- **Patch 14 or 16?** Patch 14 gives more tokens. Better for OCR and dense tasks, slower.
- **Which backbone for dense features?** DINOv2. Use CLIP or SigLIP to match text.
- **Learned or sinusoidal position?** Learned wins at fixed resolution. Sinusoidal wins when resolution changes.

from: projects/chart-storyboard-builder/README.md, projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/README.md, projects/diagram-reading-companion/README.md, projects/service-ownership-navigator/README.md, projects/diagram-reading-companion/solution/cli.ts

## Explain a real Terraform plan
type: annotated-code
lang: bash
from: projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/README.md, projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/solution/cli.py

```bash
terraform show -json saved.plan > input.json  # saved plan as JSON
python3 cli.py input.json --output review  # never applies the plan
# review/change-brief.md        addresses with local anchors
# review/resource-impact.json   graph.edges and resources
# review/review.html            changes, edges, unresolved
```

## Plan explainer pipeline
type: flow
from: projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/API.md, projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/solution/main.py

1. **load_plan**: accepts only format major 1. It keeps actions and masked `before` and `after`.
2. **load_plan**: shows sensitive values as `[sensitive]` and computed values as `[unknown]`.
3. **classify**: maps each exact action sequence to one action name.
4. **impact_graph**: links references and `depends_on` by the longest address prefix.
5. **impact_graph**: skips `var`, `local`, `path`, `count`, `each`, `terraform` and `self`.
6. **explain**: writes Markdown with one anchor per address and the declared dependencies.

type: command-table
from: projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/solution/main.py, projects/infrastructure-plan-explainer/API.md

| `["create"]` | create |
| `["update"]` | update, in place |
| `["delete", "create"]` | replace |
| `["create", "delete"]` | replace |
| `["delete"]` | delete |
| `["read"]`, `["no-op"]`, `["forget"]` | read, no-op, forget |
| any other list | `unsupported action sequence` |

## Diagram companion
type: architecture
from: projects/diagram-reading-companion/solution/main.ts, projects/diagram-reading-companion/solution/cli.ts

```arch
node | an | 3,1 | analyzeGraph() | order, branches, cycles | process
node | rev | 3,2 | reviewGraph() | order, reviewed | process
node | graph | 2,2 | graph.json | reviewed manifest | store

edge | load | an | graph
```
